intent: Compare the wicket-taking effectiveness of bowlers in the first 6 overs versus the remaining overs of the match.
structure: Use CASE statements to define 'First 6 Overs' and 'Remaining Overs'. Group by bowler and these phases. Calculate the average wickets per ball for each bowler in each phase.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN CAST(bowler_wickets AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS wickets_per_ball_first_6,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN CAST(bowler_wickets AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS wickets_per_ball_remaining
FROM df
WHERE
  bowler_bowls_done > 0
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  wickets_per_ball_first_6 IS NOT NULL OR wickets_per_ball_remaining IS NOT NULL;

intent: Examine the consistency of boundary hitting by batsmen across different phases of the innings: Powerplay (first 6 overs) and Middle Overs (overs 7-15).
structure: Use CASE statements to define 'Powerplay' and 'Middle Overs'. Group by batsman and these phases. Calculate the average number of fours and sixes per ball faced in each phase.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN CAST(batsman_fours AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_fours_per_ball_powerplay,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN CAST(batsman_fours AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_fours_per_ball_middle,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN CAST(batsman_sixes AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_sixes_per_ball_powerplay,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN CAST(batsman_sixes AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS avg_sixes_per_ball_middle
FROM df
WHERE
  batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  avg_fours_per_ball_powerplay IS NOT NULL OR avg_fours_per_ball_middle IS NOT NULL OR avg_sixes_per_ball_powerplay IS NOT NULL OR avg_sixes_per_ball_middle IS NOT NULL;

intent: Compare the boundary-hitting frequency (fours and sixes) of batsmen in the middle overs (overs 7-15) versus the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CASE statements to define 'Middle Overs' and 'Death Overs'. Group by batsman and these phases. Calculate the average number of fours and sixes per ball faced in each phase.
sql:
WITH MatchMaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    df.batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15 THEN df.batsman_fours ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_fours_per_ball_middle,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOver) - 5 THEN df.batsman_fours ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOver) - 5 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_fours_per_ball_death,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15 THEN df.batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_sixes_per_ball_middle,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOver) - 5 THEN df.batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOver) - 5 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_sixes_per_ball_death
FROM
    df
GROUP BY
    df.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a batsman faces to hit their first six.
structure: Use a CTE to find the first six delivery for each batsman, then calculate the average of these deliveries.
sql:
WITH batsman_balls_faced_ranked AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_sixes,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS balls_faced_cumulative
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_bowls_faced = 1
)
SELECT
    AVG(T1.first_six_balls_faced * 1.0) AS avg_balls_to_first_six
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MIN(balls_faced_cumulative) AS first_six_balls_faced
    FROM
        batsman_balls_faced_ranked
    WHERE
        batsman_sixes > 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman
) AS T1;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by calculating the average number of runs they score in the first 3 balls they face within each over, comparing this to their average runs in the remaining balls of the same over.
structure: Group by batsman. Calculate average runs scored in the first 3 balls of an over and average runs scored in the remaining balls of an over for each batsman. Use CASE expressions to differentiate between the first 3 balls and the rest.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_num, -- Corrected: use CEIL for over number as per dataset description
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CEIL(overs) ORDER BY overs) AS batsman_ball_in_over_seq
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_bowls_faced = 1 -- Only consider balls actually faced by the batsman for sequencing and counting
),
batsman_stats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_ball_in_over_seq <= 3 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS total_runs_first_3,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_ball_in_over_seq > 3 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS total_runs_rest,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_ball_in_over_seq <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_balls_first_3,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_ball_in_over_seq > 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_balls_rest
    FROM
        numbered_balls
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    total_runs_first_3 * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_balls_first_3, 0) AS avg_runs_first_3_balls, -- Added NULLIF for divide-by-zero protection
    total_runs_rest * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_balls_rest, 0) AS avg_runs_rest_of_over -- Added NULLIF for divide-by-zero protection
FROM
    batsman_stats
WHERE
    (total_balls_first_3 > 0 OR total_balls_rest > 0) -- Filter for batsmen with valid averages in at least one scenario
ORDER BY
    avg_runs_first_3_balls DESC;

intent: Identify bowlers who have a high wicket-taking rate in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall wicket-taking rate.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate overall wicket rate and death over wicket rate for each bowler. Compare these rates. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH BowlerWicketRates AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        CAST(SUM(bowler_wickets) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS overall_wicket_rate,
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_wicket_rate
    FROM df
    GROUP BY bowler
    HAVING SUM(bowler_bowls_done) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    overall_wicket_rate,
    death_overs_wicket_rate
FROM BowlerWicketRates
ORDER BY death_overs_wicket_rate DESC;

intent: Determine the average runs conceded by each bowler in overs where at least one wicket was taken, compared to their average runs conceded in overs where no wickets were taken.
structure: Group by bowler. Use CASE expressions to calculate average runs conceded in wicket-taking overs and non-wicket-taking overs. Grouping by CEIL(overs) to consider over-level events.
sql:
WITH OverSummary AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
        SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded_in_over,
        SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets_in_over
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    AVG(CASE WHEN total_wickets_in_over > 0 THEN total_runs_conceded_in_over END) AS avg_runs_wicket_over,
    AVG(CASE WHEN total_wickets_in_over = 0 THEN total_runs_conceded_in_over END) AS avg_runs_non_wicket_over
FROM
    OverSummary
GROUP BY
    bowler
HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN total_wickets_in_over > 0 THEN CEIL(overs) END) > 0 AND
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN total_wickets_in_over = 0 THEN CEIL(overs) END) > 0
ORDER BY
    avg_runs_wicket_over DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the middle overs (overs 7-15) compared to their strike rate in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Group by batsman. Use CASE statements and CEIL(overs) to define middle and death overs. Calculate strike rate for each phase using conditional aggregation. Filter for batsmen who faced a minimum number of balls in each phase.
sql: SELECT t.batsman, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) = 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0) / CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) END END AS middle_overs_strike_rate, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > max_overs.MAX_OVER_CEIL - 5 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) = 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > max_overs.MAX_OVER_CEIL - 5 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > max_overs.MAX_OVER_CEIL - 5 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0) / CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > max_overs.MAX_OVER_CEIL - 5 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > max_overs.MAX_OVER_CEIL - 5 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) END END AS death_overs_strike_rate FROM df AS t, (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS MAX_OVER_CEIL FROM df) AS max_overs GROUP BY t.batsman HAVING middle_overs_strike_rate IS NOT NULL OR death_overs_strike_rate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC

intent: Find the bowlers who have the highest percentage of their wickets taken in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CTEs to calculate total wickets and death over wickets for each bowler. Compute the percentage. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH WicketAnalysis AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_wickets
    FROM df
    GROUP BY bowler
    HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CAST(death_overs_wickets AS REAL) / total_wickets * 100 AS percentage_wickets_in_death_overs
FROM WicketAnalysis
ORDER BY percentage_wickets_in_death_overs DESC;

structure: Filter deliveries where batsman_fours > 0, find the minimum over for each batsman, and calculate the average of these minimum overs. Use a subquery to find the minimum over per batsman.
sql:
WITH FirstFourDelivery AS (
  SELECT

structure: Use CASE statements to categorize overs into phases (e.g., 1-6, 7-15, 16-20). Group by batsman and phase, and sum the batsman_sixes. Use CEIL(overs) for phase definition.
sql:
SELECT

FROM df

intent: Analyze the trend of runs conceded by a specific bowler over successive overs using a rolling average.
structure: Use a window function to calculate a rolling average of runs conceded by a bowler over a specified number of preceding overs.
sql:
WITH OverRuns AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_num,
        SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_in_over
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs)
),
RollingAverages AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        over_num,
        AVG(runs_in_over) OVER (
            PARTITION BY bowler
            ORDER BY over_num
            ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS rolling_avg_runs_3_overs_per_over_num
    FROM
        OverRuns
)
SELECT
    df.bowler,
    df.overs,
    ra.rolling_avg_runs_3_overs_per_over_num AS rolling_avg_runs_3_overs
FROM
    df
JOIN
    RollingAverages ra
ON
    df.bowler = ra.bowler AND CEIL(df.overs) = ra.over_num
ORDER BY
    df.bowler,
    df.overs;

structure: Group by batsman, calculate strike rate (runs/balls faced) for deliveries within the last 5 overs using a CASE expression. Use a subquery to determine the maximum over number. Filter for batsmen with a minimum number of balls faced in these overs.
sql:
WITH DeathOvers AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY batsman
  HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) >= 10

  CAST(total_runs AS REAL) / total_balls_faced * 100 AS death_overs_strike_rate

intent: Examine the boundary-hitting efficiency of batsmen by calculating the percentage of their total runs that come from fours and sixes. This highlights players who rely heavily on boundaries.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate total runs and total runs from boundaries (fours*4 + sixes*6). Compute the percentage of boundary runs to total runs using a CASE expression to handle division by zero.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_runs) * 100
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_percentage
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY boundary_percentage DESC;

sql:
WITH BatsmanBallsFaced AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as balls_faced_sequence_num
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_bowls_faced = 1
),
FirstScoringBallRank AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MIN(balls_faced_sequence_num) as deliveries_to_first_run
    FROM
        BatsmanBallsFaced
    WHERE
        batsman_runs > 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman
FROM
    FirstScoringBallRank
ORDER BY
    deliveries_to_first_run ASC,
    batsman ASC
LIMIT 1;

intent: Analyze the overall contribution of each batsman to the total team score.
structure: Use CTEs. One CTE calculates total runs by each batsman. Another CTE calculates overall total team runs. Join them and calculate the percentage.
sql:
WITH BatsmanRuns AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_batsman_runs
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman
),
TotalRuns AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(team_runs) AS overall_total_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  br.batsman,
  (CAST(br.total_batsman_runs AS REAL) * 100.0) / NULLIF(tr.overall_total_runs, 0) AS batsman_contribution_percentage
FROM BatsmanRuns AS br

ORDER BY
  batsman_contribution_percentage DESC;

intent: Analyze bowler performance in powerplay and death overs, comparing economy rates.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'powerplay' and 'death overs' based on CEIL(overs). Aggregate runs and balls bowled for each phase per bowler. Calculate economy rates for each phase. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH overphases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) >= 16 THEN 'death_overs'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs_conceded,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_balls_bowled,
  (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6.0) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS powerplay_economy,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_runs_conceded,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_balls_bowled,
  (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6.0) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_overs_economy
FROM overphases
WHERE
  phase IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  powerplay_economy ASC,
  death_overs_economy ASC;

structure: Uses a CTE to identify dot balls, then uses window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to assign sequence numbers within each batsman's innings. Another CTE is used to find consecutive dot balls using a self-join. Finally, counts the longest streak per batsman.
sql:
WITH numbered_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall
    FROM df
    WHERE batsman_bowls_faced = 1
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        rn_overall - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM numbered_deliveries
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(streak_length) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM streaks
    WHERE batsman_runs = 0
    GROUP BY batsman, streak_group_id
) AS batsman_dot_ball_streaks
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY max_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Determine the strike rate of batsmen in the middle overs (overs 6-15) compared to the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CASE statements to define two phases (middle overs and death overs). Group by batsman and calculate the strike rate (total runs / total balls faced) for each phase. This query will use a subquery to determine the total number of overs in an innings.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 5 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_strike_rate AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM over_phases
  WHERE phase = 'Middle Overs' OR phase = 'Death Overs'
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT
  psr.batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS middle_overs_strike_rate,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phase_strike_rate AS psr
GROUP BY psr.batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 1 OR SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 1
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Find the maximum number of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman in the entire match.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Then, use another CTE to create a sequence of these dot balls for each batsman. Finally, calculate the consecutive count of these dot balls by using a self-join on the sequence.
sql:
WITH BallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_seq,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
DotBallGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        ball_seq,
        -- This 'group_id_for_dots' is crucial for identifying consecutive blocks of dot balls.
        -- It's derived by subtracting a sequential number of dot balls (within a batsman's plays)
        -- from the overall sequential number of all balls faced by that batsman.
        -- For consecutive dot balls, this difference will remain constant.
        ball_seq - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS group_id_for_dots
    FROM
        BallSequence
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(consecutive_dot_balls) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls
    FROM
        DotBallGroups
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        group_id_for_dots
) AS ConsecutiveCounts
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

structure: Using CTEs to identify dot balls and then calculating consecutive streaks. Grouping by bowler, aggregation: count of consecutive dot balls.
sql:
WITH dotballsequence AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS rn
  FROM df
),
consecutivedots AS (
  SELECT
    t1.bowler,
    t1.rn
  FROM dotballsequence AS t1
  LEFT JOIN dotballsequence AS t2
    ON t1.bowler = t2.bowler AND t1.rn = t2.rn - 1
  WHERE
    t1.is_dot_ball = 1 AND t2.is_dot_ball = 1
) 
SELECT
  bowler,
  COUNT(*) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM consecutivedots
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  max_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) and compare it to their strike rate in the middle overs (overs 11-15).
structure: Group by batsman. Calculate strike rate for middle overs and death overs using CASE expressions and conditional aggregation. Use subqueries to define overs. Use SUM for runs and balls faced. Calculate ratios. Use column aliases for strike rates. No window functions or CTEs.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS middle_overs_strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman

intent: Analyze the momentum shift by comparing the average runs scored in consecutive overs.
structure: Use a CTE to calculate the total runs scored in each over (using CEIL(overs)). Use a window function (LAG) to get the runs from the previous over. Calculate the difference in runs between consecutive overs. Order by over number.
sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    ceil(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    ceil(overs)
)
SELECT
  over_number,

  LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY over_number) AS previous_over_runs,
  runs_in_over - LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY over_number) AS run_differential
FROM over_runs
ORDER BY
  over_number;

structure: Calculate total overs bowled by each bowler. Identify maiden overs (total runs given by bowler in an over = 0). Group by bowler and calculate the percentage of maiden overs out of total overs bowled.
sql:
WITH OverMaiden AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
),
MaidenCounts AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN runs_in_over = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS maiden_overs,
    COUNT(DISTINCT over_number) AS total_overs
  FROM OverMaiden
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CAST(maiden_overs AS REAL) * 100 / total_overs AS maiden_over_percentage
FROM MaidenCounts
WHERE
  total_overs > 0
ORDER BY
  maiden_over_percentage DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 20% of overs) and compare it to their overall strike rate.

SELECT

  CASE WHEN sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) * 0.8 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) * 0.8 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) * 0.8 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
  sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 OR sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) * 0.8 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0

  batsman;

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in different phases of the innings (early, middle, death overs).
structure: Use CASE to define phases based on CEIL(overs). Calculate strike rate for each phase using SUM aggregation. Group by batsman and phase. Then aggregate by batsman to show phase-specific strike rates.
sql:
WITH overphases AS (
  SELECT batsman,
         batsman_runs,
         batsman_bowls_faced,
         CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early Overs'
              WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 12 THEN 'Middle Overs'
              ELSE 'Death Overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phasestrikerate AS (
  SELECT batsman,
         phase,
         SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
         SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM overphases
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT psr.batsman,
       CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Early Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Early Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Early Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS early_overs_strike_rate,
       CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS middle_overs_strike_rate,
       CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phasestrikerate AS psr
GROUP BY psr.batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Early Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY psr.batsman;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by each bowler in the entire match.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify dot balls, then uses window functions to group consecutive dot balls, and finally calculates the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH dot_ball_flag AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) -
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) as streak_group
  FROM dot_ball_flag
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

WITH over_phases AS (

SELECT

intent: Determine the average number of balls faced by a batsman before hitting their first boundary (four or six).
structure: Use a CTE to flag balls where a boundary was hit and assign a row number for each batsman. Another CTE to select the first boundary for each batsman. Calculate the average balls faced up to that point.
sql:
WITH BatsmanBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_faced_seq_num
    FROM
        df
),
FirstBoundaryBall AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MIN(ball_faced_seq_num) AS balls_to_first_boundary
    FROM
        BatsmanBalls
    WHERE
        batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    CAST(balls_to_first_boundary AS REAL) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM
    FirstBoundaryBall
ORDER BY
    avg_balls_to_first_boundary ASC;

WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT

    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,

  AVG(CASE WHEN over_no <= 6 THEN runs_in_over ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_pp,

FROM over_runs
GROUP BY

ORDER BY
  avg_runs_death DESC, avg_runs_middle DESC, avg_runs_pp DESC;

structure: Use a CTE to filter for death overs and calculate wickets and runs per bowler. Then calculate wickets per over. Group by bowler. Use CASE expression for phase filtering.
sql:
WITH death_overs_bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_in_death_overs,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CEIL(overs)) AS overs_bowled_in_death
  FROM df

    bowler
)

  CASE
    WHEN overs_bowled_in_death > 0 THEN CAST(wickets_in_death_overs AS REAL) / overs_bowled_in_death

FROM death_overs_bowler_stats
WHERE overs_bowled_in_death > 0
ORDER BY
  wickets_per_over_death DESC;

intent: For a specified batsman, find their longest consecutive streak of scoring runs (i.e., not dot balls).
structure: Uses CTEs to first flag non-dot balls. Then uses window functions to group consecutive non-dot balls for the specified batsman. Finally, calculates the maximum streak length for that batsman.
sql:
WITH scoring_ball_flag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_scoring_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE batsman = ' batsman'
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    is_scoring_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_scoring_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM scoring_ball_flag
  WHERE is_scoring_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_scoring_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY batsman, streak_group
) AS subquery;

intent: Identify the longest streak of dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls, another CTE to create streak groups, and then group by batsman to find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BowlerDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
GroupedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- This window function assigns a group identifier for consecutive balls.
        -- It increments the counter whenever a non-dot ball (batsman_runs > 0) is encountered.
        -- Consecutive dot balls will share the same 'group_id' as long as no non-dot ball intervenes.
        SUM(CASE WHEN is_dot_ball = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS group_id
    FROM
        BowlerDeliveries
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(consecutive_dot_balls), 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls
    FROM
        GroupedBalls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Filter to count only dot balls within each group
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        group_id
) AS DotBallCounts
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Find the maximum number of consecutive deliveries a batsman has faced without scoring any runs (dot balls) within each over.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls. Then, use window functions to calculate consecutive dot ball counts within each over for each batsman. Finally, find the maximum consecutive dot ball count per batsman.
sql:
WITH over_balls_with_dot_flag AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_num, -- Corrected: Use CEIL(overs) as per dataset rules
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
dot_balls_numbered AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_num ORDER BY overs) AS rn_in_over,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_num, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_dot_ball_seq
    FROM
        over_balls_with_dot_flag
),
consecutive_dot_ball_groups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        (rn_in_over - rn_dot_ball_seq) AS streak_group
    FROM
        dot_balls_numbered
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        streak_group,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        consecutive_dot_ball_groups
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        over_num,
        streak_group
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over
FROM
    streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of dot balls faced by each batsman in an over.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use another CTE with window functions to group consecutive dot balls within an over. Group by batsman to find the maximum streak length. Use CASE for dot ball identification and row_number for streak grouping.
sql:
WITH BallData AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_num, -- Correctly derive over number using CEIL(overs)
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CEIL(overs) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_in_over -- Row number for all balls within each batsman's over
  FROM df
),
DotBallStreaksGroup AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    over_num,
    -- Calculate a streak_group_id by subtracting two row numbers.
    -- This ID will be constant for consecutive dot balls within each (batsman, over_num) group.
    rn_in_over - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_num ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
  FROM BallData
  WHERE
    is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only consider dot balls for streaks
),
CalculatedStreaks AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    over_num,
    streak_group_id,
    COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length -- Count balls in each streak group
  FROM DotBallStreaksGroup
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_num,
    streak_group_id
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over -- Find the maximum streak length for each batsman
FROM CalculatedStreaks
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over DESC;

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman within a single over.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls, another CTE to create streak groups using window functions (ROW_NUMBER), then group by batsman and streak group to find the length of each streak, and finally find the maximum streak length per batsman.
sql:
WITH dot_ball_flag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    over_number,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_number ORDER BY overs) -
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_number, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM dot_ball_flag
  WHERE
    is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over
FROM (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    over_number,
    streak_group,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over DESC;

intent: Find the batsmen who have the highest strike rate in the death overs (last 10 overs) and also performed well in the initial overs.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate strike rates for different phases of the innings (first 10, next 10, last 10), then filter and order by death overs strike rate, and apply a condition on initial overs strike rate.
sql:
WITH over_blocks AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN 'Middle'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 20 THEN 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
),
strike_rates_by_phase AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    CASE WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate
  FROM over_blocks
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN strike_rate ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_early,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN strike_rate ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_middle,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN strike_rate ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_late
FROM strike_rates_by_phase
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  strike_rate_late > 0 OR strike_rate_early > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_late DESC;

intent: Find the average number of balls a bowler bowls before picking up their first wicket.
structure: Use a CTE to rank deliveries for each bowler and identify the delivery of their first wicket, then calculate the average number of balls bowled before that point.
sql:
WITH bowler_wicket_order AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS delivery_index
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler_wickets > 0
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  AVG(bowler_bowls_done - 1) AS avg_balls_before_first_wicket
FROM bowler_wicket_order
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  AVG(bowler_bowls_done - 1) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
  avg_balls_before_first_wicket ASC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs) of an innings.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate strike rate using conditional aggregation for death overs. Uses CASE expression.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2) > 0
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Calculate strike rate using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced). Use CASE statements with CEIL(overs) to define 'death overs' and 'early overs'. Group by batsman. Use window functions to determine the total number of overs for comparison.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Early Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS early_overs_strike_rate
FROM OverPhases
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman in a single over.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls. Use another CTE with window functions to identify consecutive dot ball streaks within each over. Group by batsman and the streak group to count the length. Requires CTEs and window functions.
sql:
WITH OverAndBallData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number, -- Correctly identify the over number
        overs, -- Used for ordering within an over
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_non_dot_ball -- Identify non-dot balls
    FROM
        df
),
GroupConsecutiveDotBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_number,
        batsman_runs,
        -- This 'dot_ball_group_id' creates a new group whenever a non-dot ball occurs within an over for a batsman.
        -- Consecutive dot balls will share the same group_id until a non-dot ball breaks the sequence.
        -- The sum increments only for non-dot balls, effectively grouping consecutive dot balls together.
        SUM(is_non_dot_ball) OVER (
            PARTITION BY batsman, over_number
            ORDER BY overs
        ) AS dot_ball_group_id
    FROM
        OverAndBallData
),
ConsecutiveDotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls_count
    FROM
        GroupConsecutiveDotBalls
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0 -- Filter to count only dot balls within these identified sequences
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        over_number,
        dot_ball_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(consecutive_dot_balls_count) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over
FROM
    ConsecutiveDotBallCounts
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over DESC;

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive non-boundary scoring balls (singles, doubles, threes, or dots) faced by each batsman.
structure: This query uses CTEs to first flag non-boundary scoring balls and then create streak groups using `ROW_NUMBER()`. It calculates the length of each streak and finds the maximum streak length per batsman.
sql:
WITH non_boundary_flag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 OR batsman_runs = 1 OR batsman_runs = 2 OR batsman_runs = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_non_boundary_scoring_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_non_boundary_scoring_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_non_boundary_scoring_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM non_boundary_flag
  WHERE is_non_boundary_scoring_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_non_boundary_scoring_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_non_boundary_scoring_balls DESC;

sql:
WITH batsman_delivery_rank AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn
  FROM df
),
first_wicket_delivery AS (
  SELECT

    rn AS balls_faced_before_wicket
  FROM batsman_delivery_rank

FROM first_wicket_delivery
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_before_first_wicket ASC;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate variation for batsmen across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Group by batsman and phase (derived from CEIL(overs)). Calculate the average runs per ball within each phase for each batsman. Use CASE expressions for phase definition.
sql:
with phase_analysis as (
  select
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    case
      when ceil(overs) <= 6 then 'Early'
      when ceil(overs) > 6 and ceil(overs) <= 15 then 'Middle'
      else 'Late'
    end as phase
  from df
)
select
  batsman,
  phase,
  case
    when sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 then cast(sum(batsman_runs) as real) / sum(batsman_bowls_faced)
    else 0
  end as avg_runs_per_ball
from phase_analysis
group by
  batsman,
  phase
order by
  batsman,
  case phase when 'Early' then 1 when 'Middle' then 2 when 'Late' then 3 end;

sql:
with last_overs as (
  select
    max(ceil(overs)) as max_over
  from df
)
select
  d.batsman,
  case
    when sum(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 then cast(sum(d.batsman_runs) as real) * 100 / sum(d.batsman_bowls_faced)

from df as d
where

group by

having
  sum(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
order by
  death_overs_strike_rate desc;

intent: Calculate the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman within a single over, to understand their ability to negate pressure or build an innings patiently.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls, then another CTE with window functions to calculate consecutive dot ball streaks within each over. Finally, group by batsman to find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_num,
        overs, -- Keep original overs for ordering within an over
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
NumberedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_num ORDER BY overs) AS rn_in_over,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, over_num, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_in_dot_group
    FROM
        BallData
),
ConsecutiveDotGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        (rn_in_over - rn_in_dot_group) AS consecutive_group_id
    FROM
        NumberedBalls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only consider dot balls for grouping consecutive sequences
),
DotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        over_num,
        consecutive_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls_in_this_group
    FROM
        ConsecutiveDotGroups
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        over_num,
        consecutive_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive non-boundary scoring balls for each batsman.
structure: Identify non-boundary scoring balls using a CASE expression. Use window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to create streak groups and then aggregate to find the maximum streak length per batsman.
sql:
WITH deliveries_with_flag AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE
            WHEN batsman_runs IN (0, 1, 2, 3) THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_non_boundary_scoring_ball_flag
    FROM
        df
),
numbered_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_non_boundary_scoring_ball_flag,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as rn
    FROM
        deliveries_with_flag
),
streaks_grouped AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_non_boundary_scoring_ball_flag,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_non_boundary_scoring_ball_flag ORDER BY overs) as streak_group_id
    FROM
        numbered_deliveries
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id, 
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        streaks_grouped
    WHERE
        is_non_boundary_scoring_ball_flag = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(sl.current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_consecutive_non_boundary_scoring_balls
FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT batsman FROM df) AS d
LEFT JOIN
    streak_lengths sl ON d.batsman = sl.batsman
GROUP BY
    d.batsman

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive non-boundary scoring balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Uses CTEs to flag non-boundary scoring balls and then uses window functions to identify consecutive streaks of these balls. Groups by batsman and streak group to count streak lengths. Uses CASE expressions to identify non-boundary scoring balls.
sql:
WITH BallFlags AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        (CASE WHEN batsman_fours = 0 AND batsman_sixes = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_non_boundary_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as rn
    FROM df
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_non_boundary_ball,
        -- Determine if a new streak of non-boundary balls begins
        CASE
            -- A streak starts if it's the first ball faced by the batsman AND it's a non-boundary
            WHEN is_non_boundary_ball = 1 AND rn = 1 THEN 1
            -- A streak also starts if the current ball is a non-boundary AND the previous ball was a boundary
            WHEN is_non_boundary_ball = 1 AND LAG(is_non_boundary_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS streak_start_flag
    FROM BallFlags
),
GroupedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_non_boundary_ball,
        -- Assign a unique ID to each consecutive streak of non-boundary balls
        SUM(streak_start_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM Streaks
),
ConsecutiveCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(overs) AS current_streak_length
    FROM GroupedStreaks
    WHERE is_non_boundary_ball = 1 -- Only count balls that are part of a non-boundary streak
    GROUP BY batsman, streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_consecutive_non_boundary_scoring_balls
FROM ConsecutiveCounts
GROUP BY batsman;

intent: Determine the maximum number of consecutive dot balls faced by a batsman within a single over.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls, then use window functions to identify consecutive dot ball streaks within each over. Group by batsman and find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH dot_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot
  FROM df
),
consecutive_dots AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CAST(overs AS INT) ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CAST(overs AS INT), is_dot ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM dot_balls
  WHERE is_dot = 1
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(streak_length) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over
FROM (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM consecutive_dots
  GROUP BY batsman, streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING MAX(streak_length) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY max_consecutive_dot_balls_in_over DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive balls faced by a batsman without scoring any runs.
structure: Identify balls where batsman_runs is 0. Use window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to identify consecutive sequences of these balls for each batsman. Calculate the length of each streak and find the maximum streak length per batsman. Order by maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
GroupIdentifiers AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_by_status
    FROM
        BallSequence
),
ConsecutiveDotBallGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        (rn_overall - rn_by_status) AS group_id
    FROM
        GroupIdentifiers
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
),
DotBallCountsPerSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_consecutive_dot_balls_count
    FROM
        ConsecutiveDotBallGroups
    GROUP BY
        batsman, group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_consecutive_dot_balls_count) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    DotBallCountsPerSequence
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per wicket for each bowler in the first 6 overs and in the rest of the innings.
structure: For each bowler, calculate the average runs conceded per wicket in the first 6 overs and in the overs after the 6th. Use CASE expressions based on CEIL(overs) to differentiate phases. Group by bowler and filter for bowlers who have taken wickets in these phases.
sql:
WITH BowlerAggregatedStats AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_first_6_overs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_first_6_overs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_rest_of_innings,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_rest_of_innings
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
        WHEN bas.wickets_first_6_overs > 0 THEN bas.runs_first_6_overs * 1.0 / bas.wickets_first_6_overs
        ELSE NULL
    END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_first_6_overs,
    CASE
        WHEN bas.wickets_rest_of_innings > 0 THEN bas.runs_rest_of_innings * 1.0 / bas.wickets_rest_of_innings
        ELSE NULL
    END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_rest_of_innings
FROM
    BowlerAggregatedStats AS bas
WHERE
    bas.wickets_first_6_overs > 0 OR bas.wickets_rest_of_innings > 0
ORDER BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the longest streak of consecutive balls faced by a batsman without scoring any runs.
structure: Use a CTE to identify balls where the batsman scored zero runs. Then, use another CTE with window functions to group consecutive zero-run balls. Finally, calculate the maximum streak length for each batsman.
sql:
WITH BallEvents AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_scoring_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        is_scoring_ball,
        -- The group_id increments every time a batsman scores runs.
        -- This creates distinct groups of consecutive zero-run balls.
        SUM(is_scoring_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        BallEvents
),
ZeroRunStreaks AS (
    -- Count consecutive zero-run balls within each streak_group_id
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_zero_run_balls
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0 -- Only consider zero-run balls for streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
MaxStreaks AS (
    -- Find the maximum streak of zero-run balls for each batsman
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(consecutive_zero_run_balls) AS max_streak_for_batsman
    FROM
        ZeroRunStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
-- Combine with all batsmen to ensure everyone is included and handle NULLs
SELECT
    DISTINCT T1.batsman,
    COALESCE(T2.max_streak_for_batsman, 0) AS longest_consecutive_zero_run_balls
FROM
    df AS T1
LEFT JOIN
    MaxStreaks AS T2
ON
    T1.batsman = T2.batsman
ORDER BY
    T1.batsman;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive balls a bowler has bowled without conceding any runs.
structure: Use a CTE to identify balls where the bowler conceded zero runs. Then, use another CTE with window functions to group consecutive zero-run balls for each bowler. Finally, calculate the maximum streak length for each bowler.
sql:
WITH BallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE
            WHEN bowler_runs_given > 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_run_ball,
        SUM(CASE WHEN bowler_runs_given > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (
            PARTITION BY bowler
            ORDER BY overs
        ) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        df
),
ZeroRunStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        BallStreaks
    WHERE
        is_run_ball = 0
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    COALESCE(MAX(current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_consecutive_zero_run_balls
FROM
    ZeroRunStreaks
GROUP BY
    bowler
ORDER BY
    bowler;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls faced by a batsman before hitting their first boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use a CTE to identify the first boundary for each batsman. Calculate the delivery number for that boundary. Then, group by batsman and calculate the average of these delivery numbers.
sql:
WITH innings_detection AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary,
    -- Detect the start of a new innings/spell for a batsman
    -- A new innings is assumed if it's the very first ball for the batsman in the dataset
    -- OR if the current 'overs' value is less than or equal to the previous 'overs' value for that batsman,
    -- which indicates an 'overs' reset, typically signifying a new innings.
    CASE
      WHEN LAG(overs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) IS NULL THEN 1
      WHEN overs <= LAG(overs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS is_new_innings
  FROM df
),
innings_numbered AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_boundary,
    -- Assign a unique 'innings_id' for each continuous batting spell of a batsman
    SUM(is_new_innings) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS innings_id
  FROM innings_detection
),
balls_in_innings AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    innings_id,
    overs,
    is_boundary,
    -- Calculate the sequential ball number within each identified innings/spell
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, innings_id ORDER BY overs) AS ball_idx_in_innings
  FROM innings_numbered
),
first_boundary_per_innings AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    innings_id,
    -- Find the ball index (number of balls faced) for the first boundary in each innings/spell
    MIN(ball_idx_in_innings) AS balls_to_first_boundary_in_innings
  FROM balls_in_innings
  WHERE is_boundary = TRUE
  GROUP BY batsman, innings_id
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  -- For each batsman, calculate the average of these 'balls to first boundary' values across all their innings/spells
  AVG(CAST(balls_to_first_boundary_in_innings AS REAL)) AS avg_balls_before_first_boundary
FROM first_boundary_per_innings
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_before_first_boundary ASC;

intent: Calculate the percentage of wickets taken by a bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs) relative to their total wickets.
structure: Use a CTE to define 'death overs' and 'non-death overs'. Group by bowler. Use conditional aggregation within the CASE statement to sum wickets in death overs and total wickets. Calculate the percentage.
sql:
WITH phaseanalysis AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs' ELSE 'Non-Death Overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS percentage_wickets_in_death_overs
FROM phaseanalysis
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
ORDER BY percentage_wickets_in_death_overs DESC;

intent: Identify the strike rate of a specific bowler in death overs versus their overall strike rate.
structure: Use a CTE to define 'death overs' (last 5 overs) and 'overall'. Group by bowler. Use conditional aggregation to calculate strike rate (runs given/wickets) for each phase for a specific bowler. Include a WHERE clause for the specific bowler.
sql:
WITH phaseanalysis AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs' ELSE 'Overall' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Overall' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Overall' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Overall' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phaseanalysis
WHERE bowler = 'Azmatullah'
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate ASC;
description: Calculates and compares the strike rate (runs conceded per wicket taken) of a specific bowler in the death overs versus their overall strike rate throughout the match. This query requires a bowler name to be provided as a placeholder.
original_sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    -- Overall strike rate (runs conceded per wicket taken)
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(bowler_wickets), 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
    -- Death overs strike rate (runs conceded per wicket taken in death overs)
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MaxOver) - 5 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 /
    NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MaxOver) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM
    df
WHERE
    bowler = '{bowler}'
GROUP BY
    bowler
HAVING
    SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0;

intent: Determine the number of deliveries where a batsman scored boundaries (4s or 6s) in the first half of the total overs compared to the second half.
structure: Calculate the total number of overs. Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'First Half' and 'Second Half'. Count deliveries with 4s or 6s within each half. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH over_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS total_overs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  d.batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (o.total_overs / 2.0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_first_half,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (o.total_overs / 2.0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_second_half
FROM df AS d
CROSS JOIN over_ranges AS o
WHERE
  d.batsman_fours > 0 OR d.batsman_sixes > 0
GROUP BY
  d.batsman;

intent: Show the average number of balls a batsman faces before hitting their first boundary in the match.
structure: Use a CTE to rank deliveries for each batsman and identify the first boundary, then calculate the average delivery number for these events.
sql:
WITH BallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        TRUNC(overs) * 6 + (overs - TRUNC(overs)) * 10 AS ball_abs_idx,
        LAG(TRUNC(overs) * 6 + (overs - TRUNC(overs)) * 10, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_ball_abs_idx,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_batsman_career
    FROM df
),
BattingSessionFlags AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        CASE
            WHEN rn_batsman_career = 1 THEN 1
            WHEN ball_abs_idx - prev_ball_abs_idx > 1 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_new_session_start
    FROM BallSequence
),
CalculatedSessions AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        SUM(is_new_session_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS batsman_session_id
    FROM BattingSessionFlags
),
BallsToFirstBoundary AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_session_id,
        -- Calculate cumulative balls faced only for balls where batsman_bowls_faced = 1
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, batsman_session_id ORDER BY overs) AS balls_faced_in_session,
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary
    FROM CalculatedSessions
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_faced_in_session) AS avg_balls_before_first_boundary
FROM BallsToFirstBoundary
WHERE is_boundary
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Analyze the trend of batsman strike rates across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late) to understand how their scoring pace changes.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define three phases based on over number (CEIL(overs)). Group by batsman and phase, calculating the average strike rate (SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)) for each group. Use window functions for ranking over deliveries.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  CASE
    WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM phase_data
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN 1
    WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN 2
    ELSE 3
  END;

intent: Analyze bowler wicket-taking efficiency by calculating the average number of runs conceded per wicket taken in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings.

SELECT

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_rest_of_innings
FROM df
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0
  OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the first 6 overs compared to their strike rate in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to categorize deliveries into 'powerplay' (first 6 overs) and 'death' (last 5 overs) based on CEIL(overs). Then, calculate strike rates (runs/balls) for each phase using conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH phase_analysis AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'death_overs'
      ELSE 'middle_overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_analysis
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: For each bowler, determine the longest streak of consecutive balls without conceding any runs (dot balls).
structure: Use CTEs to first identify dot balls, then create groups based on consecutive dot balls, and finally calculate the maximum length of these groups per bowler.
sql:
WITH zero_run_balls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN bowler_runs_given = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM zero_run_balls
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING MAX(streak_length) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls conceded by each bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Filter for death overs. Use a CTE to identify dot balls and then use window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to find consecutive streaks of dot balls per bowler. Group by bowler and streak to find the max streak length.
sql:
WITH DeathOversBalls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    batsman_runs
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
),
zero_run_balls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM DeathOversBalls
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM zero_run_balls
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
),
bowler_dot_streaks AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
),
max_bowler_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_death_overs
    FROM bowler_dot_streaks
    GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT
  dob.bowler,
  COALESCE(mbs.longest_consecutive_dot_balls_death_overs, 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_death_overs
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT bowler FROM DeathOversBalls) AS dob
LEFT JOIN max_bowler_streaks mbs
  ON dob.bowler = mbs.bowler
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_balls_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the ratio of fours to sixes hit by each batsman, focusing only on deliveries where boundaries were scored.
structure: Filter for deliveries where batsman_fours > 0 or batsman_sixes > 0. Group by batsman. Calculate the ratio of total fours to total sixes.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_fours) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_sixes)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS four_to_six_ratio
FROM df

GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0
ORDER BY
  four_to_six_ratio DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) and compare it with their strike rate in the first 10 overs.
structure: This query uses CTEs to define two phases: first 10 overs and last 5 overs. It then groups by batsman, calculates strike rate (batsman_runs / batsman_bowls_faced * 100) for each phase, and compares them. It uses CASE expressions to bucket overs into phases. Aggregations include SUM and COUNT. Window functions are not used.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10 OR CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_first_10_overs,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_data
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a batsman faces before hitting their first boundary (four or six).
structure: This query uses a CTE with a window function to rank deliveries for each batsman. It filters for deliveries that are boundaries (fours or sixes). It then calculates the average of the delivery number at which the first boundary occurred for each batsman. Aggregations include AVG and ROW_NUMBER. Window functions are used.
sql:
WITH GlobalBallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler, -- Include bowler for a more robust global ordering
        overs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        -- Create a stable global sequence number for all balls to ensure deterministic ordering for LAG/SUM.
        -- This handles cases where 'overs' resets for different team innings.
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY overs, batsman, bowler, team_runs) AS global_ball_seq
    FROM df
),
TeamInningsIdentifier AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        -- Detect the start of a new team innings. 'overs' typically resets (e.g., from 19.6 back to 0.1).
        -- LAG(overs, 1, 999.9) sets the default value for the first row to a high number, ensuring it's marked as a new innings start.
        CASE WHEN LAG(overs, 1, 999.9) OVER (ORDER BY global_ball_seq) >= overs THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new_team_innings_flag
    FROM GlobalBallSequence
),
AssignedTeamInnings AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        -- Assign a unique ID to each distinct team innings.
        SUM(is_new_team_innings_flag) OVER (ORDER BY global_ball_seq) AS team_innings_id
    FROM TeamInningsIdentifier
),
BatsmanBallsInInnings AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        team_innings_id,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        -- Count balls faced by the batsman within each of their identified team innings.
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, team_innings_id ORDER BY global_ball_seq) AS balls_faced_in_current_innings
    FROM AssignedTeamInnings
    WHERE batsman_bowls_faced = 1 -- Only count balls actually faced by the batsman
),
FirstBoundaryBall AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        team_innings_id,
        MIN(balls_faced_in_current_innings) AS balls_to_first_boundary_in_innings
    FROM BatsmanBallsInInnings
    WHERE batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
    GROUP BY batsman, team_innings_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_to_first_boundary_in_innings) AS avg_balls_before_first_boundary
FROM FirstBoundaryBall
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by a bowler in the middle overs (overs 7-15).
structure: This query uses CTEs to identify dot balls within the middle overs and creates streak groups using window functions. It then aggregates to find the length of each streak and determines the maximum streak length per bowler. Aggregations include COUNT. CASE expressions are used to identify dot balls and filter overs. Window functions are used.
sql:
WITH middle_overs_dot_balls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0.0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM middle_overs_dot_balls
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_middle_overs
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING MAX(streak_length) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY longest_consecutive_dot_balls_middle_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the longest streak of consecutive non-boundary scoring balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to flag non-boundary balls, then another CTE to create streak groups. Finally, group by batsman and find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH ball_scoring_status AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE
            WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND batsman_fours = 0 AND batsman_sixes = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_non_scoring_ball
    FROM df
),
numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_non_scoring_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_non_scoring_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_status_group
    FROM ball_scoring_status
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_non_scoring_ball,
        (rn_overall - rn_status_group) AS streak_group
    FROM numbered_balls
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(CASE WHEN is_non_scoring_ball = 1 THEN streak_length ELSE 0 END) AS longest_consecutive_non_boundary_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_non_scoring_ball,
        streak_group,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM streaks
    GROUP BY batsman, is_non_scoring_ball, streak_group
) AS grouped_streaks
GROUP BY batsman;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs of the innings) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to define phases (death overs vs. non-death overs) and then calculate strike rate using conditional aggregation. Group by batsman. Window function not used. CASE expression used for phase.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM phase_data
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0;
