WITH MatchOverInfo AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_number
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  d.batsman,
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (moi.max_over_number - 10) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (moi.max_over_number - 10) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (moi.max_over_number - 10) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (moi.max_over_number - 10) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_other_overs
FROM
  df AS d
CROSS JOIN
  MatchOverInfo AS moi
GROUP BY
  d.batsman
HAVING
  SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  d.batsman;

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by each bowler.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use another CTE with window functions to group consecutive dot balls. Calculate the max streak length per bowler. Requires CTEs and window functions.
sql:
WITH BowlerList AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT bowler
    FROM df
),
RankedDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS rn_total,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_status_group
    FROM
        df
),
GroupedDotStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        (rn_total - rn_status_group) AS streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        RankedDeliveries
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        (rn_total - rn_status_group)
)
SELECT
    bl.bowler,
    COALESCE(MAX(gds.current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    BowlerList bl
LEFT JOIN
    GroupedDotStreaks gds ON bl.bowler = gds.bowler
GROUP BY
    bl.bowler
ORDER BY
    bl.bowler;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in powerplay overs (first 10 overs) versus middle overs (overs 11-15) and death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CASE statements to define three phases: Powerplay, Middle Overs, Death Overs. Calculate strike rate for each phase by grouping by batsman. Requires CASE statements and grouping by CEIL(overs).
sql:
WITH phase_analysis AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_middle_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_analysis
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 10 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate strike rates using CASE expressions for over phases and aggregate by batsman. Uses subqueries and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH MatchMaxOverNum AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num
    FROM df
),
BatsmanPhaseStats AS (
    SELECT
        d.batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOverNum) - 10 THEN 'Death Overs'
            ELSE 'Other Overs'
        END AS phase,
        SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM
        df AS d
    GROUP BY
        d.batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MatchMaxOverNum) - 10 THEN 'Death Overs'
            ELSE 'Other Overs'
        END
)
SELECT
    bps.batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN bps.total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN bps.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS other_overs_strike_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bps.total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bps.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM
    BatsmanPhaseStats AS bps
GROUP BY
    bps.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN bps.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR
    SUM(CASE WHEN bps.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bps.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    bps.batsman;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive balls taken by each bowler in the death overs (last 10 overs).
structure: Uses CTEs to identify wicket-taking balls in death overs, then window functions to group consecutive wickets, and aggregates to find the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH death_overs_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_wicket_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_wicket_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM death_overs_wickets
  WHERE is_wicket_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_wickets_death_overs
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  MAX(streak_length) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_wickets_death_overs DESC;

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per wicket taken by bowlers in different phases of the innings (Powerplay, Middle Overs, Death Overs).
structure: Uses CASE statements to define three phases based on CEIL(overs), aggregates runs conceded and wickets for each phase, and calculates the average runs per wicket.
sql:
WITH phase_bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_given,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    phase
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN CAST(total_runs_given AS REAL) / total_wickets ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_per_wicket_powerplay,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN CAST(total_runs_given AS REAL) / total_wickets ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_per_wicket_middle,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN CAST(total_runs_given AS REAL) / total_wickets ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_per_wicket_death
FROM phase_bowler_stats
WHERE
  total_wickets > 0
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT phase) > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to define two phases: 'death overs' and 'rest of innings'. Calculate total runs and balls faced for each batsman in each phase. Compute strike rate for each phase using conditional aggregation. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM phase_data
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

structure: Use CTEs to define phases (death overs vs. rest of innings). Group by batsman, calculate total runs and total balls faced for each phase. Compute strike rate (runs/balls * 100) for each phase using conditional aggregation. The outer query selects batsman and their strike rates for both phases.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_rest_of_innings,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_rest_of_innings
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN balls_death_overs > 0 THEN CAST(runs_death_overs AS REAL) * 100 / balls_death_overs ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE WHEN balls_rest_of_innings > 0 THEN CAST(runs_rest_of_innings AS REAL) * 100 / balls_rest_of_innings ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM phase_data
WHERE balls_death_overs > 0 OR balls_rest_of_innings > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Calculate the average number of runs conceded by bowlers in overs where they took at least one wicket, comparing first 10 overs vs. the rest.
structure: Use CASE expressions to define two phases: 'first 10 overs' and 'rest of innings'. Filter for overs where wickets were taken. Calculate the average runs given by bowler within each phase using AVG aggregation. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH WicketOversInfo AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_num
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler_wickets > 0
),
BowlerWicketOverStats AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler,
        d.bowler_runs_given,
        d.bowler_bowls_done,
        CEIL(d.overs) AS current_over_num
    FROM
        df d
    INNER JOIN
        WicketOversInfo woi ON d.bowler = woi.bowler AND CEIL(d.overs) = woi.over_num
)
SELECT

intent: Calculate the boundary percentage for batsmen in the first powerplay (first 6 overs) versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to categorize overs into 'powerplay' and 'later overs'. Then, group by batsman and calculate the proportion of runs scored from boundaries in each phase.
sql:
WITH phase_analysis AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay' ELSE 'Later Overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0 
  END AS boundary_percentage_powerplay,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0 
  END AS boundary_percentage_later_overs
FROM phase_analysis
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive balls without a wicket for each bowler.
structure: Use CTEs to identify wicket balls, then use window functions to group consecutive non-wicket balls and find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH AllBowlers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT bowler
    FROM df
),
BowlerDeliveriesGrouped AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        bowler_wickets,
        SUM(CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS wicket_group_id
    FROM
        df
),
NonWicketSequences AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        wicket_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_non_wicket_balls
    FROM
        BowlerDeliveriesGrouped
    WHERE
        bowler_wickets = 0
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        wicket_group_id
),
BowlerMaxSequences AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        COALESCE(MAX(consecutive_non_wicket_balls), 0) AS longest_consecutive_non_wicket_balls
    FROM
        NonWicketSequences
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    ab.bowler,
    COALESCE(bms.longest_consecutive_non_wicket_balls, 0) AS longest_consecutive_non_wicket_balls
FROM
    AllBowlers ab
LEFT JOIN
    BowlerMaxSequences bms ON ab.bowler = bms.bowler;

sql:
WITH phase_bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_powerplay,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_powerplay,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_middle,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_middle,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_death,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_death
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE WHEN wickets_powerplay > 0 THEN CAST(runs_powerplay AS REAL) / wickets_powerplay ELSE NULL END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN wickets_middle > 0 THEN CAST(runs_middle AS REAL) / wickets_middle ELSE NULL END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_middle,
  CASE WHEN wickets_death > 0 THEN CAST(runs_death AS REAL) / wickets_death ELSE NULL END AS avg_runs_per_wicket_death
FROM phase_bowler_stats
WHERE wickets_powerplay > 0 OR wickets_middle > 0 OR wickets_death > 0
ORDER BY bowler;

intent: Analyze the variation in bowling economy rate between the first 6 overs and the remaining overs of the innings for each bowler.

sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN df.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS economy_rate_first_6_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN df.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS economy_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM df
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(df.bowler_bowls_done) > 10 -- Bowler must have bowled at least 10 balls overall

intent: Find the longest streak of dot balls bowled by any bowler against a specific batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Another CTE to group consecutive dot balls using row_number window function. Finally, calculate the max streak length per bowler and batsman. Involves window functions (row_number) and CTEs.
sql:
WITH AllPairs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        bowler,
        batsman
    FROM
        df
),
OrderedDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, batsman ORDER BY overs) as rn
    FROM
        df
),
DotBallGroups AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        batsman,
        rn,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, batsman ORDER BY rn) as block_id
    FROM
        OrderedDeliveries
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
ConsecutiveDotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        batsman,
        block_id,
        COUNT(*) as current_block_length
    FROM
        DotBallGroups
    GROUP BY
        bowler, batsman, block_id
),
MaxConsecutiveDotBalls AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        batsman,
        MAX(current_block_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls_calc
    FROM
        ConsecutiveDotBallCounts
    GROUP BY
        bowler, batsman
)
SELECT
    ap.bowler,
    ap.batsman,
    COALESCE(mcdb.longest_consecutive_dot_balls_calc, 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    AllPairs ap
LEFT JOIN
    MaxConsecutiveDotBalls mcdb
ON
    ap.bowler = mcdb.bowler AND ap.batsman = mcdb.batsman

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls for each bowler.
structure: CTE to flag dot balls, another CTE to group consecutive dot balls using window functions, then find the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH dot_ball_flag AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE bowler = 'Azmatullah'
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM dot_ball_flag
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY
  bowler;
description: This query identifies the longest sequence of consecutive dot balls bowled by a specific bowler. It first flags deliveries that resulted in no runs, then uses window functions to group consecutive dot balls, and finally determines the maximum length of such streaks for each bowler.
original_sql:
WITH BowlerDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY overs) AS seq_num_overall
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler = '{bowler}'
),
DotBallGroups AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        is_dot_ball,
        seq_num_overall - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS group_id
    FROM
        BowlerDeliveries
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    MAX(CASE WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 THEN streak_length ELSE 0 END) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        is_dot_ball,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM
        DotBallGroups
    GROUP BY
        bowler, is_dot_ball, group_id
) AS Streaks
GROUP BY
    bowler;

WITH death_overs_data AS (

  FROM df

intent: Compare the economy rate of bowlers in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings.
structure: CTE to calculate runs given and balls bowled for two phases (first 10 overs and rest), then join and calculate economy rates.
sql:
WITH phase_economy AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs' ELSE 'Rest of Innings' END AS phase,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_given,
    SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS balls_bowled
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler, phase
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(p1.bowler, p2.bowler) AS bowler,
  CASE WHEN p1.balls_bowled > 0 THEN CAST(p1.runs_given AS REAL) * 6 / p1.balls_bowled ELSE 0.0 END AS economy_first_10_overs,
  CASE WHEN p2.balls_bowled > 0 THEN CAST(p2.runs_given AS REAL) * 6 / p2.balls_bowled ELSE 0.0 END AS economy_rest_of_innings
FROM (SELECT bowler, runs_given, balls_bowled FROM phase_economy WHERE phase = 'First 10 Overs') AS p1
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT bowler, runs_given, balls_bowled FROM phase_economy WHERE phase = 'Rest of Innings') AS p2
  ON p1.bowler = p2.bowler
ORDER BY COALESCE(p1.bowler, p2.bowler);

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Uses a CTE to calculate runs and balls faced in death overs and rest of innings. Then calculates strike rate for both phases using division. Groups by batsman. Uses CASE statements for phase definition. Outputs a single row per batsman with two strike rate metrics.
sql:
WITH phase_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_rest_of_innings,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_rest_of_innings
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN balls_death_overs > 0 THEN CAST(runs_death_overs AS REAL) * 100 / balls_death_overs ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE WHEN balls_rest_of_innings > 0 THEN CAST(runs_rest_of_innings AS REAL) * 100 / balls_rest_of_innings ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM phase_strike_rates
WHERE balls_death_overs > 0 OR balls_rest_of_innings > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

WITH middle_overs_boundary AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by each bowler.
structure: Use CTEs to flag dot balls. Then, use window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to identify consecutive streaks of dot balls. Group by bowler and streak group to count streak lengths, then find the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH dot_ball_flag AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM dot_ball_flag
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    streak_group,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY bowler, streak_group
) AS subquery
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING MAX(streak_length) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by each bowler.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls (batsman_runs = 0). Use another CTE with window functions (ROW_NUMBER) to identify consecutive sequences of dot balls. Group by bowler and streak group to find streak lengths. Find the maximum streak length for each bowler.
sql:
WITH BowlerBalls AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS rn
    FROM df
),
GroupedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY rn) AS grp
    FROM BowlerBalls
),
DotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        grp,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM GroupedBalls
    WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY bowler, grp
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM DotBallStreaks
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Calculate the economy rate of bowlers across different phases of the innings: Powerplay (overs 1-6), Middle Overs (7-15), and Death Overs (16-20).
structure: Use a CTE with CASE statements based on CEIL(overs) to categorize deliveries into three phases. Calculate the sum of bowler_runs_given and bowler_bowls_done for each phase per bowler. Compute economy rate (runs/6 balls) for each phase. Requires CTEs and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 16 AND 20 THEN 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS economy_rate_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS economy_rate_middle_overs,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS economy_rate_death_overs
FROM OverPhases
WHERE phase IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY
  bowler;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by each bowler.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls. Use another CTE with window functions to identify consecutive streaks of dot balls. Then, group by bowler and find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallStatus AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakIdentification AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Detect the start of a new dot ball streak
        -- A streak starts if the current ball is a dot ball AND the previous ball was NOT a dot ball (or it's the bowler's first ball)
        CASE
            WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 AND LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_new_streak_start
    FROM
        BallStatus
),
StreakGrouped AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Assign a unique ID to each consecutive streak of dot balls for a bowler
        SUM(is_new_streak_start) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakIdentification
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(overs) AS streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGrouped
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only count balls that are actually dot balls within a streak
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        streak_group_id
) AS BowlerStreakLengths
GROUP BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the batsman's tendency to hit boundaries after facing a dot ball.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls and subsequent boundary balls. Calculate the strike rate for boundary balls that immediately follow a dot ball, grouped by batsman. Utilize window functions to check the previous ball's outcome.
sql:
WITH ball_outcomes AS (
  SELECT
    overs,
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball
  FROM df
),
consecutive_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    is_dot_ball,
    is_boundary_ball,
    LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_was_dot
  FROM ball_outcomes
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_after_dot_to_boundary
FROM consecutive_balls
WHERE
  previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_after_dot_to_boundary DESC;

intent: Analyze the bowling economy rate in the death overs (last 5 overs) for each bowler.
structure: Use a subquery to find the maximum over number. Then, filter for deliveries within the last 5 overs using CEIL(overs). Calculate the economy rate (runs conceded per ball) for each bowler in these overs.
sql:
WITH death_overs AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(bowler_bowls_done) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(bowler_bowls_done)
    ELSE 0
  END AS economy_rate_death_overs
FROM death_overs
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_bowls_done) > 0
ORDER BY economy_rate_death_overs ASC;

sql: WITH phase_strike_rates AS ( SELECT batsman, SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) as runs_first_10, SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) as balls_first_10, SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) > 10 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) as runs_rest, SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) as balls_rest FROM df GROUP BY batsman ) SELECT batsman, CASE WHEN balls_first_10 > 0 THEN CAST(runs_first_10 AS REAL) * 100.0 / balls_first_10 ELSE 0 END as strike_rate_first_10, CASE WHEN balls_rest > 0 THEN CAST(runs_rest AS REAL) * 100.0 / balls_rest ELSE 0 END as strike_rate_rest FROM phase_strike_rates WHERE balls_first_10 > 0 OR balls_rest > 0 ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Calculate the proportion of runs scored by each batsman that came from boundaries (fours and sixes) against a specific bowler.
structure: Filter the data for a specific bowler. Group by batsman and calculate the sum of fours and sixes, and the sum of total batsman runs. Compute the ratio of boundary runs to total runs.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_runs) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_runs)
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_percentage
FROM df
WHERE bowler = 'M Nabi' -- Placeholder for bowler
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
ORDER BY boundary_percentage DESC;

intent: Analyze the economy rate of bowlers across different phases of an innings (powerplay, middle, death).
structure: Use a CTE to categorize overs into phases. Group by bowler and phase. Calculate economy rate using SUM(bowler_runs_given) / SUM(bowler_bowls_done). Use CASE expressions for phase definition and conditional aggregation for calculations within each phase. Ensure minimum balls bowled in each phase.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS economy_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS economy_rate_middle_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS economy_rate_death_overs
FROM OverPhases
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler;

It categorizes each delivery into a phase using a CTE and then calculates the economy rate (runs conceded per over) for each phase using conditional aggregation. Bowlers are included only if they have bowled at least one ball in any of these phases, and the results are ordered alphabetically by bowler.

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Group by batsman. Calculate overall strike rate using AVG(batsman_runs) / AVG(batsman_bowls_faced) * 100. Calculate death overs strike rate using conditional aggregation on batsman_runs and batsman_bowls_faced within the last 5 overs. Use CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN ... END for death overs.
sql:
WITH over_boundaries AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'death_overs' ELSE 'normal_overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'normal_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'normal_overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'normal_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM over_boundaries
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'normal_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Calculate the percentage of deliveries that resulted in a boundary (4s or 6s) for each batsman in the first 6 overs vs. overs 7-15 vs. overs 16-20.
structure: Use a CTE with a CASE expression to define three phases: 'first_6', 'middle_7_15', 'death_16_20'. Group by batsman and phase. Calculate the ratio of (batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) to batsman_bowls_faced for each phase.
sql:
WITH phase_analysis AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'first_6'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN 'middle_7_15'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 16 AND 20 THEN 'death_16_20'
      ELSE 'other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'first_6' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'first_6' THEN (batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'first_6' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS boundary_percentage_first_6,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'middle_7_15' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'middle_7_15' THEN (batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'middle_7_15' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS boundary_percentage_middle_7_15,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_16_20' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_16_20' THEN (batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_16_20' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS boundary_percentage_death_16_20
FROM phase_analysis
WHERE phase != 'other'
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'first_6' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'middle_7_15' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_16_20' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Determine the average runs conceded per over by each bowler, considering only overs where they bowled at least 3 balls.
structure: Use a CTE to calculate runs and balls bowled per over for each bowler. Filter this CTE to include only overs where at least 3 balls were bowled. Then, group by bowler and calculate the average runs per over.
sql:
WITH BowlerOverStats AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
        SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_in_over,
        COUNT(*) AS deliveries_in_over
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs)
),
QualifiedOversSummary AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(runs_in_over) AS total_runs_qualified_overs,
        COUNT(over_number) AS total_qualified_overs
    FROM
        BowlerOverStats
    WHERE
        deliveries_in_over >= 3
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CAST(total_runs_qualified_overs AS REAL) / NULLIF(total_qualified_overs, 0) AS avg_runs_per_over
FROM
    QualifiedOversSummary
WHERE
    total_qualified_overs >= 1
ORDER BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the trend of wickets taken by bowlers over successive overs, specifically looking at bowlers who start strong but fade.
structure: Group by bowler and CEIL(overs). Sum bowler_wickets. Use window functions to compare wicket counts in earlier overs vs. later overs. Uses CTE, CASE, and window functions.
sql:
WITH OverWickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  over_number,
  wickets_in_over,
  LAG(wickets_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY over_number) AS wickets_previous_over,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY over_number) as over_rank
FROM OverWickets
WHERE
  wickets_in_over > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  over_number;

intent: Examine the correlation between the number of dot balls a batsman faces and their subsequent performance (strike rate) in the same match.
structure: Use a window function to count dot balls faced by a batsman. Then, calculate the strike rate for a window of subsequent balls. Involves CTE and window functions.
sql:
WITH numbered_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY overs, team_runs, bowler, batsman) AS delivery_id,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball_current
    FROM df
),
deliveries_with_prev_status AS (
    SELECT
        delivery_id,
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        is_dot_ball_current,
        LAG(is_dot_ball_current, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY delivery_id) AS is_dot_ball_prev
    FROM numbered_deliveries
),
target_deliveries_for_stats AS (
    SELECT
        delivery_id,
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced
    FROM deliveries_with_prev_status
    WHERE is_dot_ball_prev = 1
),
eligible_batsmen_identification AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT T.batsman
    FROM target_deliveries_for_stats T
    JOIN numbered_deliveries N
        ON N.delivery_id BETWEEN T.delivery_id AND T.delivery_id + 11
    WHERE N.is_dot_ball_current = 1
)
SELECT
    td.batsman,
    AVG(td.batsman_runs) AS avg_runs_after_dot_ball,
    AVG(CAST(td.batsman_bowls_faced AS REAL)) AS avg_balls_after_dot_ball
FROM target_deliveries_for_stats td
WHERE td.batsman IN (SELECT batsman FROM eligible_batsmen_identification)
GROUP BY td.batsman
ORDER BY td.batsman;

intent: Calculate the average runs scored per over for each bowler throughout the match.
structure: Group by bowler and the over number (using CEIL(overs)). Calculate the sum of team runs for each over and then average these over values per bowler.
sql: SELECT bowler, CAST(SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT CEIL(overs)) AS avg_runs_per_over FROM df GROUP BY bowler ORDER BY avg_runs_per_over DESC
description: This query computes the average number of runs conceded by each bowler in each over they bowl. It helps in understanding a bowler's consistency in restricting runs across different overs.
question: For each bowler, calculate the average runs conceded per over, considering each over as a whole number derived from CEIL(overs). Present the results ordered by the average runs per over in descending order.
paraphrases: What is the average number of runs conceded by each bowler in every over they bowl, sorted by this average?

intent: Find the total number of dot balls faced by each batsman in the first 10 overs.
structure: Filter for deliveries within the first 10 overs (CEIL(overs) <= 10). Group by batsman and count the deliveries where batsman_runs is 0.
sql: SELECT batsman, COUNT(*) AS dot_balls_faced_in_first_10_overs FROM df WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10 AND batsman_runs = 0 GROUP BY batsman ORDER BY dot_balls_faced_in_first_10_overs DESC;

intent: Determine the batsmen with the highest strike rate in overs where they hit at least one boundary.
structure: Use a CASE expression to identify overs where a batsman hit at least one four or six. Group by batsman and calculate their strike rate only for these overs. Filter out batsmen with no boundaries.
sql: SELECT batsman, CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS strike_rate_with_boundary FROM df WHERE batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 GROUP BY batsman HAVING SUM(batsman_fours) + SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0 ORDER BY strike_rate_with_boundary DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of wickets taken by each bowler per over.
structure: Group by bowler, calculate the total number of wickets taken, and the total number of overs bowled (using CEIL(overs)). Then compute the ratio.
sql: SELECT bowler, CAST(SUM(bowler_wickets) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT CEIL(overs)) AS wickets_per_over FROM df GROUP BY bowler HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CEIL(overs)) > 0 ORDER BY wickets_per_over DESC;
description: This query calculates the average number of wickets taken by each bowler per over bowled. It aggregates wickets and counts distinct overs for each bowler, then divides the total wickets by the total overs to provide a 'wickets per over' metric. intent: Calculate the proportion of runs scored by a batsman that came from boundaries (4s and 6s).
structure: Group by batsman, calculate the sum of runs from boundaries and the total runs scored. Compute the ratio.
sql: SELECT batsman, CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_runs) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs IN (4, 6) THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_runs) ELSE 0 END AS boundary_run_proportion FROM df GROUP BY batsman HAVING SUM(batsman_runs) > 0 ORDER BY boundary_run_proportion DESC;

intent: Examine the wicket-taking ability of bowlers in crucial phases of the game: the first 6 overs (powerplay), middle overs (7-15), and death overs (last 5).
structure: Use CASE to define three phases based on CEIL(overs). Group by bowler and phase. Count wickets in each phase.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_powerplay,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_middle_overs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_death_overs
FROM df
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY wickets_death_overs DESC;
description: Aggregates the number of wickets taken by each bowler across three distinct phases: powerplay (first 6 overs), middle overs (7-15), and death overs (last 5 overs), ordered by death over wickets.

How many wickets did each bowler take during the powerplay, middle overs, and death overs? Present the results ordered by the number of wickets in the death overs (descending).

intent: Track the cumulative number of dot balls faced by a batsman over the course of their innings, ordered by delivery index. This helps visualize their ability to absorb pressure or break a period of dot balls.
structure: Use a window function to calculate cumulative sum of dot balls, partitioned by batsman and ordered by overs.
sql:
WITH DotBallFlag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  overs,
  SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_dot_balls
FROM DotBallFlag
ORDER BY batsman, overs;
description: Calculates the cumulative count of dot balls faced by each batsman throughout their innings, ordered by delivery index to show the progression of dot balls faced.
question: For each batsman, calculate the cumulative count of dot balls faced throughout their innings, ordered by delivery. The results should show the batsman, the delivery over, and the running total of dot balls.

Calculate a running total of dot balls for each batsman, ordered by each delivery. Show the batsman, the over, and the cumulative dot ball count.
For every batsman, provide a cumulative count of dot balls faced delivery by delivery. The output should include the batsman, the over, and the total dot balls up to that point.

intent: Identify batsmen who score the highest proportion of their runs through boundaries (fours and sixes) in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Filter for death overs using CEIL(overs), then group by batsman and calculate the ratio of boundary runs to total runs scored.
sql:
WITH death_overs_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) - 5 FROM df)
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_runs) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_runs)
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_run_percentage_death_overs
FROM death_overs_data
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundary_run_percentage_death_overs DESC;
description: This query focuses on the death overs (last 5 overs) to find batsmen who score a high percentage of their runs through boundaries. It calculates the sum of runs from fours and sixes and divides it by the total runs scored by the batsman in those overs, expressed as a percentage. This highlights batsmen who are aggressive finishers.
question: For each batsman, calculate the percentage of their total runs scored in the last 5 overs that came from boundaries (fours and sixes). This is calculated as (sum of (batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6)) * 100.0 / sum of batsman_runs, considering only batsmen who have scored more than 0 runs in these death overs. Order the results by this boundary run percentage in descending order.
paraphrases: What is the boundary run percentage for each batsman in the death overs (last 5 overs)? Calculate this as (total boundary runs / total runs) * 100, for batsmen with total runs > 0 in these overs. Display the results from highest to lowest percentage.

Determine the percentage of runs scored through boundaries by each batsman in the final 5 overs of the innings. The calculation is (sum of fours*4 + sum of sixes*6) * 100 / sum of runs, for batsmen who scored runs in this period. Rank batsmen by this percentage, highest first.

For batsmen who scored runs in the last 5 overs, what proportion of their runs came from boundaries (4s and 6s)? Present this as a percentage, calculated as (boundary runs / total runs) * 100, and order batsmen by this metric in descending order.

intent: Find batsmen who have the highest ratio of fours to sixes hit.
structure: Group by batsman, sum fours and sixes, then calculate the ratio of fours to sixes.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_fours) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_sixes)
    ELSE CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_fours) > 0 THEN NULL ELSE 0 END
  END AS fours_to_sixes_ratio
FROM df
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_fours) > 0 OR SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0
ORDER BY
  fours_to_sixes_ratio DESC;
description: This query identifies batsmen who hit more fours than sixes relative to their boundary count. It calculates the ratio of the total number of fours to the total number of sixes hit by each batsman, helping to distinguish between power hitters and boundary finders.

Calculate the fours to sixes ratio for every batsman who has hit boundaries. The ratio is sum(fours) / sum(sixes), with special handling for batsmen hitting only fours or only sixes. Display results sorted by ratio, descending.

For each batsman with at least one four or six, determine their ratio of fours hit to sixes hit. If only fours were hit, the ratio is considered. If only sixes were hit, the ratio is NULL. If neither were hit, the ratio is 0. Sort batsmen by this ratio, from largest to smallest.

intent: Calculate the average runs scored per legitimate ball by batsmen in the first 6 overs.

sql:
SELECT

intent: Analyze the batting strike rate trend by over phase to understand how batsmen adapt their scoring rate throughout an innings.
structure: Group by batsman and a derived 'phase' column (early, middle, late overs) using CASE WHEN CEIL(overs). Aggregate sum of batsman runs and sum of batsman balls faced. Calculate strike rate as a ratio. Order by batsman and phase.
sql: SELECT batsman, CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early' WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle' ELSE 'Late' END AS phase, CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS strike_rate FROM df WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0 GROUP BY batsman, phase ORDER BY batsman, CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN 3 END;

intent: Analyze the boundary hitting frequency (fours and sixes) after a dot ball for each batsman to understand momentum shifts.
structure: Use a CTE with window functions to identify dot balls and the subsequent ball's outcome. Count boundaries following dot balls per batsman. Order by the count.
sql: WITH BallOutcomes AS ( SELECT batsman, overs, CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball, CASE WHEN batsman_runs IN (4, 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball FROM df ), LaggedOutcomes AS ( SELECT batsman, overs, is_dot_ball, is_boundary_ball, LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_was_dot FROM BallOutcomes ) SELECT batsman, SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_after_dot_ball FROM LaggedOutcomes WHERE previous_ball_was_dot = 1 GROUP BY batsman HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN previous_ball_was_dot = 1 AND is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY boundaries_after_dot_ball DESC;

WITH MaxOver AS (

    FROM df
),
RunsPerDeathOver AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler,
        CEIL(d.overs) AS over_number,
        SUM(d.bowler_runs_given) AS runs_conceded_in_over
    FROM
        df d,
        MaxOver mo

    AVG(r.runs_conceded_in_over) AS avg_runs_conceded_per_death_over

    RunsPerDeathOver r

    r.bowler

intent: Analyze the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman against a specific bowler.
structure: Use CTEs and window functions (LAG and ROW_NUMBER) to identify and measure consecutive dot balls. Filter by a specific bowler using a placeholder variable. Group by batsman to find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallOutcomes AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler = 'Azmatullah'
),
StreakCalculation AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS current_streak_sum
  FROM BallOutcomes
  WHERE
    is_dot_ball = 1
),
StreakGroup AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS row_num
  FROM StreakCalculation
),
StreakDiff AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    row_num,
    LEAD(row_num, 1, row_num + 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_row_num
  FROM StreakGroup
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(next_row_num - row_num) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM StreakDiff
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  MAX(next_row_num - row_num) > 0
ORDER BY
  longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;
description: This query identifies the longest sequence of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman when playing against a specified bowler. It uses window functions to track streaks and helps understand batsman-bowler matchups in terms of pressure and control. The results are ordered by the longest streak in descending order.
original_sql:
WITH BowlerFilter AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler = '{bowler}'
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as non_dot_ball_group_id
    FROM
        BowlerFilter
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        non_dot_ball_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        non_dot_ball_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    Streaks
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    MAX(current_streak_length) > 0
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Analyze the boundary hitting consistency of batsmen by comparing their four/six hitting percentage in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: first 10 overs and later overs. For each batsman, calculate the percentage of fours and sixes out of total balls faced in each phase. Group by batsman and apply conditional aggregation. Include only batsmen who faced balls in both phases.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_fours ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS percentage_fours_first_10_overs,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS percentage_sixes_first_10_overs,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_fours ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS percentage_fours_later_overs,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS percentage_sixes_later_overs
FROM df
WHERE
  batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR sum(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Find the maximum longest streak of dot balls for each batsman.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls and then calculate the difference between consecutive row numbers within groups of dot balls. Use window functions extensively: ROW_NUMBER() for numbering dot balls and LEAD() for calculating the difference. Group by batsman and find the maximum difference.
sql:
WITH BallDetails AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn
    FROM
        df
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        BallDetails
),
DotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    DotBallStreaks
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

structure: Define 'death overs' using a CASE statement based on `CEIL(overs)` relative to the maximum over number. Group by bowler and this 'death over' phase, calculating wickets per ball.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'death_overs' ELSE 'other_overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_death_overs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS balls_in_death_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'death_overs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS wickets_per_ball_death_overs
FROM over_phases
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  balls_in_death_overs > 0
ORDER BY
  wickets_per_ball_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the change in batsman's strike rate from the initial phase of their innings to the later phase.
structure: Use a CASE statement to define 'early' (first 6 overs) and 'late' (after 6 overs) phases. Calculate the strike rate (runs/balls) for each batsman in each phase. Use a self-join or conditional aggregation to compare these two strike rates for each batsman.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'early_phase' ELSE 'late_phase' END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  s1.batsman,
  CASE WHEN s1.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(s1.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s1.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS early_phase_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN s2.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(s2.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s2.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS late_phase_strike_rate
FROM phase_stats AS s1
LEFT JOIN phase_stats AS s2 ON s1.batsman = s2.batsman AND s2.phase = 'late_phase'
WHERE s1.phase = 'early_phase'
ORDER BY
  (late_phase_strike_rate - early_phase_strike_rate) DESC;

intent: Investigate the longest streak of consecutive scoring shots (more than 0 runs) by a batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to flag non-dot balls. Then, use window functions (specifically `ROW_NUMBER` and `LEAD`) to identify consecutive sequences of these non-dot balls for each batsman. Calculate the length of these streaks and find the maximum.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_scoring_shot,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall
    FROM df
),
scoring_cumulative AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_scoring_shot,
        rn_overall,
        SUM(CASE WHEN is_scoring_shot = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_scoring_cumulative
    FROM numbered_balls
),
grouped_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_scoring_shot,
        rn_overall - rn_scoring_cumulative AS streak_group
    FROM scoring_cumulative
),
individual_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM grouped_streaks
    WHERE is_scoring_shot = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(streak_length), 0) AS longest_scoring_streak
FROM individual_streaks
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Analyze the longest streak of dot balls faced by each batsman. This identifies batsmen who struggle to rotate strike or find the boundary under pressure.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls, calculate cumulative streaks of dot balls, group these streaks, and then find the maximum length of consecutive dot balls for each batsman.
sql:
WITH AllBatsmen AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT batsman
    FROM df
),
OrderedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn
    FROM
        df
),
StreakedDotBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        rn,
        batsman_runs,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        OrderedBalls
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
DotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS dot_ball_count
    FROM
        StreakedDotBalls
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
MaxDotStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(dot_ball_count) AS max_streak
    FROM
        DotBallCounts
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    ab.batsman,
    COALESCE(mds.max_streak, 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    AllBatsmen ab
LEFT JOIN
    MaxDotStreaks mds ON ab.batsman = mds.batsman;

intent: Determine the longest streak of dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls and then calculate streaks using window functions (ROW_NUMBER and LEAD). Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH AllBallsRanked AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_all
    FROM
        df
),
DotBallsRanked AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_dots_only
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
GroupedDots AS (
    SELECT
        a.batsman,
        a.overs,
        a.rn_all - d.rn_dots_only AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        AllBallsRanked a
    INNER JOIN
        DotBallsRanked d ON a.batsman = d.batsman AND a.overs = d.overs
),
CalculatedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM
        GroupedDots
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(streak_length), 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    CalculatedStreaks
GROUP BY
    batsman

structure: Use CTEs to identify death overs and filter wickets. Group by bowler. Calculate the percentage.
sql:
WITH OverWickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_death_over_wicket
  FROM df
),
WicketCounts AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
    SUM(is_death_over_wicket * bowler_wickets) AS death_over_wickets
  FROM OverWickets
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  total_wickets,
  death_over_wickets,
  CASE
    WHEN total_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(death_over_wickets AS REAL) * 100 / total_wickets
    ELSE 0
  END AS percentage_of_death_wickets
FROM WicketCounts
ORDER BY
  percentage_of_death_wickets DESC,
  total_wickets DESC;

    is_dot_ball,
    SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS current_streak_sum
  FROM dotballs
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
),
streakgroup AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS row_num
  FROM streakcalculation
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
),
streakdiff AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    row_num,
    LEAD(row_num, 1, row_num + 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_row_num
  FROM streakgroup
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(next_row_num - row_num) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM streakdiff
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING MAX(next_row_num - row_num) > 0
ORDER BY longest_dot_ball_streak DESC
LIMIT 10;

intent: Identify the longest streak of dot balls faced by a batsman. This measures a batsman's ability to rotate strike or get out of a difficult period.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls, calculate a running sum of consecutive dot balls, and then group these streaks to find the maximum length. Window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LEAD) will be essential.
sql:
WITH BallData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
RankedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY overs) AS rn_for_type
    FROM
        BallData
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        -- The streak_group identifies consecutive sequences of dot balls using the 'gaps and islands' technique.
        -- For consecutive rows where is_dot_ball is 1, (rn - rn_for_type) will be constant.
        rn - rn_for_type AS streak_group
    FROM
        RankedBalls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- We are only interested in streaks of dot balls
),
StreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        Streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    StreakLengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Find the longest streak of dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use CTEs and window functions. First, identify dot balls. Then, use a window function to create groups for consecutive dot balls. Calculate the length of each streak and find the maximum streak length per batsman. Order by the longest streak.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn1,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS rn2
    FROM
        df
),
dot_ball_groups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        (rn1 - rn2) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        numbered_balls
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        dot_ball_groups
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls for each batsman.
structure: Using CTEs and window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LEAD) to identify and calculate differences in row numbers for consecutive dot balls, then grouping to find the maximum difference representing the longest streak. Aggregation by batsman.
sql:
WITH batsman_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS delivery_seq_num
    FROM
        df
),
dot_balls_with_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        delivery_seq_num,
        -- The difference between the overall delivery sequence number and the sequence number
        -- for only dot balls (within each batsman's deliveries) creates a unique group ID
        -- for consecutive dot balls.
        delivery_seq_num - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY delivery_seq_num) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        batsman_deliveries
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        dot_balls_with_streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    batsman;

intent: Find the average number of balls faced by a batsman before their first boundary (four or six).
structure: Using CTEs and window functions (ROW_NUMBER, SUM) to track cumulative balls faced and identify the first boundary event, then averaging the cumulative balls at that point. Grouping by batsman.
sql:
WITH batsman_cumulative_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS cumulative_balls_faced,
    (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MIN(cumulative_balls_faced) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM batsman_cumulative_stats
WHERE is_boundary = TRUE
GROUP BY
  batsman

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the first 6 overs (powerplay) versus the rest of the innings. This helps understand how batsmen approach different phases of the game.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate average runs per ball faced (strike rate) using a CASE expression to differentiate between powerplay and later overs. Uses CTEs and CASE expressions.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay' ELSE 'Later Overs' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Later Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_later_overs
FROM over_phases
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use CTEs. Create a flag for dot balls. Use window functions (ROW_NUMBER and LEAD) to identify streak start and end points. Calculate the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallStatus AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        (batsman_runs = 0) AS is_dot_ball,
        LAG((batsman_runs = 0), 1, FALSE) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakStarts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        CASE
            WHEN is_dot_ball AND NOT prev_is_dot_ball THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS streak_start_marker
    FROM
        BallStatus
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(streak_start_marker) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakStarts
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball
),
StreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        Streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    StreakLengths
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Compare the average runs scored per ball in the powerplay (first 6 overs) versus the middle overs (overs 7-15) for each batsman.
structure: Use CASE statements to define powerplay and middle overs, group by batsman, and calculate average runs per ball for each phase.
sql:
WITH PowerplayStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS pp_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS pp_balls
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) <= 6
    GROUP BY
        batsman
),
MiddleOversStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS mo_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS mo_balls
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(ps.batsman, mos.batsman) AS batsman,
    CASE WHEN ps.pp_balls > 0 THEN CAST(ps.pp_runs AS REAL) / ps.pp_balls ELSE NULL END AS avg_runs_powerplay,
    CASE WHEN mos.mo_balls > 0 THEN CAST(mos.mo_runs AS REAL) / mos.mo_balls ELSE NULL END AS avg_runs_middle_overs
FROM
    PowerplayStats ps
FULL OUTER JOIN
    MiddleOversStats mos ON ps.batsman = mos.batsman
WHERE
    (ps.pp_balls IS NOT NULL AND ps.pp_balls > 0) OR (mos.mo_balls IS NOT NULL AND mos.mo_balls > 0)
ORDER BY
    batsman;

intent: Identify the bowlers who are most effective at taking wickets in the powerplay overs.
structure: Group by bowler and calculate the sum of wickets taken in the first 6 overs. Uses a CASE expression to define the powerplay phase. Orders by wickets in descending order.

sql: SELECT df.bowler, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= 6 THEN (df.bowler_runs_given - df.batsman_runs) ELSE 0 END) AS extras_powerplay, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15 THEN (df.bowler_runs_given - df.batsman_runs) ELSE 0 END) AS extras_middle_overs, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN (df.bowler_runs_given - df.batsman_runs) ELSE 0 END) AS extras_death_overs FROM df GROUP BY df.bowler HAVING extras_powerplay > 0 OR extras_middle_overs > 0 OR extras_death_overs > 0 ORDER BY df.bowler;

intent: Analyze the distribution of batsman runs scored across different overs.
structure: Group by batsman and over number (derived from CEIL(overs)), sum batsman runs. Then, calculate the average runs per over for each batsman. Uses CTE and CASE expression for over grouping.
sql:
WITH OverRuns AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(runs_in_over) AS avg_runs_per_over
FROM OverRuns
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_per_over DESC;

intent: Calculate the percentage of dot balls faced by each batsman in the first 6 overs.
structure: Filter for the first 6 overs (CEIL(overs) <= 6). Calculate the count of dot balls (batsman_runs = 0) and total balls faced by each batsman. Compute percentage. Uses CASE expression for dot ball identification and filter.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS dot_ball_percentage_opening
FROM df
WHERE
  CEIL(overs) <= 6
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  dot_ball_percentage_opening DESC;

intent: Compare the number of boundaries hit by a batsman in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize overs into 'first 10' and 'rest'. Group by batsman and the new phase. Sum boundaries for each phase. Wide output preference for binary comparison (first 10 vs rest).
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_first_10_overs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_after_10_overs
FROM df
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) > 0
  OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundaries_first_10_overs DESC, boundaries_after_10_overs DESC;

intent: Identify the longest streak of dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use another CTE with ROW_NUMBER to assign sequence numbers to dot balls for each batsman. Use LEAD window function to find consecutive dot balls. Group by batsman and find the maximum difference in row numbers.
sql:
WITH AllBatsmen AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT batsman
    FROM df
),
OrderedDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_delivery
    FROM
        df
),
DotBallGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        rn_delivery,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_marker
    FROM
        OrderedDeliveries
),
ConsecutiveDotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_marker,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        DotBallGroups
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_marker
),
MaxStreaksPerBatsman AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak_calculated
    FROM
        ConsecutiveDotBallStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    ab.batsman,
    COALESCE(ms.longest_dot_ball_streak_calculated, 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    AllBatsmen ab
LEFT JOIN
    MaxStreaksPerBatsman ms ON ab.batsman = ms.batsman

intent: Find the bowler who has the highest maximum runs conceded in a single over.

    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,

intent: Determine the overs in which each bowler has conceded the most runs, indicating their toughest overs.
structure: Use a CTE to calculate total runs conceded by each bowler in each over (CEIL(overs)). Then, group by bowler and find the maximum runs conceded in any single over.
sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_conceded_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_number
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(runs_conceded_in_over) AS max_runs_conceded_in_any_over
FROM over_runs
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  max_runs_conceded_in_any_over DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs of the innings).
structure: Group by batsman, calculate strike rate (total runs / total balls faced * 100) using a CASE expression to filter for death overs. Use a CTE to determine the total number of overs. Window function for ordering.
sql:
WITH TotalOvers AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) as max_overs FROM df
),
DeathOverBalls AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_overs FROM TotalOvers) - 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as is_death_over
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs * is_death_over) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced * is_death_over)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM DeathOverBalls
WHERE is_death_over = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced * is_death_over) > 0
ORDER BY death_over_strike_rate DESC;
