intent: Analyze the number of boundaries (fours and sixes) hit in each over phase (Powerplay, Middle Overs, Death Overs).
structure: Use a CASE expression on CEIL(overs) to define phases. Group by bowler and sum boundaries for each phase.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_powerplay,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_middle_overs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_death_overs
FROM OverPhases
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING boundaries_powerplay > 0 OR boundaries_middle_overs > 0 OR boundaries_death_overs > 0
ORDER BY bowler;

  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundary_concession_rate_death_overs

structure: Grouping by batsman. Calculating strike rate (runs/balls faced) for two distinct phases of the innings (first 10 overs and after 10 overs) using CASE. Comparing aggregated strike rates.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_first_10_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > 10) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > 10) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > 10)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_after_10_overs
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_first_10_overs DESC;

intent: Determine the average runs conceded per over by each bowler in the death overs (last 10 overs).
structure: Grouping by bowler. Using a subquery to find the last over number. Filtering for the last 10 overs. Calculating average runs per over using team_runs. Ordering by this average.
sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_number
    FROM df
),
DeathOversStats AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded,
        SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS total_balls_bowled
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_number FROM MaxOver) - 10
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CAST(total_runs_conceded AS REAL) / total_balls_bowled AS avg_runs_per_over_death_overs
FROM
    DeathOversStats
WHERE
    total_balls_bowled > 0
ORDER BY
    avg_runs_per_over_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze bowler efficiency by calculating wickets per over in different phases of the game (early, middle, death overs).
structure: Using a CTE to define three phases of the game based on `CEIL(overs)`. Grouping by bowler and phase. Calculating wickets per over (bowler_wickets / number of balls in phase). Using CASE within aggregation to count balls per phase.
sql:
WITH BowlersWithWickets AS (
    SELECT
        bowler
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler_wickets > 0
    GROUP BY
        bowler
    HAVING
        SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
)
SELECT
    t.bowler,
    'early' AS phase,
    CAST(CASE
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 6 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 6 THEN t.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 6 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    END AS REAL) AS wickets_per_over_early,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_middle,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_death
FROM
    df AS t
JOIN
    BowlersWithWickets AS bww ON t.bowler = bww.bowler
GROUP BY
    t.bowler

UNION ALL

SELECT
    t.bowler,
    'middle' AS phase,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_early,
    CAST(CASE
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(t.overs) <= 15 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    END AS REAL) AS wickets_per_over_middle,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_death
FROM
    df AS t
JOIN
    BowlersWithWickets AS bww ON t.bowler = bww.bowler
GROUP BY
    t.bowler

UNION ALL

SELECT
    t.bowler,
    'death' AS phase,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_early,
    0.0 AS wickets_per_over_middle,
    CAST(CASE
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 15 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 15 THEN t.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > 15 THEN t.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    END AS REAL) AS wickets_per_over_death
FROM
    df AS t
JOIN
    BowlersWithWickets AS bww ON t.bowler = bww.bowler
GROUP BY
    t.bowler
ORDER BY
    bowler, phase;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of a specific batsman across different phases of the innings (early, middle, death).
structure: Use CASE to define phases based on CEIL(overs), calculate strike rate for each phase, group by batsman and phase.
sql: WITH over_phases AS ( SELECT batsman, batsman_runs, batsman_bowls_faced, CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early' WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle' ELSE 'Death' END AS phase FROM df ) SELECT batsman, phase, CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate FROM over_phases GROUP BY batsman, phase ORDER BY batsman, CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Death' THEN 3 END;

The overs are determined by the ceiling of the `overs` column. Strike rate is calculated as (total runs / balls faced) * 100. Batsmen with 0 balls faced in a phase will have a strike rate of 0.

sql: WITH MatchOver AS (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over FROM df) SELECT d.batsman, CAST(SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS overall_strike_rate, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over - 5) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over - 5) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_over_strike_rate FROM df AS d, MatchOver AS mo GROUP BY d.batsman HAVING SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0;

intent: Identify the longest streak of dot balls faced by any batsman and the corresponding batsman.
structure: Use CTEs to first identify dot balls, then use window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LEAD) to calculate consecutive streaks. Finally, aggregate to find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH AllBatsmen AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT batsman
    FROM df
),
RankedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        df
),
DotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(overs) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        RankedBalls
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
MaxStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
    FROM
        DotBallStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    ab.batsman,
    COALESCE(ms.longest_dot_ball_streak, 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    AllBatsmen ab
LEFT JOIN
    MaxStreaks ms ON ab.batsman = ms.batsman
ORDER BY
    ab.batsman;

intent: Calculate the proportion of balls that result in a boundary (4s or 6s) for each batsman.
structure: Calculate the total number of boundaries (fours + sixes) and divide by the total number of balls faced by each batsman. Group by batsman.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CAST(SUM(batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS boundary_percentage
FROM df
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0;

intent: Analyze the momentum of scoring by looking at the transition of strike rates between early (first 10 overs) and later stages of an innings.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate strike rate for the first 10 overs and the rest of the innings using CASE expressions on CEIL(overs), and compare them. Requires CTEs for clarity and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_early,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase NOT IN ('Early') THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase NOT IN ('Early') THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase NOT IN ('Early') THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_late
FROM OverPhases
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 10
ORDER BY strike_rate_late DESC;

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per over by each bowler across the entire innings.
structure: Group by bowler and use CEIL(overs) to represent each over. Calculate the average of team_runs for each over bowled by a bowler. Requires grouping by bowler and CEIL(overs), then averaging.
sql:
WITH BowlerOverRuns AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_conceded_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  AVG(runs_conceded_in_over) AS avg_runs_per_over
FROM BowlerOverRuns
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_per_over DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen in the first 6 overs versus the rest of the innings, to identify aggressive starters versus those who build innings.
structure: Use CASE expressions to categorize deliveries into 'Powerplay' (CEIL(overs) <= 6) and 'Rest of Innings'. Calculate strike rate for each category using conditional aggregation. Group by batsman.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM df
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 5
ORDER BY strike_rate_powerplay DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the first 6 overs (powerplay) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Group by batsman, use CASE expressions to differentiate between powerplay and non-powerplay overs, calculate strike rate (runs/balls) for each phase using SUM and COUNT aggregates.
sql:
WITH BattingStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_balls,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS non_powerplay_runs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS non_powerplay_balls
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        batsman
    HAVING
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
),
BowledBatsmen AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        bowler AS player_name
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler_bowls_done > 0
)
SELECT
    bs.batsman,
    CAST(bs.powerplay_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.powerplay_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_powerplay,
    CAST(bs.non_powerplay_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bs.non_powerplay_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_non_powerplay
FROM
    BattingStats bs
JOIN
    BowledBatsmen bb ON bs.batsman = bb.player_name;

It uses conditional aggregation within the SUM and COUNT functions to compute runs and balls faced for each phase separately, then calculates the strike rate for each phase. Batsmen with no balls faced in either phase are excluded.

intent: Compare the wicket-taking ability of bowlers in the first 6 overs versus the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Group by bowler, use CASE expressions to define powerplay and death overs, sum wickets in each phase, and calculate wickets per over for each phase.
sql:
WITH MaxOverNum AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS wickets_per_over_powerplay,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM MaxOverNum) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM MaxOverNum) - 5 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS wickets_per_over_death_overs
FROM
    df
GROUP BY
    bowler
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) >= 6
    OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM MaxOverNum) - 5 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) >= 6;

intent: Calculate the total number of dot balls conceded by each bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to identify death overs, filter for deliveries where batsman_runs is 0, group by bowler, count the dot balls.
sql:
WITH death_overs_data AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
  WHERE ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 5
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(is_dot_ball) AS dot_balls_conceded_death_overs
FROM death_overs_data
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY dot_balls_conceded_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the variation in batsman strike rate across different phases of an innings (powerplay vs. death overs).
structure: Group by batsman, calculate strike rate for powerplay (first 6 overs) and death overs (last 6 overs) using CASE statements, and compare them.
sql:
WITH OverBoundaries AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num FROM df
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    CAST(
        CASE
            WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
        END AS REAL
    ) AS strike_rate_powerplay,
    CAST(
        CASE
            WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM OverBoundaries) - 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0.0
            ELSE SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM OverBoundaries) - 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM OverBoundaries) - 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
        END AS REAL
    ) AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM
    df
GROUP BY
    batsman;

sql:
WITH max_over_cte AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over FROM df
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    COALESCE(
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0),
        0.0
    ) AS wickets_per_over_powerplay,
    COALESCE(
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM max_over_cte) - 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) * 6.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM max_over_cte) - 6 THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0),
        0.0
    ) AS wickets_per_over_death_overs
FROM
    df
GROUP BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the trend of runs conceded by each bowler across different phases of the innings.
structure: Create phases using CASE statement on CEIL(overs), then group by bowler and phase, calculating average runs conceded per over.
sql:
WITH BowlerPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  SUM(bowler_runs_given) * 6.0 / NULLIF(SUM(bowler_bowls_done), 0) AS avg_runs_conceded_per_over
FROM BowlerPhases
GROUP BY
  bowler,
  phase
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE phase
    WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Middle Overs' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Death Overs' THEN 3
  END;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate for each batsman. This involves subqueries or CTEs to calculate strike rates separately, then joining or combining them. Use CASE statements for conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH overall_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_batsman_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_batsman_balls_faced
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
),
death_over_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_over_batsman_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_over_batsman_balls_faced
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  o.batsman,
  CAST(o.total_batsman_runs * 100.0 AS REAL) / NULLIF(o.total_batsman_balls_faced, 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
  CAST(COALESCE(d.death_over_batsman_runs, 0) * 100.0 AS REAL) / NULLIF(COALESCE(d.death_over_batsman_balls_faced, 0), 0) AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM overall_stats AS o
LEFT JOIN death_over_stats AS d
  ON o.batsman = d.batsman
WHERE
  o.total_batsman_balls_faced > 0
ORDER BY
  overall_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman in the entire match.
structure: Identify dot balls using a CASE expression. Use window functions to assign a group to each streak of dot balls. Count the length of each streak and find the maximum for each batsman.
sql:
WITH dotballs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_dot_ball = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS non_dot_streak_group
  FROM dotballs
),
max_streak AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streaks
  WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    non_dot_streak_group
  ORDER BY
    streak_length DESC
)
SELECT MAX(streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM max_streak;

intent: Analyze the impact of dot balls by finding the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use window functions to calculate consecutive streaks of dot balls. Group by batsman and find the maximum streak length.
sql:
WITH BallStatus AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_group
    FROM
        BallStatus
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(MAX(streak_length), 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM
        Streaks
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        (rn - rn_group)
) AS DotBallStreaks;

sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_first_10_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_last_10_overs
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0

intent: Compare the strike rate of a specific batsman in the first 10 overs versus the last 10 overs.
structure: Use a CTE with CASE expressions to define phases (first 10 and last 10 overs), then calculate strike rates for each phase and compare.
sql:
WITH MaxOverNumber AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over
    FROM df
),
First10OversSR AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate_first_10_overs
    FROM df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) <= 10
    GROUP BY batsman
),
Last10OversSR AS (
    SELECT
        df.batsman,
        CAST(SUM(df.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate_last_10_overs
    FROM df
    CROSS JOIN MaxOverNumber
    WHERE
        CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over FROM MaxOverNumber) - 10
    GROUP BY df.batsman
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(F10.batsman, L10.batsman) AS batsman,
    F10.strike_rate_first_10_overs,
    L10.strike_rate_last_10_overs
FROM First10OversSR F10
FULL OUTER JOIN Last10OversSR L10
    ON F10.batsman = L10.batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Identify batsmen who have a higher strike rate in the first 6 overs (powerplay) compared to the rest of the match.
structure: Calculate strike rate for first 6 overs and strike rate for remaining overs for each batsman. Use CASE statements to bucket overs and conditional aggregation. Compare the two strike rates.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_match
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_powerplay DESC;

intent: Analyze the impact of dot balls on subsequent scoring for each batsman, specifically how often a boundary (4 or 6) is hit immediately after a dot ball.
structure: Uses a CTE to identify dot balls and boundaries, a window function to check the previous ball's type, grouping by batsman, and counting occurrences.
sql:
WITH ball_types AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs IN (4, 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
lagged_ball_types AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    is_boundary,
    LAG(is_dot, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_is_dot
  FROM ball_types
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS boundary_after_dot_count
FROM lagged_ball_types
WHERE
  is_boundary = 1 AND previous_is_dot = 1
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  boundary_after_dot_count DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a bowler bowls in an over after conceding at least one run.
structure: Use a CTE to filter for overs where a bowler conceded runs, then another CTE to count balls per over. Finally, group by bowler and calculate the average. Aggregation: Average of balls per over. Filtering: Only overs where runs were conceded. Grouping: by bowler.
sql:
WITH overs_with_runs AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_number
  HAVING
    SUM(team_runs) > 0
),
balls_per_over AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    COUNT(overs) AS balls_in_this_over
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) IN (
      SELECT
        over_number
      FROM overs_with_runs
    )
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  AVG(balls_in_this_over) AS avg_balls_after_conceding_run
FROM balls_per_over
GROUP BY
  bowler

WITH max_overs_cte AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_ceiling_overs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  T1.bowler,
  T1.phase,
  T1.total_wickets
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      df.bowler,
      'Powerplay' AS phase,
      SUM(df.bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets
    FROM df
    WHERE
      CEIL(df.overs) <= 10
    GROUP BY
      df.bowler
    UNION ALL

      df.bowler,
      'Death Overs' AS phase,
      SUM(df.bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets

    GROUP BY
      df.bowler

intent: Identify the longest streak of consecutive dot balls conceded by each bowler.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use a window function (LAG) to compare consecutive deliveries. Another CTE to group consecutive dot balls and count streak lengths. Final selection of the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH BowlerDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreaksIdentified AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS rn_status_change
    FROM
        BowlerDeliveries
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        (rn_overall - rn_status_change) AS streak_group
    FROM
        StreaksIdentified
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Filter for dot balls only
),
CalculatedStreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        streak_group
),
MaxStreakPerBowler AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_streak_val
    FROM
        CalculatedStreakLengths
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    d.bowler,
    COALESCE(ms.longest_streak_val, 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_ball_streak
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT bowler FROM df
) AS d
LEFT JOIN MaxStreakPerBowler AS ms
ON d.bowler = ms.bowler;

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in the first six overs versus the death overs (last six overs) of an innings.
structure: Use a CTE to define phases (first six and last six overs) using CEIL(overs). Calculate strike rate for each phase using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) within each phase for each batsman. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH phase_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'First 6 Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) <= 6 OR CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 6 Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS first_6_overs_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 6 Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS first_6_overs_balls,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 6 Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 6 Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 6 Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS first_6_overs_strike_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_balls,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phase_strike_rates
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
  first_6_overs_balls > 0 OR death_overs_balls > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Identify dot balls, then use a window function (ROW_NUMBER) to create groups of consecutive dot balls, count the length of each streak, and find the maximum streak length for each batsman. This query uses CTEs and window functions.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT

        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM df

streak_groups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY rn) AS streak_group_id

),
dot_ball_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM streak_groups
    WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY batsman, streak_group_id
)

    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM dot_ball_streaks
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

WITH ball_status AS (

WITH wicket_balls AS (

intent: Assess the economy rate of bowlers during specific phases of the innings (e.g., powerplay, middle overs, death overs).
structure: Use CASE statement on CEIL(overs) to define phases. Group by bowler and phase. Calculate the total runs conceded and total balls bowled for each bowler in each phase. Compute economy rate (runs per ball).
sql:
WITH BowlerPhase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) >= 1 AND CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  SUM(bowler_runs_given) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(bowler_bowls_done), 0) AS economy_rate
FROM BowlerPhase
GROUP BY
  bowler,
  phase
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN 1
    WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN 2
    ELSE 3
  END;

intent: Analyze the variation in a batsman's strike rate across different phases of an innings (early, middle, death overs).
structure: Group by batsman and phase (derived using CASE on CEIL(overs)). Calculate strike rate (total batsman runs / total batsman balls faced) for each group. Use CASE expression for phase definition. Use subquery or CTE to define phases.
sql:
WITH PhaseRuns AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'

  FROM df

    batsman,
    phase
)

    WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM PhaseRuns
ORDER BY

    WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN 1
    WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN 2

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls bowled by a specific bowler.
structure: Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) to identify dot balls. Then, use another CTE with window functions to group consecutive dot balls. Finally, calculate the maximum streak length for each bowler.
sql:
WITH dot_balls AS (
  SELECT bowler, overs, CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
),
consecutive_dots AS (
  SELECT bowler, overs, is_dot_ball,
         SUM(CASE WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS non_dot_group
  FROM dot_balls
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT bowler, overs, is_dot_ball,
         SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, non_dot_group ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS current_streak
  FROM consecutive_dots
)
SELECT bowler, MAX(current_streak) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM streak_groups
WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Find the number of overs where a bowler took at least one wicket and also conceded at least one boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use CTEs to identify overs with wickets and overs with boundaries for each bowler. Join these CTEs and count the common overs.
sql:
WITH wicket_overs AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df
  WHERE bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY bowler, over_number
),
boundary_overs AS (

)
SELECT

  COUNT(w.over_number) AS overs_with_wickets_and_boundaries
FROM wicket_overs AS w

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the first half of their innings compared to the second half.
structure: Calculate strike rate (runs/balls * 100) for each batsman, split into two halves based on the sequence of balls faced. Use window functions to determine ball sequence and inning halves, then aggregate. Group by batsman and inning half. Output will have batsman, first half SR, second half SR.
sql:
WITH ballseq AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_sequence
  FROM df
),
inninghalves AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN ball_sequence <= (SELECT MAX(ball_sequence) FROM ballseq WHERE batsman = bs.batsman) / 2 THEN 'First Half'
      ELSE 'Second Half'
    END AS inning_half
  FROM ballseq AS bs
),
strikerates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    inning_half,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate
  FROM inninghalves
  GROUP BY batsman, inning_half
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(CASE WHEN inning_half = 'First Half' THEN strike_rate ELSE NULL END) AS first_half_sr,
  MAX(CASE WHEN inning_half = 'Second Half' THEN strike_rate ELSE NULL END) AS second_half_sr
FROM strikerates
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Analyze the run distribution across different phases of the innings for each batsman, focusing on how many runs were scored through boundaries (fours and sixes) versus singles and twos.
structure: Group by batsman and an over-based phase (early, middle, late). Aggregate sums of total runs and boundary runs. Calculate the percentage of runs scored via boundaries.
sql:
WITH PhaseRuns AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS early_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS middle_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS late_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6 ELSE 0 END) AS early_boundary_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6 ELSE 0 END) AS middle_boundary_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6 ELSE 0 END) AS late_boundary_runs
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN early_runs > 0 THEN CAST(early_boundary_runs AS REAL) * 100 / early_runs ELSE 0 END AS early_boundary_percentage,
  CASE WHEN middle_runs > 0 THEN CAST(middle_boundary_runs AS REAL) * 100 / middle_runs ELSE 0 END AS middle_boundary_percentage,
  CASE WHEN late_runs > 0 THEN CAST(late_boundary_runs AS REAL) * 100 / late_runs ELSE 0 END AS late_boundary_percentage
FROM PhaseRuns
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Determine the longest sequence of consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman, indicating periods of pressure or conservative batting.
structure: Use window functions to assign a consecutive group ID to dot balls for each batsman. Count the number of dot balls within each group to find the length of each streak. Find the maximum streak length per batsman.
sql:
WITH DotBalls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot
  FROM df
),
StreakGroups AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    SUM(is_dot) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS consecutive_dot_group
  FROM DotBalls
  WHERE is_dot = 1
),
ConsecutiveCounts AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    consecutive_dot_group,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM StreakGroups
  GROUP BY batsman, consecutive_dot_group
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM ConsecutiveCounts
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY longest_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Evaluate the wicket-taking effectiveness of bowlers during the death overs by calculating their wickets per ball ratio in this phase.
structure: Filter data for the last 5 overs of the innings. For each bowler, calculate the sum of wickets taken and the total balls bowled in this phase. Compute the wickets per ball ratio.
sql:
WITH DeathOverBowlerStats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_in_death,
    COUNT(*) AS balls_in_death
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE WHEN balls_in_death > 0 THEN CAST(wickets_in_death AS REAL) / balls_in_death ELSE 0 END AS death_over_wicket_rate
FROM DeathOverBowlerStats
WHERE balls_in_death > 0
ORDER BY death_over_wicket_rate DESC;

intent: Assess bowler economy rate variation across different phases of the innings: powerplay, middle overs, and death overs.
structure: Divide overs into three phases using CASE expression based on CEIL(overs). Calculate total runs conceded and total balls bowled for each bowler within each phase. Compute the economy rate for each phase.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
PhaseEconomy AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    phase,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded,
    SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS total_balls_bowled
  FROM OverPhases
  GROUP BY bowler, phase
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN (CAST(total_runs_conceded AS REAL) * 6.0) / NULLIF(total_balls_bowled, 0) ELSE NULL END) AS powerplay_economy,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN (CAST(total_runs_conceded AS REAL) * 6.0) / NULLIF(total_balls_bowled, 0) ELSE NULL END) AS middle_overs_economy,
  MAX(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN (CAST(total_runs_conceded AS REAL) * 6.0) / NULLIF(total_balls_bowled, 0) ELSE NULL END) AS death_overs_economy
FROM PhaseEconomy
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY bowler;

intent: Find the average runs scored per over for each batsman.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate the sum of batsman_runs, and divide by the total number of overs faced. Use CEIL(overs) to determine the over number and a subquery to find the maximum over number for normalization. Use a CASE expression to handle division by zero.
sql:
WITH batsman_overs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman, CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(over_number) = 0 THEN 0.0
    ELSE CAST(SUM(runs_in_over) AS REAL) / COUNT(over_number)
  END AS avg_runs_per_over
FROM batsman_overs
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY avg_runs_per_over DESC;

sql:
WITH death_overs_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs_in_death_overs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_in_death_overs
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN total_balls_in_death_overs = 0 THEN 0.0

  END AS strike_rate_in_death_overs
FROM death_overs_data
WHERE total_balls_in_death_overs >= 10
ORDER BY strike_rate_in_death_overs DESC
LIMIT 5;

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use CTEs to first identify dot balls, then group consecutive dot balls, and finally count the length of each streak. Use window functions to partition and order the data.
sql:
WITH grouped_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_identifier
  FROM
    df
),
streak_lengths AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    streak_group_identifier,
    COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
  FROM
    grouped_balls
  WHERE
    batsman_runs = 0
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    streak_group_identifier
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_dot_ball_streak
FROM
  streak_lengths
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Analyze the momentum shift by examining the runs scored in consecutive overs, identifying significant increases or decreases.
structure: Calculate runs scored per over using GROUP BY CEIL(overs). Use LAG window function to get the runs from the previous over and calculate the difference.
sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    over_number
)
SELECT
  over_number,
  runs_in_over,
  LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY over_number) AS previous_over_runs,
  runs_in_over - LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY over_number) AS run_difference
FROM over_runs
ORDER BY over_number;

intent: Identify the balls where a batsman scored a boundary immediately after facing a dot ball, indicating a potential shift in pressure or intent.
structure: Use a CTE to mark dot balls and boundary balls, then use a window function (LAG) to check the previous ball's status, and finally count boundary balls that followed dot balls for each batsman.
sql:
WITH ball_events AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_bowls_faced = 1 AND batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    CASE WHEN batsman_bowls_faced = 1 AND (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball
  FROM df
),
lagged_events AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot_ball,
    is_boundary_ball,
    LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_was_dot
  FROM ball_events
),
boundary_after_dot_counts AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS boundary_after_dot_count
  FROM lagged_events
  WHERE
    is_boundary_ball = 1
    AND previous_ball_was_dot = 1
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  b.batsman,
  COALESCE(badc.boundary_after_dot_count, 0) AS boundary_after_dot_count
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT batsman FROM df) AS b
LEFT JOIN boundary_after_dot_counts AS badc
  ON b.batsman = badc.batsman
ORDER BY
  b.batsman;

intent: Identify streaks of consecutive boundary balls (4s or 6s) hit by batsmen.
structure: Use window functions to identify boundary balls and then calculate consecutive streaks. Uses window functions and CASE expression.
sql:
WITH BallEvents AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        batsman,
        (CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_boundary
    FROM
        df
),
GroupChanges AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        batsman,
        is_boundary,
        -- This flag is 1 if the 'is_boundary' value is different from the previous one.
        -- We initialize LAG with 0, meaning the first ball is treated as if it followed a non-boundary.
        CASE
            WHEN is_boundary = LAG(is_boundary, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) THEN 0
            ELSE 1
        END AS is_new_group_start
    FROM
        BallEvents
),
GroupedData AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        batsman,
        is_boundary,
        -- This 'streak_group_id' increments every time the `is_boundary` value changes.
        -- It effectively assigns unique IDs to consecutive runs of 0s and 1s.
        SUM(is_new_group_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        GroupChanges
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_boundary_streak
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(overs) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        GroupedData
    WHERE
        is_boundary = 1 -- We only care about streaks of boundaries
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
) AS IndividualStreaks
GROUP BY
    batsman

sql:
WITH ball_status AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs IN (4, 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
lagged_status AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    is_boundary,
    -- Get the status of the previous ball for the same batsman
    LAG(is_dot, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_was_dot
  FROM ball_status
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS boundary_after_dot_count
FROM lagged_status
WHERE is_boundary = 1 AND previous_ball_was_dot = 1
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY boundary_after_dot_count DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of runs conceded by each bowler in overs where at least one wicket was taken.
structure: Use a CTE to identify overs with wickets, then group by bowler and calculate the average runs conceded in those specific overs.
sql:
WITH WicketTakingOvers AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df

    bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
),

  GROUP BY
    d.bowler,
    CEIL(d.overs)
)
SELECT
  rcwo.bowler,
  AVG(rcwo.runs_conceded_in_this_over) AS avg_runs_conceded_in_wicket_overs
FROM RunsConcededPerWicketOver AS rcwo

intent: Identify the longest consecutive streak of dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use CTEs. First, identify dot balls. Second, use a window function to calculate the current consecutive dot ball streak. Then, use another window function to identify the start of each streak. Finally, calculate the length of each streak and find the maximum.
sql:
WITH RankedDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_non_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        SUM(is_non_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        RankedDeliveries
),
StreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    current_streak_length AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    StreakLengths
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC
LIMIT 1;

intent: Analyze the highest number of balls a bowler has bowled consecutively without taking a wicket, identifying the maximum streak length per bowler.
structure: Group by bowler, use a window function to identify non-wicket balls, group again to count consecutive non-wicket balls, and finally find the maximum streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH BowlerDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        bowler_wickets,
        CASE WHEN bowler_wickets = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_non_wicket_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakIdentification AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_non_wicket_ball,
        -- Mark the start of a new non-wicket streak:
        -- It's a new streak if the current ball is a non-wicket ball
        -- AND the previous ball (for the same bowler, ordered by overs)
        -- was either a wicket ball (0) or it's the very first ball of the bowler's spell (default 0 for LAG).
        CASE
            WHEN is_non_wicket_ball = 1 AND LAG(is_non_wicket_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_streak_start
    FROM
        BowlerDeliveries
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        is_non_wicket_ball,
        -- Assign a unique ID to each streak of non-wicket balls for each bowler.
        -- This sum increments only when 'is_streak_start' is 1, effectively grouping consecutive non-wicket balls.
        SUM(is_streak_start) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakIdentification
),
CalculatedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        is_non_wicket_ball = 1 -- Only count balls that are part of a non-wicket streak
    GROUP BY
        bowler,
        streak_group_id
),
BowlerMaxStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        MAX(current_streak_length) AS max_streak
    FROM
        CalculatedStreaks
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
-- To ensure all bowlers are included, even those with no non-wicket balls (which implies a longest streak of 0),
-- we get a distinct list of all bowlers from the original table and LEFT JOIN the calculated max streaks.
SELECT
    DISTINCT d.bowler,
    COALESCE(bms.max_streak, 0) AS longest_non_wicket_streak
FROM
    df AS d
LEFT JOIN
    BowlerMaxStreaks AS bms
ON
    d.bowler = bms.bowler;

WITH BallSequence AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,

intent: Find the bowlers who have conceded the most runs in overs where they have also taken wickets.
structure: Create a CTE to identify overs where a bowler took wickets, then join back to the main table to sum runs given in those specific overs and group by bowler.
sql:
WITH wicketovers AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    ceil(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_number
)
SELECT
  d.bowler,
  SUM(d.bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_in_wicket_overs
FROM df AS d
JOIN wicketovers AS wo
  ON d.bowler = wo.bowler AND ceil(d.overs) = wo.over_number
GROUP BY
  d.bowler
ORDER BY
  total_runs_in_wicket_overs DESC;

WITH boundary_overs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df

  SELECT
    df.batsman,
    SUM(df.batsman_runs) AS total_runs,

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive balls a batsman faced without scoring a run.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Use another CTE to group consecutive dot balls using a window function. Calculate the length of each streak and find the maximum length per batsman. Uses window functions and CASE expressions.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_for_state
    FROM
        df
),
streak_groups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        (rn_overall - rn_for_state) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        numbered_balls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        streak_groups
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman;

WITH ball_status AS (

intent: Analyze the streak of non-scoring (dot) balls faced by a batsman, and identify batsmen with long streaks of dot balls.
structure: Use a window function to identify dot balls. Then, use another window function to create groups for consecutive dot balls. Count the length of these streaks for each batsman. Order by streak length.
sql:
WITH BallDetails AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        LAG(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Create a unique group ID for consecutive streaks of the same ball type (dot/non-dot).
        -- A new group starts when the current ball's type is different from the previous ball's type.
        SUM(CASE WHEN is_dot_ball <> prev_is_dot_ball THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        BallDetails
),
DotBallStreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM
        Streaks
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Filter to consider only dot balls for streak calculation
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
MaxDotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
    FROM
        DotBallStreakLengths
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    b.batsman,
    COALESCE(m.longest_dot_ball_streak, 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT batsman FROM df) AS b
LEFT JOIN
    MaxDotBallStreaks AS m ON b.batsman = m.batsman
ORDER BY
    b.batsman;

sql:

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by a batsman, indicating their ability to survive pressure or defend. This uses window functions to track streaks.
structure: Use a CASE expression to identify dot balls. Use window functions (LAG and ROW_NUMBER) to group consecutive dot balls. Calculate the length of each streak and find the maximum streak length per batsman. Use CTEs.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_group_type
    FROM
        df
),
dot_ball_streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        rn_overall - rn_group_type AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        numbered_balls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        dot_ball_streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in death overs (e.g., last 5 overs) to assess their finishing ability. This query uses CASE for phase definition and CTEs.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define 'death overs' based on CEIL(overs). Calculate strike rate (runs/balls) for each batsman within this phase. Group by batsman. Use CTEs.
sql:
WITH DeathOverStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Over' ELSE 'Other' END AS phase
  FROM df
),
StrikeRateInDeath AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0
      ELSE CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    END AS strike_rate
  FROM DeathOverStats
  WHERE phase = 'Death Over'
  GROUP BY
    batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  strike_rate
FROM StrikeRateInDeath
ORDER BY
  strike_rate DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of runs conceded by a bowler in overs where they took at least one wicket.
structure: Use a CTE to identify overs where a bowler took a wicket. Join this back to the main table to sum runs conceded in those specific overs and count the overs. Calculate the average.
sql:
WITH WicketOvers AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs)
),
RunsInWicketOvers AS (
  SELECT
    d.bowler,
    SUM(d.bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_in_wicket_overs,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CEIL(d.overs)) AS num_wicket_overs
  FROM df AS d
  JOIN WicketOvers AS wo ON d.bowler = wo.bowler AND CEIL(d.overs) = wo.over_number
  GROUP BY
    d.bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN num_wicket_overs > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs_in_wicket_overs AS REAL) / num_wicket_overs
    ELSE 0
  END AS avg_runs_conceded_per_wicket_over
FROM RunsInWicketOvers
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_conceded_per_wicket_over DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of each batsman in the powerplay overs (first 6 overs) and compare it to their strike rate in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to define 'phase' (powerplay, death, middle) based on CEIL(overs). Group by batsman and phase, calculating strike rate (SUM(batsman_runs) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)). Join the results for powerplay and death overs for each batsman.
sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num FROM df
),
PowerplayStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS pp_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS pp_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6
  GROUP BY batsman
),
DeathOversStats AS (
  SELECT
    d.batsman,
    SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS do_runs,
    SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS do_balls
  FROM df AS d
  CROSS JOIN MaxOver AS mo
  WHERE CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over_num - 5)
  GROUP BY d.batsman
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(pps.batsman, dos.batsman) AS batsman,
  pps.pp_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(pps.pp_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  dos.do_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(dos.do_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_death
FROM PowerplayStats AS pps
FULL OUTER JOIN DeathOversStats AS dos
  ON pps.batsman = dos.batsman
ORDER BY
  COALESCE(pps.batsman, dos.batsman);

intent: Calculate the total number of sixes hit by each batsman in the 'middle overs' (between the first 6 and last 5 overs) and their conversion rate of sixes per balls faced in this phase.

WITH middle_overs_data AS (

      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_sixes) AS total_sixes_middle_overs,

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their strike rate in the first 10 overs, highlighting changes in aggression.
structure: This query uses CTEs to define phases (first 10 overs and death overs) and then calculates strike rates (runs/ball) for each phase. It joins the results to compare the strike rates side-by-side for each batsman. Aggregation: SUM. Grouping: batsman, phase. Window Functions: None. CTEs: Yes. CASE expressions: Yes. Subqueries: Yes.
sql:
WITH OverMax AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_val
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    df.batsman,
    CASE
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= 10 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= 10 THEN df.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= 10 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    END AS strike_rate_first_10_overs,
    CASE
        WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > OverMax.max_over_val - 5 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > OverMax.max_over_val - 5 THEN df.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > OverMax.max_over_val - 5 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM
    df
CROSS JOIN
    OverMax
GROUP BY
    df.batsman

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per over by each bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs), identifying bowlers who are expensive at the end of the innings.
structure: This query first calculates the total runs conceded in each over for each bowler. It then filters for the death overs and calculates the average of these over-totals per bowler. Aggregation: SUM, AVG. Grouping: bowler, CEIL(overs). Window Functions: None. CTEs: Yes. CASE expressions: None. Subqueries: Yes.
sql:
with over_runs as (
  select 
    bowler, 
    ceil(overs) as over_number,
    sum(team_runs) as runs_in_over
  from df
  group by bowler, over_number
)
select 
  bowler,

from over_runs
where over_number > (select max(ceil(overs)) from df) - 5
group by bowler
order by avg_runs_per_death_over desc;

intent: Identify batsmen who perform exceptionally well (high strike rate) against specific bowlers compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate strike rate for each batsman overall and against each bowler. Use CTEs to separate these calculations. Compare the two strike rates.
sql:
WITH batsman_overall_sr AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) END AS overall_sr
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
),
batsman_bowler_sr AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    bowler,
    CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) END AS bb_sr
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman, bowler
)
SELECT
  bbs.batsman,
  bbs.bowler,
  bbs.bb_sr AS batsman_bowler_strike_rate,
  bos.overall_sr AS batsman_overall_strike_rate
FROM batsman_bowler_sr AS bbs
JOIN batsman_overall_sr AS bos ON bbs.batsman = bos.batsman
WHERE bbs.bb_sr > bos.overall_sr * 1.2 -- Consider a 20% increase as exceptional
ORDER BY
  batsman_bowler_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen in the initial overs versus the middle overs.
structure: Define 'initial overs' (e.g., first 10) and 'middle overs' using CASE statements. Calculate strike rate for each batsman in these two phases and present them side-by-side.
sql:
WITH phase_sr AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Initial Overs'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Late Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE ceil(overs) <= 15 -- Only consider first 15 overs for this comparison
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  s1.batsman,
  CASE WHEN s1.total_balls = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(s1.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s1.total_balls END AS strike_rate_initial_overs,
  CASE WHEN s2.total_balls = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(s2.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s2.total_balls END AS strike_rate_middle_overs
FROM phase_sr AS s1
LEFT JOIN phase_sr AS s2 ON s1.batsman = s2.batsman AND s2.phase = 'Middle Overs'
WHERE s1.phase = 'Initial Overs'
ORDER BY s1.batsman;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs of the innings) and compare it with their overall strike rate.
structure: Use a CTE to define death overs. Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate for each batsman. Use conditional aggregation or subqueries to compare.
sql:
WITH DeathOverStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death' ELSE 'Normal' END AS phase
  FROM df
),
StrikeRates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN 0
      ELSE CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    END AS death_overs_strike_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0
      ELSE CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    END AS overall_strike_rate
  FROM DeathOverStats
  GROUP BY
    batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  overall_strike_rate,
  death_overs_strike_rate
FROM StrikeRates
ORDER BY
  death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded by a bowler per over, considering only overs where they bowled at least 3 balls.
structure: Use a CTE to count balls bowled per over for each bowler. Filter for overs with at least 3 balls. Group by bowler and over. Calculate the average runs conceded per over.
sql:
WITH OverBallCount AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_no,
    COUNT(*) AS balls_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_no
),
FilteredOvers AS (
  SELECT
    d.bowler,
    CEIL(d.overs) AS over_no,
    d.bowler_runs_given
  FROM df AS d
  JOIN OverBallCount AS obc
    ON d.bowler = obc.bowler AND CEIL(d.overs) = obc.over_no
  WHERE
    obc.balls_in_over >= 3
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(over_no) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE CAST(SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT over_no) END AS avg_runs_conceded_per_over
FROM FilteredOvers
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_conceded_per_over DESC;

intent: Analyze the trend of batsman strike rates across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late) to understand their batting approach.
structure: Use CTEs to define phases based on over number (CEIL(overs)). Calculate strike rate (batsman_runs/batsman_bowls_faced) for each batsman within each phase. Group by batsman and phase. Use CASE expressions for phase definition.
sql:
WITH phased_deliveries AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    CASE
      WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0
      ELSE SUM(batsman_runs) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    END AS strike_rate
  FROM phased_deliveries
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  strike_rate AS strike_rate_early,
  (SELECT strike_rate FROM strike_rates sr2 WHERE sr2.batsman = sr1.batsman AND sr2.phase = 'Middle') AS strike_rate_middle,
  (SELECT strike_rate FROM strike_rates sr3 WHERE sr3.batsman = sr1.batsman AND sr3.phase = 'Late') AS strike_rate_late
FROM strike_rates AS sr1
WHERE
  sr1.phase = 'Early'
ORDER BY
  batsman;

The 'Early' phase is defined as the first 6 overs, 'Middle' as overs 7-15, and 'Late' as overs 16 until the end of the innings. intent: Calculate the average runs per ball conceded by bowlers in the initial phase (first 6 overs) and compare it with their average in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to define 'initial' and 'death' overs based on CEIL(overs). Calculate average runs per ball for each bowler in each phase and join the CTE to itself for a wide output.
sql:
WITH MaxOverNumber AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_val
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 6 THEN d.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 6 THEN d.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_initial_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_over_val - 5) THEN d.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_over_val - 5) THEN d.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_death_overs
FROM
    df AS d
CROSS JOIN
    MaxOverNumber AS m
GROUP BY
    d.bowler
ORDER BY
    d.bowler;

intent: Find the longest streak of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls, then use window functions to create streak groups, and finally count the maximum streak length per batsman and bowler.
sql:
WITH BallDetails AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE
            WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_dot_ball,
        -- This flag identifies non-dot balls which act as streak breakers
        CASE
            WHEN batsman_runs != 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_non_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Calculate a running sum of non-dot balls. This sum will be constant
        -- for consecutive dot balls, providing a unique group ID for each streak.
        SUM(is_non_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        BallDetails
),
DotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only consider dot balls for streak counting
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        bowler,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    bowler,
    -- Get the maximum streak length for each batsman-bowler pair.
    -- COALESCE handles cases where a batsman-bowler pair never had a dot ball, 
    -- returning 0 instead of NULL.
    COALESCE(MAX(current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    DotBallStreaks
GROUP BY
    batsman,
    bowler
ORDER BY
    batsman, bowler;

intent: Analyze the distribution of batsman strike rates across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late) for a specific batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to categorize deliveries into innings phases (early, middle, late) based on over number. Then, calculate strike rate for each batsman within each phase. Finally, pivot the results to have phase strike rates as separate columns for each batsman.
sql: SELECT batsman, SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_early, SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) > 6 AND CEILING(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) > 6 AND CEILING(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_middle, SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) > 15 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEILING(overs) > 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_late FROM df GROUP BY batsman

intent: Track the cumulative number of dot balls faced by each batsman, ordered by the delivery sequence.
structure: Create a CTE to identify dot balls. Then, use a window function to calculate the cumulative sum of dot balls for each batsman, ordered by 'overs'.
sql:
WITH dot_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  overs,
  SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_dot_balls
FROM dot_balls
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  overs;

intent: Determine the proportion of wickets taken by each bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs) relative to their total wickets.
structure: Use a CTE to flag deliveries in death overs. Group by bowler. Calculate total wickets and death over wickets. Compute the ratio. Uses CASE expression.
sql:
WITH DeathOverWickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_death_over_wicket
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over_wicket = 1 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS death_over_wickets,
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over_wicket = 1 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_wickets) AS death_over_wicket_percentage
FROM DeathOverWickets
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0;

intent: Calculate the longest consecutive streak of balls where a batsman scored a boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use CTEs to identify boundary balls, group them into streaks, and then find the maximum length of these streaks.
sql:
WITH RankedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_total,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_per_boundary_type
    FROM
        df
),
GroupedBoundaryStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        -- The difference `rn_total - rn_per_boundary_type` creates a unique group identifier
        -- for consecutive rows with the same `is_boundary` value. We are interested in groups where `is_boundary` is TRUE.
        rn_total - rn_per_boundary_type AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        RankedBalls
    WHERE
        is_boundary = TRUE
),
StreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        GroupedBoundaryStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(current_streak_length), 0) AS longest_boundary_streak
FROM
    StreakLengths
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Analyze the momentum of scoring by looking at the difference in runs scored by a batsman on a given ball compared to the average runs they score on balls within the same over.
structure: Window function to calculate average runs per ball within an over for each batsman. Then, calculate the difference between the runs scored on a specific ball and this average. Finally, select these values along with ball details, ordering by the difference to see significant deviations.
sql:
WITH over_avg_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    AVG(batsman_runs) AS avg_runs_per_ball_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
),
delivery_impact AS (
  SELECT
    d.overs,
    d.batsman,
    d.batsman_runs,
    oar.avg_runs_per_ball_in_over,
    d.batsman_runs - oar.avg_runs_per_ball_in_over AS run_difference
  FROM df AS d
  JOIN over_avg_runs AS oar
    ON d.batsman = oar.batsman AND CEIL(d.overs) = oar.over_number
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  overs,
  batsman_runs,
  avg_runs_per_ball_in_over,
  run_difference
FROM delivery_impact
WHERE
  run_difference > 0
ORDER BY
  run_difference DESC
LIMIT 10;

intent: Calculate the difference in runs scored between consecutive overs for each batsman, to identify batsmen who show significant form fluctuations over consecutive overs.
structure: CTE to calculate total runs scored by each batsman in each over. Then use a window function to get the runs from the previous over and calculate the difference. Uses CASE for initial null values.
sql:
WITH batsman_over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  over_number,
  runs_in_over,
  LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY over_number) AS runs_in_previous_over,
  runs_in_over - LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY over_number) AS run_difference_from_previous_over
FROM batsman_over_runs
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  over_number;

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in the first powerplay (first 6 overs) versus the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CTEs to calculate strike rates for each phase. Calculate strike rate as (SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)) * 100. Group by batsman and phase. Aggregation: Ratio (strike rate). Grouping: Batsman, Phase (using CASE on CEIL(overs)). CTEs used.
sql:
WITH phase_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) <= 6 OR CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  s1.batsman,
  CASE WHEN s1.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(s1.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s1.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN s2.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(s2.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / s2.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_strike_rates AS s1
LEFT JOIN phase_strike_rates AS s2 ON s1.batsman = s2.batsman AND s2.phase = 'Death Overs'
WHERE s1.phase = 'Powerplay'
ORDER BY
  s1.batsman;

intent: Identify the batsmen who have hit the most consecutive boundaries (fours or sixes) and determine the length of their longest streak. This reveals batsmen who can accelerate consistently through boundaries.
structure: Identify boundary balls using CASE. Group consecutive boundary balls using window functions (ROW_NUMBER or similar for grouping). Count the length of each streak. Find the maximum streak length per batsman. Uses CTE, CASE, and window functions.
sql:
WITH boundary_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_boundary,
    SUM(is_boundary) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS boundary_streak_group
  FROM boundary_balls
  WHERE
    is_boundary = 1
),
consecutive_counts AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    boundary_streak_group,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    boundary_streak_group
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_consecutive_boundary_streak
FROM consecutive_counts
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  longest_consecutive_boundary_streak DESC;

intent: Analyze the ratio of wickets taken to runs conceded by each bowler in the first 6 overs versus the death overs (last 5 overs). This shows which bowlers are effective at taking wickets under different pressure scenarios.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate wickets and runs conceded by each bowler, categorized into 'first 6 overs' and 'death overs' using CASE and CEIL(overs). Calculate the wicket-to-run ratio for both phases. Uses CTEs, CASE, CEIL(overs), and division.
sql:
WITH phase_bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_first_6,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_given_first_6,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_death,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_given_death
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE WHEN runs_given_first_6 > 0 THEN CAST(wickets_first_6 AS REAL) / runs_given_first_6 ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_first_6,
  CASE WHEN runs_given_death > 0 THEN CAST(wickets_death AS REAL) / runs_given_death ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_death
FROM phase_bowler_stats
WHERE
  runs_given_first_6 > 0 OR runs_given_death > 0
