intent: Analyze the run-scoring trend of batsmen by comparing their strike rates in the first half versus the second half of their innings.
structure: Use a CTE to rank deliveries for each batsman and determine the midpoint of their innings. Split deliveries into 'first_half' and 'second_half' using a CASE statement based on the rank. Group by batsman and calculate strike rates for each half using conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH BatsmanBallDetails AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_seq_num,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman) AS total_balls_for_batsman
    FROM df
),
BatsmanHalfSplit AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        CASE
            WHEN ball_seq_num <= total_balls_for_batsman / 2.0 THEN 'first_half'
            ELSE 'second_half'
        END AS innings_phase
    FROM BatsmanBallDetails
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'first_half' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_first_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'first_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_first_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'second_half' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_second_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'second_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_second_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'first_half' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'first_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_first_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'second_half' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'second_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_second_half
FROM BatsmanHalfSplit
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'first_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 5 AND
    SUM(CASE WHEN innings_phase = 'second_half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 5
ORDER BY strike_rate_second_half DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in death overs (last 5 overs of the match) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and strike rate in death overs for each batsman. Use subqueries to determine match total overs and filter for death overs. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH batsman_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
),
death_overs_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.batsman,
    SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS death_over_runs,
    SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_over_balls
  FROM df AS d
  JOIN (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS total_overs FROM df
  ) AS match_info ON CEIL(d.overs) > match_info.total_overs - 5
  GROUP BY d.batsman
)
SELECT
  bs.batsman,
  CASE WHEN bs.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(bs.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / bs.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN dos.death_over_balls > 0 THEN CAST(dos.death_over_runs AS REAL) * 100 / dos.death_over_balls ELSE 0 END AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM batsman_stats AS bs
LEFT JOIN death_overs_stats AS dos ON bs.batsman = dos.batsman
WHERE bs.total_balls > 0
ORDER BY death_over_strike_rate DESC;

WITH death_overs_data AS (
  SELECT
    d.batsman,
    d.batsman_runs,
    d.batsman_fours,
    d.batsman_sixes,
    CASE WHEN d.batsman_runs IN (4, 6) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END AS boundary_runs,

FROM death_overs_data

intent: Determine the longest streak of consecutive dot balls for each bowler.
structure: Uses CTEs and window functions (ROW_NUMBER, SUM) to identify streaks of dot balls. Aggregation is MAX(streak_length). Grouping is by bowler.
sql:
WITH dot_balls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot
  FROM df
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY overs) AS overall_rn,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) - SUM(is_dot) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM dot_balls
),
consecutive_dots AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    streak_group,
    COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_groups
  WHERE is_dot = 1
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    streak_group
  HAVING
    COUNT(*) > 0
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM consecutive_dots
GROUP BY
  bowler
ORDER BY
  longest_dot_ball_streak DESC;

intent: Determine the strike rate of batsmen during the initial phase (first 10 overs) versus the middle phase (overs 11-20) of an innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'Initial' (CEIL(overs) <= 10) and 'Middle' (10 < CEIL(overs) <= 20). Calculate total runs and balls faced for each phase per batsman. Compute strike rate for each phase. Use CTEs to manage intermediate results.
sql:
WITH PhaseRunsAndBalls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_initial,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_initial,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_middle,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 20 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_middle
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN balls_initial > 0 THEN CAST(runs_initial AS REAL) * 100.0 / balls_initial ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_initial,
  CASE WHEN balls_middle > 0 THEN CAST(runs_middle AS REAL) * 100.0 / balls_middle ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_middle
FROM PhaseRunsAndBalls
WHERE balls_initial > 0 OR balls_middle > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_middle DESC;

intent: Analyze the batting momentum by looking at the increase in runs scored on deliveries immediately following a boundary (four or six).
structure: Use a window function to identify if the previous ball was a boundary. Then, calculate the average runs scored on balls immediately following a boundary for each batsman. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH BallAfterBoundary AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS was_previous_ball_boundary

)

  batsman,

intent: Examine the distribution of batsman runs across different phases of the innings: Early (1-5 overs), Middle (6-15 overs), and Late (16+ overs).
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize each delivery into 'Early', 'Middle', or 'Late' phases based on CEIL(overs). Then, group by batsman and these phases to calculate the total runs scored in each phase. Finally, pivot the results for a wide format.
sql:
WITH PhaseAnalysis AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 5 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase,
    batsman_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_early,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_middle,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_late
FROM PhaseAnalysis
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY runs_late DESC;

structure: Use a CTE with the LAG window function to identify dot balls. Then, in another CTE, identify boundary balls. Join these CTEs to find instances where a boundary ball follows a dot ball. Group by batsman and count these occurrences. Use LAG and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH delivery_type AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
lagged_delivery AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_boundary,
    LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_was_dot
  FROM delivery_type
)

  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS boundaries_after_dot_ball
FROM lagged_delivery
WHERE
  is_boundary = 1 AND previous_was_dot = 1
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY

sql:
SELECT

    WHEN CEIL(overs) >= 7 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'

FROM df

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in the powerplay overs versus the death overs.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'Powerplay' (first 6 overs) and 'Death Overs' (last 6 overs). Group by batsman and the new 'phase' column, aggregating runs and balls faced. Then, calculate strike rates for each phase. Use a subquery to determine the start of death overs based on the maximum over number.
sql:
WITH phase_runs_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_runs_balls
WHERE phase IN ('Powerplay', 'Death Overs')
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

structure: Use CASE expression to define phases (death overs vs. early overs). Group by batsman and phase. Calculate strike rate (total runs / total balls faced) using conditional aggregation. Use a subquery to calculate total overs.
sql:
WITH MaxOverNum AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_val FROM df
),
BatsmanPhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    T1.batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(T1.overs) > (m.max_over_val - 1) THEN T1.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(T1.overs) > (m.max_over_val - 1) THEN T1.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_balls,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(T1.overs) <= (m.max_over_val - 1) THEN T1.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS early_overs_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(T1.overs) <= (m.max_over_val - 1) THEN T1.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS early_overs_balls
  FROM df AS T1
  CROSS JOIN MaxOverNum AS m
  GROUP BY T1.batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COALESCE(death_overs_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(death_overs_balls, 0), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  COALESCE(early_overs_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(early_overs_balls, 0), 0) AS strike_rate_early_overs
FROM BatsmanPhaseStats
WHERE (death_overs_balls + early_overs_balls) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

WITH DotBall AS (
  SELECT

  FROM df
),

  SELECT

intent: Compare the average runs scored per ball in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings for each batsman.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: first 10 overs and rest of innings. Group by batsman and phase. Calculate the sum of batsman runs and batsman bowls faced for each group. Compute strike rate for each phase. Use CEIL(overs) for phase definition.
sql:
WITH BatsmanPhaseStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs'
            ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
        END AS phase,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM df
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs'
            ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
        END
),
EligibleBatsmen AS (
    SELECT
        batsman
    FROM BatsmanPhaseStats
    WHERE total_balls_faced > 0
    GROUP BY batsman
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT phase) = 2
)
SELECT
    bps.batsman,
    bps.phase,
    (CAST(bps.total_runs AS REAL) * 100.0) / NULLIF(bps.total_balls_faced, 0) AS strike_rate
FROM BatsmanPhaseStats AS bps
JOIN EligibleBatsmen AS eb
    ON bps.batsman = eb.batsman
ORDER BY
    bps.batsman,
    CASE bps.phase
        WHEN 'First 10 Overs' THEN 1
        ELSE 2
    END;

sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS over_phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  over_phase,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM OverPhases
WHERE over_phase IN ('Powerplay', 'Death Overs')
GROUP BY
  batsman,
  over_phase
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  CASE over_phase WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1 WHEN 'Death Overs' THEN 2 END;

intent: Assess the impact of wickets on scoring rate in the subsequent over.
structure: Identify overs where wickets fell and calculate the average runs scored in the over immediately following those wicket-taking overs. sql:
WITH WicketOvers AS (
  SELECT
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    CASE WHEN SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS wicket_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    CEIL(overs)
),
OverRuns AS (
  SELECT
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    CEIL(overs)
),
OverComparison AS (
  SELECT
    wo.over_number,
    wo.wicket_in_over,
    LEAD(wo.over_number, 1, wo.over_number) OVER (ORDER BY wo.over_number) AS next_over_number,
    LEAD(wo.wicket_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY wo.over_number) AS next_over_wicket
  FROM WicketOvers wo
)
SELECT
  AVG(or_next.runs_in_over) AS avg_runs_after_wicket_over
FROM OverRuns or_current
JOIN OverComparison oc ON or_current.over_number = oc.over_number
JOIN OverRuns or_next ON oc.next_over_number = or_next.over_number
WHERE oc.wicket_in_over = 1 AND oc.next_over_wicket = 0;

WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT

    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay' ELSE 'Death' END AS phase

    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls

    batsman,

FROM PhaseMetrics

    FROM StreakGroups
    WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY batsman, streak_group_id
),
MaxStreaks AS (

        MAX(streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
    FROM CalculatedStreaks

intent: Find the longest streak of dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls, then use another CTE with window functions to identify consecutive dot ball streaks. Finally, group and count to find the maximum streak length per batsman. Uses CTEs and window functions.
sql:
WITH BallData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakStartFlag AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- A new streak of dot balls starts if the current ball is a dot ball
        -- AND the previous ball (for the same batsman) was NOT a dot ball.
        -- LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) treats the 'previous' ball before the first ball
        -- of an innings as not a dot ball, correctly identifying a dot ball on the first delivery as a new streak.
        CASE
            WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 AND LAG(is_dot_ball, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_new_dot_ball_streak_start
    FROM
        BallData
),
GroupedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Cumulatively sum the 'is_new_dot_ball_streak_start' flags to assign a unique group_id
        -- to each consecutive streak of dot balls for a given batsman.
        SUM(is_new_dot_ball_streak_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakStartFlag
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only include actual dot balls for counting streaks
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length -- Count balls within each identified streak group
    FROM
        GroupedStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
) AS IndividualStreakLengths
GROUP BY
    batsman

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per over by each bowler across different phases of the innings (early, middle, death).
structure: Uses a CTE to define three phases: early (first 6 overs), middle (overs 7-15), and death (last 5 overs). Aggregates runs conceded by bowler for each phase. Calculates the average runs per over for each phase.
sql:
WITH MatchOverInfo AS (
    SELECT
        CEIL(MAX(df.overs)) AS max_match_over_num
    FROM df
),
BowlerEarlyStats AS (
    SELECT
        df.bowler,
        SUM(df.bowler_runs_given) AS early_total_runs,
        SUM(df.bowler_bowls_done) AS early_total_balls
    FROM df
    WHERE CEIL(df.overs) <= 6
    GROUP BY df.bowler
),
BowlerMiddleStats AS (
    SELECT
        df.bowler,
        SUM(df.bowler_runs_given) AS middle_total_runs,
        SUM(df.bowler_bowls_done) AS middle_total_balls
    FROM df
    WHERE CEIL(df.overs) > 6 AND CEIL(df.overs) <= 15
    GROUP BY df.bowler
),
BowlerDeathStats AS (
    SELECT
        df.bowler,
        SUM(df.bowler_runs_given) AS death_total_runs,
        SUM(df.bowler_bowls_done) AS death_total_balls
    FROM df
    WHERE CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_match_over_num FROM MatchOverInfo) - 5
    GROUP BY df.bowler
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(be.bowler, bm.bowler, bd.bowler) AS bowler,
    COALESCE(be.early_total_runs * 6.0 / NULLIF(be.early_total_balls, 0), 0.0) AS avg_runs_per_over_early,
    COALESCE(bm.middle_total_runs * 6.0 / NULLIF(bm.middle_total_balls, 0), 0.0) AS avg_runs_per_over_middle,
    COALESCE(bd.death_total_runs * 6.0 / NULLIF(bd.death_total_balls, 0), 0.0) AS avg_runs_per_over_death
FROM
    BowlerEarlyStats be
FULL OUTER JOIN BowlerMiddleStats bm ON be.bowler = bm.bowler
FULL OUTER JOIN BowlerDeathStats bd ON COALESCE(be.bowler, bm.bowler) = bd.bowler
ORDER BY
    bowler;

WITH innings_halves AS (
  SELECT

  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'Second Half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'Second Half' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'Second Half' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_second_half

intent: Determine the average number of balls a batsman takes to hit their first boundary (four or six) in the match.
structure: Use a CTE to rank deliveries for each batsman in sequence. Filter for boundary-scoring deliveries. Calculate the average rank (which represents balls faced) for the first boundary.
sql:
WITH StintIdentification AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        -- Detect start of a new batting stint/innings for a batsman
        -- A new stint starts if the batsman changes from the previous ball (globally ordered)
        -- OR if the 'overs' sequence restarts for the same batsman (e.g., from 10.6 to 0.1)
        -- The assumption here is that 'overs' restarts at 0.1 for a new innings.
        CASE
            WHEN LAG(batsman) OVER (ORDER BY overs) IS NULL THEN 1 -- First ball in dataset
            WHEN LAG(batsman) OVER (ORDER BY overs) <> batsman THEN 1
            WHEN LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) > overs THEN 1 -- overs reset for same batsman, indicating new innings
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_stint_start
    FROM df
),
StintsNumbered AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        -- Assign a unique ID to each batting stint/innings for each batsman
        SUM(is_stint_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS batsman_stint_id
    FROM StintIdentification
),
BallsToFirstBoundaryPerStint AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_stint_id,
        -- Calculate balls faced within each stint
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, batsman_stint_id ORDER BY overs) AS balls_faced_in_stint,
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary
    FROM StintsNumbered
),
FirstBoundaryInEachStint AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_stint_id,
        MIN(balls_faced_in_stint) AS balls_to_first_boundary
    FROM BallsToFirstBoundaryPerStint
    WHERE is_boundary = TRUE
    GROUP BY batsman, batsman_stint_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_to_first_boundary) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM FirstBoundaryInEachStint
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_to_first_boundary ASC;

intent: Find the average runs scored in overs immediately following an over where at least one wicket fell.
structure: Use CTEs to identify overs with wickets and calculate runs per over. Join these CTEs to find runs in overs following wicket-taking overs.
sql:
WITH WicketOvers AS (
  SELECT
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY
    CEIL(overs)
),
OverRuns AS (
  SELECT
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    CEIL(overs)
),
LaggedOverRuns AS (
  SELECT
    over_number,
    runs_in_over,
    LAG(runs_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY over_number) AS previous_over_runs
  FROM OverRuns
)
SELECT
  AVG(lor.runs_in_over) AS avg_runs_after_wicket_over
FROM LaggedOverRuns AS lor
JOIN WicketOvers AS wo ON lor.previous_over_runs > 0 AND lor.over_number = wo.over_number + 1;

intent: Identify the top N batsmen based on their total runs scored, considering only deliveries where they faced at least one ball.
structure: Group by batsman and sum their runs and balls faced. Filter for batsmen who faced at least one ball. Order by total runs and limit the results.
sql:

  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs_scored
FROM df
WHERE

intent: Analyze the batting performance by calculating the strike rate for each batsman in the first over of their innings.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate total runs and total balls faced in the first over, then compute strike rate. Use a CTE to identify the first ball of each innings for each batsman.
sql:
WITH BatsmanBalls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    overs
  FROM df
  WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
),
OverallStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM BatsmanBalls
  GROUP BY batsman
  HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
),
FirstBallInnings AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn
  FROM BatsmanBalls
),
FirstBallStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS first_ball_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS first_ball_faced
  FROM FirstBallInnings
  WHERE rn = 1
  GROUP BY batsman
  HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
)
SELECT
  os.batsman,
  CAST(os.total_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(os.total_balls_faced, 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
  CAST(fbs.first_ball_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(fbs.first_ball_faced, 0) AS first_ball_strike_rate
FROM OverallStats os
JOIN FirstBallStats fbs ON os.batsman = fbs.batsman
ORDER BY first_ball_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Identify batsmen who tend to score boundaries immediately after facing a dot ball.
structure: Use a CTE to flag dot balls, then use a window function to check the previous ball's status. Group by batsman to count boundary-after-dot-ball instances.
sql:
WITH BatsmanConsecutiveBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs AS current_batsman_runs,
        LEAD(batsman_runs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_batsman_runs,
        LEAD(batsman_fours, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_batsman_fours,
        LEAD(batsman_sixes, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_batsman_sixes
    FROM
        df
),
CalculatedInstances AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN current_batsman_runs = 0 AND (next_batsman_fours > 0 OR next_batsman_sixes > 0) THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_dot_then_boundary,
        CASE
            WHEN current_batsman_runs = 0 AND next_batsman_runs IS NOT NULL THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_dot_then_any_ball
    FROM
        BatsmanConsecutiveBalls
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(is_dot_then_boundary) AS boundaries_after_dot_ball,
    SUM(is_dot_then_any_ball) AS total_balls_analysed
FROM
    CalculatedInstances
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    SUM(is_dot_then_any_ball) >= 5
ORDER BY
    batsman

intent: Analyze the variation in scoring rate by batsmen in the death overs (last 10 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate overall strike rate and death overs strike rate for each batsman. Compare these two rates. Group by batsman. Use conditional aggregation and ratio calculation. Order by death overs strike rate.
sql:
WITH PlayerStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM df
    GROUP BY batsman
),
DeathOverStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_overs_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_overs_balls_faced
    FROM df
    WHERE ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 10
    GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
    p.batsman,
    CASE WHEN p.total_balls_faced > 0 THEN CAST(p.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / p.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
    CASE WHEN d.death_overs_balls_faced > 0 THEN CAST(d.death_overs_runs AS REAL) * 100 / d.death_overs_balls_faced ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM PlayerStats p
LEFT JOIN DeathOverStats d ON p.batsman = d.batsman
WHERE p.total_balls_faced > 0
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Identify batsmen who have a high boundary percentage (fours and sixes) in the first 10 overs of their innings.
structure: Use a CTE to filter deliveries in the first 10 overs. Calculate the total boundaries (fours + sixes) and total balls faced for each batsman within this phase. Compute the boundary percentage. Group by batsman. Order by boundary percentage.
sql:
WITH First10Overs AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
    FROM df
    WHERE ceil(overs) <= 10
    GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(boundaries AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END AS boundary_percentage
FROM First10Overs
WHERE total_balls > 0
ORDER BY boundary_percentage DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring momentum by calculating cumulative runs scored by batsmen over successive overs.
structure: Use window functions to calculate the cumulative sum of batsman runs, grouped by batsman and ordered by overs. This will show how runs accumulate over the course of an innings.
sql:
SELECT
    batsman,
    ceil(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_this_over,
    SUM(SUM(batsman_runs)) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY ceil(overs))
    AS cumulative_runs
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman, ceil(overs)
ORDER BY batsman, over_number;

intent: Analyze the boundary percentage for each batsman across different phases of the innings (Powerplay, Middle, Death).
structure: This query uses a CASE statement within a CTE to categorize overs into phases (Powerplay, Middle, Death). It then calculates total runs and total boundaries for each batsman within each phase. Finally, it computes the boundary percentage for each batsman in each phase, preferring a wide output format for each batsman if possible.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Death'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) AS total_boundaries
  FROM over_phases
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_boundaries ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_boundaries,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN total_boundaries ELSE 0 END) AS middle_boundaries,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS middle_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN total_boundaries ELSE 0 END) AS death_boundaries,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_runs
FROM phase_stats
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen in the first 10 overs versus the last 10 overs of an innings.
structure: This query uses a CTE to define phases ('Early' for first 10 overs, 'Late' for last 10 overs). It then calculates strike rate for each batsman within these phases, requiring grouping by batsman and phase, and using CASE expressions to define the phases. The output will show strike rates for both phases per batsman in a wide format.
sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_val FROM df
)
SELECT
    t.batsman,
    (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_early,
    (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > mo.max_over_val - 10 THEN t.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > mo.max_over_val - 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_late
FROM
    df AS t, MaxOver AS mo
GROUP BY
    t.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 6
    AND SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > mo.max_over_val - 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 6;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen who score only boundaries (fours or sixes) in the death overs.
structure: This query uses a CTE to identify deliveries in the death overs that were boundaries. It then aggregates by batsman to calculate total runs scored and balls faced on these boundary deliveries and computes the strike rate. It uses CASE expressions for filtering and aggregation.
sql:
WITH death_boundary_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
    AND (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0)
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_only_strike_rate
FROM death_boundary_balls
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) >= 3
ORDER BY
  boundary_only_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of a batsman in overs where they scored boundaries versus overs where they did not.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize each ball as a boundary or non-boundary. Then, group by batsman and this category to calculate the strike rate (total runs / total balls faced). Use window functions to achieve the desired grouping and aggregation.
sql:
WITH BallCategorization AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball
  FROM df
),
StrikeRateComparison AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    is_boundary_ball,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM BallCategorization
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    is_boundary_ball
)
SELECT
  src.batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN src.is_boundary_ball = 1 THEN CAST(src.total_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / src.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_with_boundaries,
  SUM(CASE WHEN src.is_boundary_ball = 0 THEN CAST(src.total_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / src.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS strike_rate_without_boundaries
FROM StrikeRateComparison AS src
WHERE src.total_balls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
  src.batsman
ORDER BY
  src.batsman;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls between boundaries hit by a specific batsman.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify boundary balls and then calculate the difference in 'overs' between consecutive boundaries for a given batsman. Finally, calculates the average of these differences.
sql:
WITH BoundaryDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        (FLOOR(overs) * 6 + CAST(ROUND((overs - FLOOR(overs)) * 10, 0) AS INT)) AS total_balls_at_boundary
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
),
ConsecutiveBoundaryIntervals AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        total_balls_at_boundary - LAG(total_balls_at_boundary) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY total_balls_at_boundary) AS balls_between_boundaries
    FROM
        BoundaryDeliveries
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_between_boundaries) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM
    ConsecutiveBoundaryIntervals
WHERE
    balls_between_boundaries IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen during the powerplay overs (first 6 overs) versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Uses a CTE to define phases (powerplay and rest of innings) based on CEIL(overs) using CASE. Aggregates runs and balls faced per batsman and phase. Calculates strike rates for each phase using conditional aggregation within the final SELECT.
sql:
WITH phasestrikerate AS (
  SELECT batsman,
         CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay' ELSE 'Rest of Innings' END AS phase,
         SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
         SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT batsman,
       CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS powerplay_strike_rate,
       CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS rest_of_innings_strike_rate
FROM phasestrikerate
WHERE total_balls > 0
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Calculate the average runs conceded per ball by bowlers in overs where they took at least one wicket.
structure: Filters for deliveries where bowler_wickets > 0. Groups by bowler and calculates the average runs given per ball in those specific overs.
sql:
WITH WicketTakingOvers AS (
    -- Identify all unique (bowler, over_number) combinations where the bowler took at least one wicket
    SELECT DISTINCT
        bowler,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number
    FROM df
    WHERE bowler_wickets > 0
)
SELECT
    d.bowler,
    SUM(d.bowler_runs_given) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(d.bowler_bowls_done), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_in_wicket_overs
FROM df AS d
INNER JOIN WicketTakingOvers AS wto
    ON d.bowler = wto.bowler
    AND CEIL(d.overs) = wto.over_number
GROUP BY
    d.bowler
HAVING
    SUM(d.bowler_bowls_done) > 0
ORDER BY
    avg_runs_per_ball_in_wicket_overs ASC;

intent: Find the average number of balls faced by a batsman before hitting their first boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use a CTE to identify the delivery number of the first boundary for each batsman. Then, calculate the average of these delivery numbers.
sql:
WITH InferredInnings AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN CEIL(overs) = 1 AND LAG(CEIL(overs)) OVER (ORDER BY overs) IS NULL THEN 1
            WHEN CEIL(overs) < LAG(CEIL(overs)) OVER (ORDER BY overs) THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END) OVER (ORDER BY overs) AS innings_id
    FROM df
),
RunningBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        innings_id,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY innings_id, batsman ORDER BY overs) AS balls_faced_in_innings
    FROM InferredInnings
),
FirstBoundaryPerInnings AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        innings_id,
        MIN(balls_faced_in_innings) AS balls_to_first_boundary
    FROM RunningBalls
    WHERE batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
    GROUP BY batsman, innings_id
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_to_first_boundary) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM FirstBoundaryPerInnings
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_to_first_boundary ASC;

intent: Investigate the scoring pattern difference between a batsman's first and last 10 overs faced.
structure: Use a CTE to bucket overs into 'early' (first 10) and 'late' (last 10) phases. Within each phase, calculate total runs and total balls faced. Then, compute the strike rate for each phase per batsman. Use CASE statement for phase definition. Window function to find max over.
sql:
WITH PhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN 'Late'
      ELSE 'Middle'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
AggPhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM PhaseStats
  WHERE phase IN ('Early', 'Late')
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_early_10_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_late_10_overs
FROM AggPhaseStats
WHERE phase IN ('Early', 'Late')
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate for each batsman. This involves CTEs for phase definition, aggregation, and then a final SELECT with conditional aggregation to compare the two strike rates.
sql:
WITH PhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Normal Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Normal Overs' THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS normal_overs_strike_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM PhaseStats
WHERE
  total_balls > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Normal Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a bowler bowls before conceding their first boundary.
structure: Flag each delivery where a boundary was conceded by the batsman. Then, for each bowler, find the sequence number of the first boundary delivery. Calculate the average of these sequence numbers. This requires ranking or row numbering within partitions and then aggregation.
sql:
WITH numbered_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        bowler,
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY overs) AS global_delivery_seq,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS bowler_delivery_seq
    FROM
        df
),
identified_spells AS (
    SELECT
        overs,
        bowler,
        is_boundary,
        (global_delivery_seq - bowler_delivery_seq) AS spell_group
    FROM
        numbered_deliveries
),
bowls_in_spell AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        spell_group,
        is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, spell_group ORDER BY overs) AS balls_in_this_spell
    FROM
        identified_spells
),
first_boundary_balls_per_spell AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        spell_group,
        MIN(balls_in_this_spell) AS first_boundary_balls
    FROM
        bowls_in_spell
    WHERE
        is_boundary = TRUE
    GROUP BY
        bowler, spell_group
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    AVG(first_boundary_balls) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM
    first_boundary_balls_per_spell
GROUP BY
    bowler
ORDER BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the first over (0-0.6) versus the rest of the innings, identifying who scores more freely early on.
structure: Use a CTE to categorize deliveries into 'first over' and 'rest of innings'. Then, group by batsman and phase, calculating strike rate (total runs / total balls faced). Finally, pivot the results to show strike rates side-by-side for comparison.
sql:
WITH PhaseDeliveries AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) = 0 THEN 'First Over'
      ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
PhaseStrikeRates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM PhaseDeliveries
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First Over' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First Over' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First Over' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_first_over
FROM PhaseStrikeRates
WHERE
  total_balls > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  strike_rate_rest_of_innings > 0 OR strike_rate_first_over > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_first_over DESC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a batsman faces between hitting consecutive boundaries (fours or sixes).
structure: Use a CTE to identify boundary balls. Then, use a window function to find the previous boundary ball for each batsman. Calculate the difference in overs (ball count) and then find the average difference, grouped by batsman.
sql:
WITH BoundaryDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        FLOOR(overs) * 6 + CAST(ROUND((overs - FLOOR(overs)) * 10) AS INTEGER) AS absolute_ball_number
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
),
LaggedBoundaries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        absolute_ball_number,
        LAG(absolute_ball_number, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY absolute_ball_number) AS prev_absolute_ball_number
    FROM
        BoundaryDeliveries
),
BallDifferences AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        absolute_ball_number - prev_absolute_ball_number AS balls_between_boundaries
    FROM
        LaggedBoundaries
    WHERE
        prev_absolute_ball_number IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(balls_between_boundaries) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM
    BallDifferences
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    avg_balls_between_boundaries ASC;

WITH DeathOvers AS (

WITH PhaseStats AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,

)
SELECT

structure: Uses a CTE to identify boundary deliveries for each bowler, assigning a sequence number. Then, calculates the average of this sequence number per bowler using AVG aggregation.
sql:
WITH BowlerSpells AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        (CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_boundary,
        LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS prev_overs,
        -- Identify the start of a new 'spell' or 'match segment' for a bowler
        -- A new spell begins if it's the first delivery for the bowler or if overs count resets
        CASE
            WHEN LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) IS NULL THEN 1 -- First delivery for this bowler in the dataset
            WHEN overs < LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) THEN 1 -- Overs count reset, indicating a new spell/match/inning
            ELSE 0
        END AS new_spell_flag
    FROM
        df
),
SpellsWithId AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_boundary,
        -- Assign a unique spell_id for each logical spell for a bowler
        SUM(new_spell_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS spell_id
    FROM
        BowlerSpells
),
DeliveriesInSpellRanked AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        spell_id,
        overs,
        is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler, spell_id ORDER BY overs) AS ball_sequence_in_spell
    FROM
        SpellsWithId
),
FirstBoundaryPerSpellInstance AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        spell_id,
        MIN(ball_sequence_in_spell) AS first_boundary_ball_num
    FROM
        DeliveriesInSpellRanked
    WHERE
        is_boundary = 1
    GROUP BY
        bowler, spell_id
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CAST(AVG(first_boundary_ball_num) AS REAL) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM
    FirstBoundaryPerSpellInstance
GROUP BY
    bowler
ORDER BY
    bowler;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by calculating the average runs scored on the ball immediately following a boundary.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify boundary balls and then uses a window function (LEAD) to get the runs scored on the next ball for each batsman. Aggregates using AVG.
sql:
WITH BattingEvents AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        (CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS batsman_ball_seq
    FROM df
),
BoundaryFollowUps AS (
    SELECT
        b1.batsman,
        b2.batsman_runs AS runs_on_next_ball
    FROM BattingEvents b1
    JOIN BattingEvents b2
        ON b1.batsman = b2.batsman
        AND b1.batsman_ball_seq + 1 = b2.batsman_ball_seq
    WHERE b1.is_boundary = 1
)

    batsman,
    AVG(runs_on_next_ball) AS avg_runs_after_boundary
FROM BoundaryFollowUps

    batsman;

WITH FirstOverStats AS (

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to non-death overs.
structure: Calculate strike rate using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) for two phases: death overs (last 2) and non-death overs. Group by batsman. Use CASE expressions to define phases.
sql:
WITH MaxOverNum AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 AS REAL)
        / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 AS REAL)
        / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_non_death_overs
FROM df AS d
CROSS JOIN MaxOverNum AS mo
GROUP BY d.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_over - 2) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY d.batsman;

intent: Analyze the batsmen's performance by calculating their strike rate in the first 6 overs (powerplay) vs. middle overs (overs 7-15) vs. death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use CASE expressions to define three phases: powerplay, middle overs, and death overs. Calculate strike rate (runs/balls * 100) for each phase, grouping by batsman. Use CTEs to structure the phase-based calculations.
sql:
WITH phased_deliveries AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN ceil(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM phased_deliveries
  WHERE phase != 'Other'
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 1 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 1 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_middle_overs,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 1 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_stats
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
  OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
  OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

sql:
WITH wickets_per_ball AS (

sql:
WITH batsman_boundary_overs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    ceil(overs) AS over_no
  FROM df
  WHERE
    batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
  GROUP BY

SELECT
  df.batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(df.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_in_boundary_overs
FROM df
JOIN batsman_boundary_overs AS bbo
  ON df.batsman = bbo.batsman AND ceil(df.overs) = bbo.over_no
GROUP BY
  df.batsman
HAVING SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_in_boundary_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Calculate strike rates using CASE statements to define phases (death vs. non-death overs) and aggregate by batsman. Uses CTEs for phase definition and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Non-Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_non_death_overs
FROM phase_stats
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Non-Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Evaluate batsman's boundary hitting consistency by finding the average number of balls between consecutive boundaries (fours or sixes) for each batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to mark deliveries that are boundaries. Then, use a window function (LAG) to find the 'overs' of the previous boundary for each batsman. Calculate the difference to find the interval and then average these intervals.
sql:
WITH boundary_deliveries AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
boundary_intervals AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs - LAG(overs, 1, overs) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS interval_to_prev_boundary
  FROM boundary_deliveries
  WHERE is_boundary = 1
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(interval_to_prev_boundary) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM boundary_intervals
WHERE interval_to_prev_boundary IS NOT NULL AND interval_to_prev_boundary > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  avg_balls_between_boundaries ASC;

intent: Determine the strike rate of a specific batsman in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'death_overs' and 'other_overs'. Calculate strike rate (total runs / total balls faced * 100) for each category per batsman using conditional aggregation. Filter for batsmen who faced a minimum number of balls in death overs.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'death_overs'
      ELSE 'other_overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
PhaseStrikeRates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM OverPhases
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT
  psr.batsman,
  (SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'death_overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'death_overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  (SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'other_overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'other_overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_other_overs
FROM PhaseStrikeRates AS psr
GROUP BY psr.batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'death_overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 10 OR SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'other_overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) >= 10
ORDER BY strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of a batsman in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Compare strike rates using CASE expressions for phases, group by batsman, use SUM for runs and balls, then calculate strike rates.
sql:
WITH MatchMaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > m.max_over_num - 5 THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > m.max_over_num - 5 THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
    SUM(d.batsman_runs) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS overall_strike_rate
FROM
    df AS d
CROSS JOIN
    MatchMaxOver AS m
WHERE
    d.batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
    d.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > m.max_over_num - 5 THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    AND SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
    strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Calculate strike rate using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) for two phases: death overs (CEIL(overs) > total_overs - 5) and other overs. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_other_overs
FROM OverPhases
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

sql:
WITH LaggedBatsmanData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,

        (CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_boundary,

FROM

intent: Calculate the proportion of wickets taken by a bowler in the initial phase of an innings (first 10 overs) versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to define two phases: 'First 10 Overs' and 'Rest of Innings' based on CEIL(overs). Calculate the sum of wickets for each bowler within each phase. Then calculate the proportion of wickets in the first phase.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs'
      ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
PhaseWickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_first_10,
    SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_rest
  FROM OverPhases
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN wickets_first_10 + wickets_rest > 0
    THEN CAST(wickets_first_10 AS REAL) * 100 / (wickets_first_10 + wickets_rest)
    ELSE 0
  END AS percentage_wickets_first_10_overs
FROM PhaseWickets
WHERE wickets_first_10 + wickets_rest > 0
ORDER BY
  percentage_wickets_first_10_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the change in batsman strike rate from the first powerplay (first 6 overs) to the second powerplay (overs 7-15).
structure: Use a CASE statement to define two phases: 'Powerplay 1' and 'Powerplay 2'. Calculate strike rate for each batsman in each phase using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced).
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay 1'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Powerplay 2'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 1' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 1' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 1' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_pp1,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 2' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 2' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay 2' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_pp2
FROM OverPhases
WHERE phase IN ('Powerplay 1', 'Powerplay 2')
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Analyze the impact of batsman boundaries (fours and sixes) on the subsequent ball's runs, per batsman.

intent: Determine the average number of balls between consecutive boundaries (fours or sixes) for each batsman.
structure: Use a CTE to identify boundary deliveries and flag them. Use a window function (LAG) to find the 'overs' value of the previous boundary for each batsman. Calculate the difference in 'overs' to get the interval. Finally, group by batsman and average these intervals, filtering for batsmen with significant intervals.
sql:
WITH BatsmanBallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs, -- Keep overs for correct ordering for ROW_NUMBER and LAG
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_number_faced
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_bowls_faced = 1 -- Only consider balls actually faced by the batsman
),
BoundaryIntervals AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        ball_number_faced,
        LAG(ball_number_faced, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_boundary_ball_number_faced
    FROM
        BatsmanBallSequence
    WHERE
        is_boundary = TRUE
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(CAST(ball_number_faced - prev_boundary_ball_number_faced AS REAL)) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM
    BoundaryIntervals
WHERE
    prev_boundary_ball_number_faced > 0 -- Exclude the interval leading up to the first boundary
    AND (ball_number_faced - prev_boundary_ball_number_faced) > 0 -- Exclude intervals of 0 balls
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    avg_balls_between_boundaries ASC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 10 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to categorize each ball into 'death overs' or 'other overs' based on CEIL(overs). Then, group by batsman and phase to sum runs and balls faced. Finally, calculate strike rates for each phase and batsman.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 10 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_strikerates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM over_phases
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  psr.batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN psr.total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_other_overs
FROM phase_strikerates AS psr
GROUP BY
  psr.batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Death Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN psr.phase = 'Other Overs' THEN psr.total_balls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

sql:
WITH over_phases AS (

    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'

),
phase_wickets AS (

  FROM over_phases

intent: Calculate the strike rate of a specific batsman in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their strike rate in all other overs.
structure: Use CTEs and CASE statements to define phases. Calculate strike rates for each phase. Filter for a specific batsman.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0

    ELSE 0

    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'

  FROM df
)

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0

    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)

structure: Use CASE to define 'Powerplay' and 'Other' phases. Calculate average runs per ball (batsman_runs / batsman_bowls_faced) for each phase. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (

      ELSE 'Other Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS avg_runs_per_ball_powerplay,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Other Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS avg_runs_per_ball_other_overs
FROM phase_stats
WHERE
  batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0

  batsman;

intent: Find the maximum number of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use a window function (LAG) to check for consecutive dot balls. A CTE will be used to identify dot balls and then LAG to compare with the previous ball. Finally, group by batsman to find the maximum streak.
sql:
WITH RankedBalls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_num,
        LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
),
StreakMarkers AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ball_num,
        CASE
            WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND prev_batsman_runs != 0 THEN 1
            WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND ball_num = 1 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_streak_start
    FROM
        RankedBalls
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ball_num,
        SUM(is_streak_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakMarkers
),
ActualDotBallStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakGroups
    WHERE
        batsman_runs = 0
),
StreakLengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_consecutive_dot_balls
    FROM
        ActualDotBallStreaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
MaxStreaksPerBatsman AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(current_consecutive_dot_balls) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
    FROM
        StreakLengths
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    MaxStreaksPerBatsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dot_balls DESC
LIMIT 1;

intent: Determine the frequency of boundaries (fours and sixes) hit by each batsman immediately after facing a dot ball.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls, then use a window function (LAG) to check the delivery immediately following a dot ball, and finally group by batsman to count subsequent boundaries.
sql:
WITH BatsmanDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS batsman_delivery_seq,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
    FROM df
),
DotBallOccurrences AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_delivery_seq AS dot_seq
    FROM
        BatsmanDeliveries
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
)
SELECT
    db.batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bd.is_boundary = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS boundaries_after_dot_ball
FROM
    DotBallOccurrences db
JOIN
    BatsmanDeliveries bd ON db.batsman = bd.batsman
                         AND bd.batsman_delivery_seq > db.dot_seq
                         AND (bd.batsman_delivery_seq - db.dot_seq) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
GROUP BY
    db.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN bd.is_boundary = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    boundaries_after_dot_ball DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate using conditional aggregation and division. Group by batsman. Use CASE for death over filtering.
sql:
WITH MatchStats AS (
    SELECT
        MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_number
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    COALESCE(SUM(d.batsman_runs) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced), 0), 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
    COALESCE(
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (ms.max_over_number - 2) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0
        / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (ms.max_over_number - 2) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0),
        0
    ) AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM
    df AS d
CROSS JOIN
    MatchStats AS ms
GROUP BY
    d.batsman;

intent: Calculate the conversion rate of dot balls to wickets for each bowler.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls and then join to find wickets on the subsequent ball. Group by bowler and calculate the ratio of wickets following dot balls to total dot balls.
sql:
WITH BowlerStats AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        LEAD(bowler_wickets, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS next_ball_wicket_status
    FROM
        df
),
CalculatedRates AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND next_ball_wicket_status = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dot_balls_followed_by_wicket,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_dot_balls_bowled
    FROM
        BowlerStats
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CAST(dot_balls_followed_by_wicket AS REAL) * 100.0 / total_dot_balls_bowled AS dot_to_wicket_conversion_rate
FROM
    CalculatedRates
WHERE
    total_dot_balls_bowled >= 1;

intent: Understand batsman's early aggression by comparing their strike rate in the powerplay (first 6 overs) to the rest of the innings.

intent: Analyze batsman's boundary hitting efficiency by looking at the number of boundaries (4s and 6s) per ball faced in different phases of the innings.
structure: Uses CASE expressions with CEIL(overs) to define three phases: Powerplay (1-6), Middle Overs (7-15), Death Overs (16+). It then calculates the sum of boundaries and balls faced for each phase and computes the boundary rate.
sql:
SELECT batsman,

intent: Determine the maximum consecutive dot balls faced by each batsman.
structure: Use window functions (LAG) to identify consecutive dot balls. Use a subquery and window function (SUM over partition) to count streaks. Group by batsman to find the maximum streak.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS global_ball_id, -- Assign a stable global order. Assumes a natural chronological order in df.
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
batsman_innings_seq AS (
    SELECT
        global_ball_id,
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Flag a new innings start for each batsman
        CASE
            WHEN LAG(batsman, 1, '') OVER (ORDER BY global_ball_id) <> batsman THEN 1 -- New batsman implies new context/innings
            WHEN LAG(overs, 1, 0.0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY global_ball_id) >= overs THEN 1 -- Overs reset or decreased (e.g. 0.6 -> 0.1 for same batsman)
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_new_innings_flag
    FROM
        numbered_balls
),
assigned_innings AS (
    SELECT
        global_ball_id,
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        -- Accumulate the innings flags to get a unique innings ID for each batsman
        SUM(is_new_innings_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY global_ball_id) AS batsman_innings_id
    FROM
        batsman_innings_seq
),
grouped_dots AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_innings_id,
        is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, batsman_innings_id ORDER BY global_ball_id) - 
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, batsman_innings_id, is_dot_ball ORDER BY global_ball_id) AS group_identifier
    FROM
        assigned_innings
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(consecutive_dot_balls) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_innings_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls
    FROM
        grouped_dots
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        batsman_innings_id,
        group_identifier
) AS subquery_consecutive_counts
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dot_balls DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of runs scored by a specific batsman on the ball immediately following a dot ball they faced.
structure: Use CTEs to first identify dot balls for a given batsman and then use the LEAD window function to find runs on the subsequent ball. Finally, calculate the average of these subsequent runs, grouped by batsman.
sql:
WITH lagged_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_ball_batsman_runs
  FROM df
),
dot_ball_followers AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs, -- These are the runs scored on the ball immediately after a dot ball
    CASE WHEN prev_ball_batsman_runs = 0 AND batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_scored_after_dot_flag
  FROM lagged_runs
  WHERE prev_ball_batsman_runs = 0 -- Filter to get only balls that immediately follow a dot ball
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(batsman_runs) AS avg_runs_after_dot_ball
FROM dot_ball_followers
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(has_scored_after_dot_flag) >= 1 -- Ensure batsman had at least one instance of scoring runs after a dot ball
ORDER BY avg_runs_after_dot_ball DESC;

structure: Use CASE expressions to split the innings into two phases: 'first 10 overs' and 'rest of innings'. Calculate strike rates for each phase using conditional aggregation. Join the results for the same batsman to calculate the difference.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs' ELSE 'Rest of Innings' END AS phase,

intent: Identify batsmen who are most effective at scoring boundaries immediately after facing a dot ball.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls faced by each batsman. Then, using a subsequent CTE and the LEAD window function, find the runs scored on the ball after a dot ball. Finally, filter for boundaries and calculate the count, grouping by batsman.
sql:
WITH LaggedData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
),
BoundariesAfterDot AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS boundaries_after_dot_ball
    FROM
        LaggedData
    WHERE
        prev_batsman_runs = 0 -- The previous ball was a dot ball for the same batsman
        AND (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) -- The current ball is a boundary
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    boundaries_after_dot_ball
FROM
    BoundariesAfterDot
WHERE
    boundaries_after_dot_ball > 0 -- Only include batsmen who have hit at least one boundary after facing a dot ball
ORDER BY
    boundaries_after_dot_ball DESC;

structure: Use a CTE to identify death overs. Calculate the sum of runs given by each bowler in death overs. Divide by the number of death overs bowled by that bowler. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH MatchMaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(FLOOR(overs)) AS max_over_num
    FROM df
),
DeathOversData AS (
    SELECT
        d.bowler,
        d.bowler_runs_given
    FROM
        df AS d
    CROSS JOIN MatchMaxOver mmo
    WHERE
        FLOOR(d.overs) >= (mmo.max_over_num - 4)
),
BowlerDeathStats AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded,
        COUNT(*) AS total_balls_bowled
    FROM
        DeathOversData
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
        WHEN total_balls_bowled = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE CAST(total_runs_conceded AS REAL) / (total_balls_bowled / 6.0)
    END AS avg_runs_conceded_per_death_over
FROM
    BowlerDeathStats;

structure: Calculate strike rate for two phases (first 6 overs and last 2 overs) for each batsman. This involves conditional aggregation within CASE statements and grouping by batsman. It will require CTEs for clarity.
sql:
WITH PhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_in_early_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_in_early_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_in_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_in_death_overs
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN balls_in_early_overs > 0 THEN CAST(runs_in_early_overs AS REAL) * 100 / balls_in_early_overs ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_early_overs,
  CASE WHEN balls_in_death_overs > 0 THEN CAST(runs_in_death_overs AS REAL) * 100 / balls_in_death_overs ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM PhaseStats
WHERE balls_in_early_overs > 0 OR balls_in_death_overs > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Determine the longest streak of dot balls faced by a batsman before getting dismissed or scoring any runs.
structure: This involves identifying dot balls, using a window function to count consecutive dot balls, and then finding the maximum of these streaks. CTEs will be used to break down the logic.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_batsman_ball_seq,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
streak_groups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn_batsman_ball_seq - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM
        numbered_balls
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM
        streak_groups
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
),
longest_streaks_per_batsman AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(current_streak_length) AS longest_dot_ball_streak_raw
    FROM
        streaks
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    COALESCE(ls.longest_dot_ball_streak_raw, 0) AS longest_dot_ball_streak
FROM
    (SELECT DISTINCT batsman FROM df) AS d
LEFT JOIN
    longest_streaks_per_batsman AS ls ON d.batsman = ls.batsman
ORDER BY
    longest_dot_ball_streak DESC, d.batsman;
