intent: Calculate the highest number of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman.
structure: Use a window function to assign a group number to consecutive dot balls for each batsman. Filter for dot balls. Group by batsman and the consecutive dot ball group number, count the balls in each group, and find the maximum count per batsman.
sql:
WITH BallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball_flag,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_batsman_delivery,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, (CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY overs) AS rn_batsman_delivery_type
    FROM df
),
ConsecutiveBlocks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball_flag,
        (rn_batsman_delivery - rn_batsman_delivery_type) AS block_id
    FROM BallSequence
),
DotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        block_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dot_balls_count
    FROM ConsecutiveBlocks
    WHERE is_dot_ball_flag = 1
    GROUP BY batsman, block_id
),
RankedDotBallCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        consecutive_dot_balls_count,
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY consecutive_dot_balls_count DESC) as rnk
    FROM DotBallCounts
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    consecutive_dot_balls_count AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM RankedDotBallCounts
WHERE rnk = 1;

structure: Use CASE expressions to define three phases based on CEIL(overs). Group by bowler and phase. Calculate runs conceded and balls bowled for each phase. Compute economy rate for each phase.
sql: SELECT bowler, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_powerplay, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS balls_powerplay, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ELSE NULL END AS economy_powerplay, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_middle, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS balls_middle, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ELSE NULL END AS economy_middle, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_death, SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS balls_death, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ELSE NULL END AS economy_death FROM df GROUP BY bowler HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY economy_death ASC

intent: Determine the overall strike rate of each batsman and compare it to their strike rate in the first over.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate overall strike rate and first-over strike rate for each batsman. Join the CTEs. Handle cases where a batsman might not have faced a ball in the first over.
sql:
WITH overall_sr AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS overall_strike_rate
  FROM df
  WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
  GROUP BY batsman
),
first_over_sr AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS first_over_strike_rate
  FROM df
  WHERE ceil(overs) = 1 AND batsman_bowls_faced > 0
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  os.batsman,
  os.overall_strike_rate,
  COALESCE(fos.first_over_strike_rate, 0) AS first_over_strike_rate
FROM overall_sr AS os
LEFT JOIN first_over_sr AS fos
  ON os.batsman = fos.batsman
ORDER BY os.overall_strike_rate DESC;

sql:

intent: Analyze the bowler's efficiency by calculating their runs conceded per wicket taken across different phases of the innings.
structure: Grouping by bowler, calculating average runs conceded per wicket for each phase (defined by CEIL(overs)). Uses CASE statements for phase definition and CTEs for intermediate calculations. Aggregations: SUM for runs/wickets, COUNT for balls, ratio for runs per wicket.
sql:
WITH PhaseRuns AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs_given,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS middle_overs_runs_given,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_runs_given
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler
),
PhaseWickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_wickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS middle_overs_wickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 15 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_wickets
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT
  pr.bowler,
  CASE WHEN pw.powerplay_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(pr.powerplay_runs_given AS REAL) / pw.powerplay_wickets ELSE NULL END AS runs_per_wicket_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN pw.middle_overs_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(pr.middle_overs_runs_given AS REAL) / pw.middle_overs_wickets ELSE NULL END AS runs_per_wicket_middle_overs,
  CASE WHEN pw.death_overs_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(pr.death_overs_runs_given AS REAL) / pw.death_overs_wickets ELSE NULL END AS runs_per_wicket_death_overs
FROM PhaseRuns pr
JOIN PhaseWickets pw ON pr.bowler = pw.bowler
WHERE pw.powerplay_wickets > 0 OR pw.middle_overs_wickets > 0 OR pw.death_overs_wickets > 0
ORDER BY runs_per_wicket_death_overs DESC NULLS LAST;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen immediately following a dot ball delivery, to assess their ability to rotate strike or attack after a defensive shot.
structure: Uses a CTE to identify dot balls, then joins back to the main table to find the next delivery's stats. Groups by batsman and calculates strike rate using SUM for runs and balls. Uses a subquery to define the 'next' ball based on `overs` ordering.
sql:
WITH LaggedData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        overs,
        LAG(batsman_runs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_batsman_runs,
        LAG(overs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_overs
    FROM
        df
),
FilteredDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced
    FROM
        LaggedData
    WHERE
        prev_batsman_runs = 0 -- The previous ball faced by the same batsman was a dot ball
        AND (overs - prev_overs) <= 0.2 -- And the current ball is within 0.2 overs of that previous ball
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CAST(batsman_runs AS REAL)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate_after_dot
FROM
    FilteredDeliveries
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 -- Ensure at least one ball was faced after a dot ball
ORDER BY
    strike_rate_after_dot DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of a specific batsman across all their innings, with a focus on their performance in the very first over of any innings they played.
structure: Uses CTEs to calculate overall strike rate and first-over strike rate separately, then joins them. Employs CASE expressions within aggregations. Uses a placeholder for the batsman's name.
sql:
WITH OverallSR AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate
  FROM df
  WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
  GROUP BY batsman
),
FirstOverSR AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS first_over_strike_rate
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) = 1 AND batsman_bowls_faced > 0
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  osr.batsman,
  osr.overall_strike_rate,
  COALESCE(fosr.first_over_strike_rate, 0) AS first_over_strike_rate
FROM OverallSR osr
LEFT JOIN FirstOverSR fosr ON osr.batsman = fosr.batsman
WHERE osr.batsman = 'Head'
ORDER BY osr.overall_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the momentum shift by comparing the batsman's strike rate in overs where they scored boundaries versus overs where they did not.
structure: Grouping by batsman. Uses CASE expressions to differentiate overs with boundaries vs. no boundaries. Calculates strike rate for each category using SUM for runs and balls. Aggregations: SUM, ratio.
sql:
WITH BatsmanOverBoundaryStatus AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
        MAX(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_boundary_in_over
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs)
)
SELECT
    df.batsman,
    COALESCE(
        SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 1 THEN df.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 /
        NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 1 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0),
        0
    ) AS strike_rate_boundary_overs,
    COALESCE(
        SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 0 THEN df.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 /
        NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 0 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0),
        0
    ) AS strike_rate_non_boundary_overs
FROM
    df
JOIN
    BatsmanOverBoundaryStatus bs ON df.batsman = bs.batsman AND CEIL(df.overs) = bs.over_number
GROUP BY
    df.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 1 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    OR SUM(CASE WHEN bs.has_boundary_in_over = 0 THEN df.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    df.batsman;

intent: Examine the streak of consecutive dot balls faced by batsmen, to identify those who struggle to break periods of pressure.
structure: Uses CTEs to first identify dot balls, then uses a window function (SUM with PARTITION BY) to group consecutive dot balls. Finally, counts the occurrences within each streak group.
sql:
WITH batsman_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        LAG(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot_ball
    FROM df
),
streak_identification AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 AND prev_is_dot_ball = 0 THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
    FROM batsman_balls
    WHERE is_dot_ball = 1
),
streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group,
        COUNT(*) AS current_streak_length
    FROM streak_identification
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(current_streak_length) AS max_consecutive_dots
FROM streak_lengths
GROUP BY
    batsman
ORDER BY
    max_consecutive_dots DESC
LIMIT 10

intent: Compare the strike rate of the top 5 run-scoring batsmen against the bowlers who conceded the most runs overall.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify top batsmen and most expensive bowlers. Then calculates strike rate for each batsman against each of those bowlers. Aggregations: SUM, ratio. Uses subqueries and filtering.
sql:
WITH TopBatsmen AS (
  SELECT batsman
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman
  ORDER BY SUM(batsman_runs) DESC
  LIMIT 5
),
MostExpensiveBowlers AS (
  SELECT bowler
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler
  ORDER BY SUM(bowler_runs_given) DESC
  LIMIT 5
)
SELECT
  d.batsman,
  d.bowler,
  CASE WHEN SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate
FROM df AS d
WHERE d.batsman IN (SELECT batsman FROM TopBatsmen)
  AND d.bowler IN (SELECT bowler FROM MostExpensiveBowlers)
GROUP BY d.batsman, d.bowler
ORDER BY d.batsman, strike_rate DESC;

intent: Determine the maximum number of consecutive dot balls faced by any batsman against a specific bowler.
structure: Use CTEs to identify dot balls and then to calculate consecutive dot ball streaks. Use window functions for streak grouping. Group by batsman and bowler. COUNT aggregation.
sql:
WITH LaggedDots AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        LAG(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, bowler ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
StreakStart AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        CASE WHEN is_dot_ball = 1 AND prev_is_dot_ball = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new_dot_streak_start
    FROM
        LaggedDots
),
GroupedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        overs,
        is_dot_ball,
        SUM(is_new_dot_streak_start) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, bowler ORDER BY overs) AS dot_streak_group_id
    FROM
        StreakStart
),
CalculatedStreaks AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        bowler,
        dot_streak_group_id,
        COUNT(overs) AS consecutive_dots

sql:
WITH wicket_deliveries AS (
  SELECT bowler, overs FROM df WHERE bowler_wickets > 0
),
subsequent_runs AS (
  SELECT wd.bowler, df.bowler_runs_given
  FROM wicket_deliveries wd
  JOIN df ON wd.bowler = df.bowler AND df.overs > wd.overs AND df.overs < wd.overs + 0.4 -- Assuming max 6 balls per over, 0.4 is approx 3 balls
  WHERE df.overs <= wd.overs + 0.3
)
SELECT wd.bowler, AVG(sr.bowler_runs_given) AS avg_runs_after_wicket
FROM wicket_deliveries wd
JOIN subsequent_runs sr ON wd.bowler = sr.bowler
GROUP BY wd.bowler
HAVING COUNT(sr.bowler_runs_given) >= 1 -- Ensure there was at least one ball after wicket
ORDER BY avg_runs_after_wicket ASC;

intent: Determine the maximum number of consecutive dot balls any batsman has faced in the match.
structure: Identify dot balls. Use a window function to create groups of consecutive dot balls. Count the balls in each group. Find the maximum count per batsman.
sql:
WITH numbered_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn_overall
    FROM
        df
),
grouped_dot_balls AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn_overall - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS group_id
    FROM
        numbered_balls
),
consecutive_dot_counts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        group_id,
        COUNT(*) AS current_consecutive_count
    FROM
        grouped_dot_balls
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        group_id
)
SELECT
    T1.batsman,
    COALESCE(MAX(T2.current_consecutive_count), 0) AS max_consecutive_dot_balls
FROM
    df AS T1
LEFT JOIN
    consecutive_dot_counts AS T2
ON
    T1.batsman = T2.batsman
GROUP BY
    T1.batsman;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen immediately after they have hit a six.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate the strike rate using SUM(batsman_runs) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced), using a CASE statement to identify balls where a six was hit, and filter for batsmen who have hit at least one six.
sql:
WITH BatsmenHittingSixes AS (
    -- First, identify all unique batsmen who have hit at least one six in the entire dataset.
    SELECT DISTINCT batsman
    FROM df
    WHERE batsman_sixes > 0
),
DeliveriesWithPrevSixFlag AS (
    -- For each delivery, determine if the immediately preceding delivery for the same batsman was a six.
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        LAG(batsman_sixes, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_delivery_batsman_sixes
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    da.batsman,
    -- Calculate strike rate: total runs scored after a six divided by total balls faced after a six, multiplied by 100.
    -- Use NULLIF to prevent division by zero; if total balls faced is 0, the strike rate will be NULL.
    (SUM(da.batsman_runs) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(da.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate_after_six
FROM DeliveriesWithPrevSixFlag AS da
INNER JOIN BatsmenHittingSixes AS bhs
    ON da.batsman = bhs.batsman
WHERE
    da.prev_delivery_batsman_sixes > 0 -- Only consider deliveries that followed a six
GROUP BY
    da.batsman
ORDER BY
    strike_rate_after_six DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a bowler bowls before conceding their first wicket in the match.
structure: Use a CTE to find the first wicket for each bowler. Join back to the main table to count balls bowled up to that point. Calculate the average.
sql:
WITH first_wicket AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    MIN(overs) AS first_wicket_over
  FROM df
  WHERE
    bowler_wickets > 0
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  fw.bowler,
  AVG(df.bowler_bowls_done) AS avg_balls_before_first_wicket
FROM df
JOIN first_wicket AS fw
  ON df.bowler = fw.bowler AND df.overs >= fw.first_wicket_over
GROUP BY
  fw.bowler
HAVING
  COUNT(df.overs) > 0
ORDER BY
  avg_balls_before_first_wicket;

intent: Compare the strike rate of a batsman in the first 6 overs versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use CASE statement to differentiate between first 6 overs and rest. Group by batsman. Calculate strike rates for both conditions using conditional aggregation.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_first_6_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Analyze the performance variation of bowlers across different phases of an innings. Specifically, calculate the strike rate (runs conceded per wicket taken) for each bowler in the early (first 6 overs) and late (last 6 overs) stages of the innings.
structure: Use CTEs to define early and late phases. Group by bowler. Calculate the sum of runs conceded and wickets taken for each phase. Calculate strike rate as runs/wickets for each phase. Output bowler, early_phase_strike_rate, and late_phase_strike_rate.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6 THEN 'Late'
      ELSE 'Middle'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_given,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    phase
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_runs_given ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS early_phase_strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_runs_given ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS late_phase_strike_rate
FROM phase_stats
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN total_wickets ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by looking at their run-scoring rate in the first 3 balls versus the rest of the over. This query calculates the average runs scored per ball in the first three deliveries and the remaining deliveries of an over for each batsman.
structure: Use CASE expressions to differentiate between the first 3 balls and the rest of the over within each CEIL(overs). Calculate average batsman_runs for both segments. Group by batsman and CEIL(overs).
sql:
WITH OverDetails AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
        CAST((overs - FLOOR(overs)) * 10 AS INTEGER) AS ball_in_over,
        batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    over_number,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ball_in_over <= 3 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN ball_in_over <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_first_3_balls,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ball_in_over > 3 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN ball_in_over > 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_rest_of_over
FROM
    OverDetails
GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
ORDER BY
    batsman,
    over_number;

intent: Identify bowlers who are more or less effective in taking wickets during the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall wicket-taking ability.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate overall wickets per bowler and wickets per bowler in death overs. Calculate the ratio of death over wickets to overall wickets. Define death overs using CEIL(overs).
sql:
WITH overall_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets
  FROM
    df
  GROUP BY
    bowler
),
death_over_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS death_wickets
  FROM
    df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  ow.bowler,
  CAST(COALESCE(d.death_wickets, 0) AS REAL) / ow.total_wickets AS death_over_wicket_ratio
FROM
  overall_wickets AS ow
LEFT JOIN
  death_over_wickets AS d
ON
  ow.bowler = d.bowler
WHERE
  ow.total_wickets > 0
ORDER BY
  death_over_wicket_ratio DESC;

intent: Analyze the boundary concession rate (fours and sixes) by bowlers in the death overs.
structure: Filter for death overs (last 5 overs). Calculate the total boundaries conceded (fours + sixes) by each bowler. Divide by the total balls bowled by the bowler in death overs to get the rate. Define death overs using CEIL(overs).
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  CAST(SUM(batsman_fours + batsman_sixes) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS death_over_boundary_concession_rate
FROM
  df
WHERE
  CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(bowler_bowls_done) > 0
ORDER BY
  death_over_boundary_concession_rate DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a bowler bowls before conceding their first run.
structure: Use a CTE to find the first instance where bowler_runs_given > 0 for each bowler. Then, calculate the number of balls bowled before that instance for each bowler. Order results by the average balls before conceding runs.
sql:
WITH BowlerFirstRunDelivery AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        MIN(overs) AS first_run_overs
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        bowler_runs_given > 0
    GROUP BY
        bowler
)
SELECT
    d.bowler,
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN bfrd.first_run_overs IS NULL THEN d.bowler_bowls_done -- If bowler never conceded a run, count all their balls
        WHEN d.overs < bfrd.first_run_overs THEN d.bowler_bowls_done -- Count balls before their first run-conceding delivery
        ELSE 0
    END) AS avg_balls_before_first_run
FROM
    df AS d
LEFT JOIN
    BowlerFirstRunDelivery AS bfrd
ON
    d.bowler = bfrd.bowler
GROUP BY
    d.bowler
ORDER BY
    avg_balls_before_first_run DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen during the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Use a CTE to calculate death over stats (runs, balls) and overall stats. Then join them and calculate strike rates. Group by batsman. Uses CASE expressions for phase definition and CTE.
sql:
WITH 
  over_stats AS (
    SELECT 
      batsman,
      SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_runs,
      SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS death_balls,
      SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
      SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
    FROM df
    GROUP BY batsman
  )
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN death_balls > 0 THEN CAST(death_runs AS REAL) * 100 / death_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs,
  CASE WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_overall
FROM over_stats
WHERE death_balls > 0 OR total_balls > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Calculate the cumulative number of dot balls faced by each batsman over the course of the match, over the sequence of deliveries.
structure: Use a CTE to mark dot balls and then a window function for cumulative sum. Order by over number to show progression. Uses CTE and window functions.
sql:
WITH dot_balls AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  overs,
  SUM(is_dot_ball) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS cumulative_dot_balls
FROM dot_balls
ORDER BY batsman, overs;

SELECT

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a batsman faces before hitting their first boundary (four or six) within the first 10 overs.
structure: Use CTE to find the minimum over where each batsman hits a boundary. Join back to the main table to count balls faced before that over for each batsman. Use AVG to find the average balls faced before first boundary.
sql:
WITH first_boundary AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    MIN(overs) AS first_boundary_over
  FROM df
  WHERE
    batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
    AND CEIL(overs) <= 10
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  d.batsman,
  AVG(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS avg_balls_before_first_boundary_in_10_overs
FROM df AS d
JOIN first_boundary AS fb ON d.batsman = fb.batsman AND d.overs < fb.first_boundary_over
GROUP BY d.batsman
HAVING COUNT(d.overs) > 0
ORDER BY avg_balls_before_first_boundary_in_10_overs;

question: For each batsman, what is the average number of balls they faced before hitting their first boundary (four or six) within the first 10 overs?   CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6)

    ELSE 0

    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_late_overs
FROM df
WHERE
  batsman_bowls_faced > 0

  batsman

intent: Calculate the strike rate for a specific batsman when scoring boundaries (4s and 6s) versus when scoring other runs (1s, 2s, 3s).
structure: Uses CASE statements to differentiate between boundary runs and other runs. Calculates strike rate for each category by dividing total runs by total balls faced. Uses conditional aggregation.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_fours) + SUM(batsman_sixes) > 0 AND SUM(batsman_runs) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) * 100
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_on_boundaries,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_runs) - (SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END)) > 0 AND SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) - SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours = 0 AND batsman_sixes = 0 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours = 0 AND batsman_sixes = 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) * 100
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_on_non_boundaries
FROM df
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY

structure: Uses CTE to define death overs and non-death overs. Calculates wickets for each category per bowler. Compares wickets in death overs vs. non-death overs.
sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_innings_over FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_innings_over - 5) THEN d.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_death_overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_innings_over - 5) THEN d.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_other_overs,
    CASE
        WHEN SUM(d.bowler_wickets) = 0 THEN 0.0
        ELSE CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_innings_over - 5) THEN d.bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(d.bowler_wickets)
    END AS proportion_wickets_in_death_overs
FROM
    df AS d
CROSS JOIN
    MaxOver AS mo
GROUP BY
    d.bowler
ORDER BY
    proportion_wickets_in_death_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the average number of balls a batsman faces before hitting their first boundary (a four or a six) within the first 10 overs. This helps understand how quickly batsmen tend to start attacking.
structure: This query involves a CTE to identify the over of the first boundary for each batsman in the first 10 overs. Then, it joins back to the main table to count the balls faced by each batsman before their first boundary within that initial phase and calculates the average. It groups by batsman and orders by the average balls faced.
sql:
WITH FilteredDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) AS is_boundary,
        LAG(batsman, 1, '') OVER (ORDER BY overs, bowler_bowls_done) AS prev_batsman,
        LAG(overs, 1, 0.0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs, bowler_bowls_done) AS prev_batsman_overs_for_same_batsman
    FROM df
    WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10
),
BatsmanAppearances AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        is_boundary,
        -- Detect start of a new 'appearance' (simulated innings) for a batsman
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN prev_batsman = '' THEN 1 -- First ball in the filtered dataset (covers first row case)
            WHEN batsman != prev_batsman THEN 1 -- Batsman changed from previous ball
            WHEN overs < prev_batsman_overs_for_same_batsman THEN 1 -- Overs reset for the same batsman (implies new innings/match)
            ELSE 0
        END) OVER (ORDER BY overs, bowler_bowls_done) AS appearance_marker
    FROM FilteredDeliveries
),
RankedAppearances AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        is_boundary,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY appearance_marker) AS batsman_appearance_id
    FROM BatsmanAppearances
),
BallsFacedInAppearance AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_appearance_id,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        is_boundary,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, batsman_appearance_id ORDER BY overs, bowler_bowls_done) AS balls_faced_cumulative
    FROM RankedAppearances
),
FirstBoundaryPerAppearance AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_appearance_id,
        MIN(balls_faced_cumulative) AS first_boundary_ball_num
    FROM BallsFacedInAppearance
    WHERE is_boundary = TRUE
    GROUP BY batsman, batsman_appearance_id
)
SELECT
    fbp.batsman,
    AVG(fbp.first_boundary_ball_num - 1) AS avg_balls_before_first_boundary
FROM FirstBoundaryPerAppearance AS fbp
GROUP BY fbp.batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_before_first_boundary;

SELECT

  AVG(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN CAST(batsman_runs AS REAL) ELSE NULL END) AS strike_rate_middle_overs
FROM df
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
  OR SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0

WITH bowler_wicket_counts AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_death_overs

intent: Examine the bowling performance of a specific bowler by calculating their wickets taken and runs conceded across different phases of the innings (e.g., early, middle, late).
structure: Use a CTE to define innings phases based on CEIL(overs). Then, group by bowler and phase, summing wickets and runs conceded. Finally, calculate a wickets-per-run ratio or similar efficiency metric.
sql:
WITH OverPhases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    bowler_runs_given,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM
    df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
  SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(bowler_runs_given) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_wickets) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_runs_given)
    ELSE 0
  END AS wickets_per_run_ratio
FROM
  OverPhases
GROUP BY
  bowler,
  phase
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN 1
    WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN 2
    WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN 3
  END;

intent: Compare the run-scoring efficiency (runs per ball) of batsmen in the first half versus the second half of the total balls they faced in the match.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate cumulative balls faced and total balls faced per batsman. Then, partition the data into first and second halves based on cumulative balls faced and calculate the average runs per ball for each half.
sql:
WITH BallCounts AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    -- Calculate the cumulative sum of 'balls faced' for each batsman, ordered by 'overs'.
    -- This defines the sequence of actual balls faced, ignoring deliveries where batsman_bowls_faced is 0.
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS cumulative_balls_faced,
    -- Calculate the total 'balls faced' by each batsman in the entire match.
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM
    df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  -- Calculate average runs per ball for the first half of the batsman's innings
  SUM(CASE WHEN cumulative_balls_faced <= CEIL(total_balls_faced / 2.0) THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 /
  NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN cumulative_balls_faced <= CEIL(total_balls_faced / 2.0) THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_first_half,
  -- Calculate average runs per ball for the second half of the batsman's innings
  SUM(CASE WHEN cumulative_balls_faced > CEIL(total_balls_faced / 2.0) THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 /
  NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN cumulative_balls_faced > CEIL(total_balls_faced / 2.0) THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_second_half
FROM
  BallCounts
WHERE
  total_balls_faced > 0 -- Filter out batsmen who faced no balls, to avoid division by zero or NULL results for their entire entry
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  batsman;

intent: Calculate the proportion of deliveries by each bowler that resulted in a wicket across different phases of the innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Using CTEs to define phases based on CEIL(overs), group by bowler and phase, and calculate the ratio of wickets to total balls delivered in each phase. Uses CASE for bucketing and CTEs.
sql:
WITH delivery_phases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_wickets,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS wicket_per_ball_percentage
FROM delivery_phases
WHERE
  phase IS NOT NULL AND bowler_bowls_done > 0
GROUP BY
  bowler,
  phase
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Late' THEN 3 END;

intent: Identify bowlers who are particularly effective at picking up wickets in the death overs, relative to their overall wicket-taking ability.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate overall wickets and wickets in death overs (last X overs). Then, calculate a ratio or difference to highlight bowlers who are disproportionately successful in the death overs. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS death_over_wickets,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS balls_in_death_overs,
    COUNT(*) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  total_wickets,
  death_over_wickets,
  CASE
    WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_wickets AS REAL) / total_balls
    ELSE 0
  END AS overall_wicket_per_ball,
  CASE
    WHEN balls_in_death_overs > 0 THEN CAST(death_over_wickets AS REAL) / balls_in_death_overs
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_over_wicket_per_ball,
  CASE
    WHEN balls_in_death_overs > 0 THEN CAST(death_over_wickets AS REAL) / balls_in_death_overs - (CAST(total_wickets AS REAL) / total_balls)
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_over_wicket_advantage
FROM bowler_stats
WHERE
  total_balls > 0 AND balls_in_death_overs > 0
ORDER BY
  death_over_wicket_advantage DESC;

intent: Investigate the strike rate of batsmen in death overs (last 5 overs) versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Group by batsman. Use CASE statements to partition runs and balls faced into 'death overs' and 'rest of innings'. Calculate strike rates for each phase.
sql:
WITH MaxOvers AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_total_overs
    FROM df
),
BatsmanPhaseStats AS (
    SELECT
        d.batsman,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_total_overs - 5) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_death_overs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (mo.max_total_overs - 5) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_death_overs,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_total_overs - 5) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_rest_of_innings,
        SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= (mo.max_total_overs - 5) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_rest_of_innings
    FROM
        df d, MaxOvers mo
    WHERE d.batsman_bowls_faced > 0
    GROUP BY
        d.batsman
)
SELECT
    bps.batsman,
    (bps.runs_death_overs * 100.0 / NULLIF(bps.balls_death_overs, 0)) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
    (bps.runs_rest_of_innings * 100.0 / NULLIF(bps.balls_rest_of_innings, 0)) AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM
    BatsmanPhaseStats bps
WHERE
    bps.balls_death_overs > 0 AND bps.balls_rest_of_innings > 0
ORDER BY
    bps.batsman;

intent: Compare the average runs scored per over by a bowler in the first half versus the second half of the match.
structure: Uses CTEs to define match halves based on over number, then calculates the average runs per over for each half using conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH MatchOverLimit AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_number
  FROM df
),
BowlerHalfStats AS (
  SELECT
    df.bowler,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= (SELECT max_over_number FROM MatchOverLimit) / 2.0 THEN df.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_first_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) <= (SELECT max_over_number FROM MatchOverLimit) / 2.0 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) AS balls_first_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_number FROM MatchOverLimit) / 2.0 THEN df.bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS runs_second_half,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(df.overs) > (SELECT max_over_number FROM MatchOverLimit) / 2.0 THEN df.bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) AS balls_second_half
  FROM df
  GROUP BY df.bowler
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN balls_first_half > 0 THEN CAST(runs_first_half AS REAL) / (balls_first_half / 6.0)
    ELSE 0.0
  END AS avg_runs_per_over_first_half,
  CASE
    WHEN balls_second_half > 0 THEN CAST(runs_second_half AS REAL) / (balls_second_half / 6.0)
    ELSE 0.0
  END AS avg_runs_per_over_second_half
FROM BowlerHalfStats
ORDER BY bowler;

intent: Analyze the strike rate variation of batsmen across different phases of their innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Use a CASE expression to define three innings phases based on CEIL(overs). Group by batsman and phase. Calculate strike rate (total batsman runs / total batsman balls faced * 100) for each phase using SUM aggregation. Employ a CTE to define phases. Use a WIDE OUTPUT preference for the phases.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 5 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN CAST(batsman_runs AS REAL) / batsman_bowls_faced * 100 ELSE NULL END) AS strike_rate_early,
  AVG(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN CAST(batsman_runs AS REAL) / batsman_bowls_faced * 100 ELSE NULL END) AS strike_rate_middle,
  AVG(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN CAST(batsman_runs AS REAL) / batsman_bowls_faced * 100 ELSE NULL END) AS strike_rate_late
FROM phase_data
WHERE batsman_bowls_faced > 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY batsman;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by looking at their average runs scored per ball in the first half versus the second half of deliveries they faced in an innings.
structure: Use a CTE to calculate cumulative balls faced and total balls faced for each batsman. Partition by batsman and order by overs. sql:
WITH RankedBalls AS (

        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as ball_seq_num
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_bowls_faced > 0
),
BatsmanStats AS (
    SELECT
        r.batsman,
        r.overs,
        r.batsman_runs,
        r.batsman_bowls_faced,
        r.ball_seq_num,
        SUM(r.batsman_bowls_faced) OVER (PARTITION BY r.batsman) as total_balls_faced_for_batsman
    FROM
        RankedBalls r
),
FinalCalculations AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN ball_seq_num <= CEIL(total_balls_faced_for_batsman / 2.0) THEN batsman_runs
                ELSE 0
            END) as runs_first_half,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN ball_seq_num <= CEIL(total_balls_faced_for_batsman / 2.0) THEN batsman_bowls_faced
                ELSE 0
            END) as balls_first_half,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN ball_seq_num > CEIL(total_balls_faced_for_batsman / 2.0) THEN batsman_runs
                ELSE 0
            END) as runs_second_half,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN ball_seq_num > CEIL(total_balls_faced_for_batsman / 2.0) THEN batsman_bowls_faced
                ELSE 0
            END) as balls_second_half,
        MAX(total_balls_faced_for_batsman) as overall_total_balls_for_batsman
    FROM
        BatsmanStats
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    CAST(runs_first_half AS REAL) / NULLIF(balls_first_half, 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_first_half,
    CAST(runs_second_half AS REAL) / NULLIF(balls_second_half, 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_second_half
FROM
    FinalCalculations
WHERE
    overall_total_balls_for_batsman > 0;

intent: Analyze the batting strike rate in the first and last 10 overs of an innings.
structure: Use a CTE to define phases ('early' and 'late') based on CEIL(overs). Then, group by batsman and phase to calculate total runs and balls faced. Finally, calculate strike rate for each phase, displaying them in a wide format.
sql:
WITH batsman_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN 'early'
      ELSE 'late'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_early,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS balls_early,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_early,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_late,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS balls_late,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_late
FROM batsman_phases
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'late' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_late DESC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a bowler bowls before taking their first wicket.
structure: Use a CTE with a window function to find the cumulative balls bowled and identify the over number for the first wicket for each bowler. Then, calculate the average balls bowled before the first wicket.
sql:
WITH BowlerDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        bowler_wickets,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) as rn_delivery
    FROM df
    WHERE bowler IS NOT NULL
),
BowlerSpells AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        bowler_wickets,
        rn_delivery,
        -- Detect the start of a new spell: if the current `overs` value is less than or equal to the previous `overs` value
        -- for the same bowler (partitioned by bowler and ordered by delivery number), it signifies a reset (new innings/match).
        -- Also, the very first delivery for a bowler is a new spell.
        CASE
            WHEN LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY rn_delivery) IS NULL THEN 1
            WHEN overs <= LAG(overs) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY rn_delivery) THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS is_new_spell_start
    FROM BowlerDeliveries
),
NumberedSpells AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        overs,
        bowler_bowls_done,
        bowler_wickets,
        -- Assign a unique spell_id for each continuous bowling period for a bowler.
        -- This is done by summing the 'is_new_spell_start' flags.
        SUM(is_new_spell_start) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY rn_delivery) AS spell_id
    FROM BowlerSpells
),
FirstWicketInSpell AS (
    SELECT
        bowler,
        spell_id,
        -- Find the `overs` value of the first wicket taken within each identified spell.
        MIN(overs) AS first_wicket_overs
    FROM NumberedSpells
    WHERE bowler_wickets > 0
    GROUP BY bowler, spell_id
),
BallsToFirstWicket AS (
    SELECT
        ns.bowler,
        ns.spell_id,
        -- Sum 'bowler_bowls_done' (which usually counts as 1 ball) for all balls bowled
        -- up to and including the first wicket delivery in that specific spell.
        SUM(ns.bowler_bowls_done) AS balls_bowled_to_first_wicket
    FROM NumberedSpells ns
    JOIN FirstWicketInSpell fw
        ON ns.bowler = fw.bowler
        AND ns.spell_id = fw.spell_id
    WHERE ns.overs <= fw.first_wicket_overs -- Include the wicket-taking ball
    GROUP BY ns.bowler, ns.spell_id
    HAVING SUM(ns.bowler_bowls_done) > 0 -- Ensure at least one ball was bowled in the spell
)
SELECT
    bowler,
    -- Calculate the average of these 'balls_bowled_to_first_wicket' counts for each bowler
    -- across all their identified spells.
    AVG(balls_bowled_to_first_wicket * 1.0) AS avg_balls_until_first_wicket
FROM BallsToFirstWicket
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY avg_balls_until_first_wicket ASC;

intent: Analyze the trend of batsman strike rates across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Use CTEs to define innings phases based on CEIL(overs). Calculate total runs and total balls faced for each batsman within each phase. Compute strike rate (runs/balls) for each phase. Group by batsman and phase.
sql:
WITH phase_analysis AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY batsman, phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  CASE WHEN total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate
FROM phase_analysis
ORDER BY batsman, CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Late' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Calculate batting strike rates for two phases (death overs and rest of innings) using conditional aggregation within a CTE, then compare them. Group by batsman.
sql:
WITH phase_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Rest of Innings'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_strike_rates
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

WITH batsman_over_runs AS (

WITH over_bowler_stats AS (

  FROM df

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN wickets_in_over > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN wickets_in_over > 0 THEN runs_in_over ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN wickets_in_over > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

intent: Calculate the progression of a batsman's strike rate throughout the innings, comparing powerplay, middle overs, and death overs.
structure: Use CASE statements to define innings phases based on CEIL(overs). Group by batsman and phase. Calculate strike rate (runs/balls faced) for each phase.
sql:
SELECT

  CASE
    WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
    WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
    ELSE 'Death Overs'
  END AS phase,
  SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
  END AS strike_rate

intent: Analyze the momentum of scoring by batsmen, specifically looking at consecutive balls faced where runs were scored (excluding dot balls).
structure: Use a CTE to identify balls where runs were scored. Then use LAG to check for consecutive scoring balls. Finally, group by batsman and count streaks.
sql:
WITH batsman_deliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as delivery_seq_num
    FROM df
),
scoring_deliveries_with_group_id AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        delivery_seq_num,
        delivery_seq_num - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as streak_group_identifier
    FROM batsman_deliveries
    WHERE batsman_runs > 0
),
batsman_streak_lengths AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        streak_group_identifier,
        COUNT(*) AS streak_length
    FROM scoring_deliveries_with_group_id
    GROUP BY batsman, streak_group_identifier
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(streak_length) AS total_consecutive_scoring_deliveries
FROM batsman_streak_lengths
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY total_consecutive_scoring_deliveries DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall scoring rate.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate overall batsman_runs/batsman_bowls_faced and death_overs batsman_runs/batsman_bowls_faced using CASE for phase, compare the two rates.
sql:
WITH OverData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        CEIL(overs) AS current_over
    FROM df
),
MaxOver AS (
    SELECT
        MAX(current_over) AS max_innings_over
    FROM OverData
)
SELECT
    od.batsman,
    CAST(SUM(od.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(SUM(od.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN od.current_over >= (mo.max_innings_over - 4) THEN od.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 /
    NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN od.current_over >= (mo.max_innings_over - 4) THEN od.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM OverData AS od
CROSS JOIN MaxOver AS mo
GROUP BY od.batsman
HAVING SUM(od.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0

intent: Analyze the bowling performance by calculating the strike rate (average balls per wicket) for each bowler specifically in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: This query groups data by bowler, calculates the total wickets and total balls faced by each bowler in the death overs using a CASE expression on CEIL(overs), and then computes the strike rate as balls per wicket. It includes a HAVING clause to filter bowlers who have bowled a minimum number of balls in death overs. Window functions or CTEs are not used.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS death_over_balls,
  SUM(bowler_wickets) AS death_over_wickets,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_wickets)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM df
WHERE
  CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(bowler_bowls_done) >= 5
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_death_overs ASC;

intent: Examine the pressure a bowler exerts by looking at the proportion of dot balls they bowl in contrast to their total deliveries in different phases of the innings.
structure: Use CASE expressions to define innings phases (e.g., powerplay, middle overs, death overs). Group by bowler and phase. Count total balls and dot balls (where team_runs = 0). Calculate the dot ball percentage for each bowler in each phase.
sql:
WITH phase_bowler_stats AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE 
      WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(CASE WHEN team_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dot_balls,
    COUNT(*) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    phase
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  dot_balls,
  total_balls,
  CAST(dot_balls AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls AS dot_ball_percentage
FROM phase_bowler_stats
WHERE total_balls > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE phase
    WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Middle Overs' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Death Overs' THEN 3
  END;

intent: Assess the batting impact by identifying the proportion of a batsman's total runs that come from boundaries in the death overs.
structure: Filter for death overs (e.g., last 10 overs). Group by batsman. Calculate the sum of runs scored from boundaries (fours + sixes) and the sum of all runs scored by the batsman in these overs. Calculate the percentage.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) AS boundary_runs_death_overs,
  SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs_death_overs,
  (SUM(batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(batsman_runs), 0) AS boundary_percentage_death_overs
FROM df
WHERE
  CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER) > (SELECT MAX(CAST(CEIL(overs) AS INTEGER)) FROM df) - 10
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundary_percentage_death_overs DESC;

sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_off_bowler,

  CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_against_bowler
FROM df

  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0

structure: Group by bowler. Calculate total runs given by the bowler. Separately, calculate total runs given by the bowler specifically from boundaries (fours and sixes). Calculate the percentage of runs conceded as boundaries.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS total_runs_conceded,
  SUM(CASE WHEN df.batsman_fours > 0 OR df.batsman_sixes > 0 THEN df.team_runs ELSE 0 END) AS boundary_runs_conceded,
  CASE WHEN SUM(bowler_runs_given) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN df.batsman_fours > 0 OR df.batsman_sixes > 0 THEN df.team_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(bowler_runs_given) ELSE 0 END AS boundary_run_percentage
FROM df
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(bowler_runs_given) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundary_run_percentage DESC;

intent: Analyze the number of consecutive scoring deliveries faced by each batsman, considering only boundaries (fours and sixes) as scoring.
structure: Use a CTE to first identify 'scoring' deliveries (fours or sixes). Then, use a window function (lag) to determine consecutive scoring deliveries. Finally, count the streaks of consecutive scoring deliveries for each batsman.
sql:
WITH DeliveryFlags AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        (CASE WHEN (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_boundary
    FROM df
),
StreakIdentification AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_boundary,
        -- Determine if this delivery starts a new streak of boundaries
        -- A new streak starts if current is a boundary AND the previous delivery (for the same batsman) was NOT a boundary (or it's the first delivery).
        CASE
            WHEN is_boundary = 1 AND LAG(is_boundary, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END AS start_new_streak
    FROM DeliveryFlags
),
StreakGroups AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        is_boundary,
        -- Assign a unique ID for each continuous streak of boundaries.
        -- This ID increments whenever a 'start_new_streak' event occurs.
        SUM(start_new_streak) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group_id
    FROM StreakIdentification
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(consecutive_boundary_deliveries) AS consecutive_boundary_deliveries
FROM (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_boundary_deliveries
    FROM StreakGroups
    WHERE is_boundary = 1
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        streak_group_id
) AS StreakCounts
GROUP BY batsman
ORDER BY consecutive_boundary_deliveries DESC;

intent: Identify the top 5 batsmen who score the highest percentage of their runs through boundaries (4s and 6s) in the first 6 overs.
structure: Using a CTE to calculate boundary runs and total runs in the first 6 overs, then grouping by batsman and calculating the boundary percentage. Uses CTE and CASE expression.
sql:
WITH first_6_overs_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS boundary_runs,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6
  GROUP BY batsman
  HAVING SUM(batsman_runs) > 0
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CAST(boundary_runs AS REAL) * 100 / total_runs AS boundary_percentage
FROM first_6_overs_stats
ORDER BY boundary_percentage DESC
LIMIT 5;

intent: Calculate the number of maiden overs bowled by each bowler.
structure: Grouping by bowler and using a conditional aggregation (COUNT with CASE) to count overs where bowler_runs_given is 0.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE runs_in_over = 0) AS maiden_overs
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(team_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler, over_number
)
GROUP BY bowler
ORDER BY maiden_overs DESC;

intent: Calculate the proportion of wickets taken by a specific bowler in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their total wickets.
structure: Uses a subquery to find the maximum over, then aggregates wickets and runs given by bowler, with a CASE expression to distinguish death over wickets. Uses CTEs, CASE expressions, and subqueries.
sql:
WITH max_over AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) as max_over
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > max_over - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS death_over_wickets,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > max_over - 5 THEN bowler_wickets ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(bowler_wickets)
    ELSE 0
  END AS percentage_death_over_wickets
FROM df, max_over
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
ORDER BY percentage_death_over_wickets DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring variation by batsmen across different phases of the innings. Specifically, compare the average runs scored per ball faced by batsmen in the powerplay (first 6 overs) versus the death overs (last 6 overs).
structure: Use CTEs to define powerplay and death over stats for each batsman. Calculate runs per ball faced for each phase using SUM aggregations and CASE expressions. Join CTEs and perform final calculations, including a difference calculation.
sql:
WITH powerplay_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS pp_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS pp_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 6
  GROUP BY batsman
),
death_over_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_balls
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT 
  COALESCE(pp.batsman, d.batsman) AS batsman,
  CASE WHEN pp.pp_balls > 0 THEN CAST(pp.pp_runs AS REAL) * 100 / pp.pp_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE WHEN d.death_balls > 0 THEN CAST(d.death_runs AS REAL) * 100 / d.death_balls ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM powerplay_stats AS pp
FULL OUTER JOIN death_over_stats AS d ON pp.batsman = d.batsman
WHERE (pp.pp_balls > 0 OR d.death_balls > 0)

intent: Investigate the wicket-taking ability of bowlers during specific phases of the game. Calculate the wicket-per-run ratio for each bowler in the initial phase (first 10 overs) and compare it to their ratio in the middle phase (overs 11-15).
structure: Use CTEs to define stats for initial and middle phases per bowler. Calculate wickets and runs given per phase. Compute the wicket-run ratio using CASE for division by zero handling. Use CAST for float division.
sql:
WITH initial_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_initial,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_initial
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10
  GROUP BY bowler
),
middle_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_middle,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_middle
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15
  GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(i.bowler, m.bowler) AS bowler,
  CAST(i.wickets_initial AS REAL) * 1.0 / NULLIF(i.runs_initial, 0) AS wicket_run_ratio_initial,
  CAST(m.wickets_middle AS REAL) * 1.0 / NULLIF(m.runs_middle, 0) AS wicket_run_ratio_middle
FROM initial_phase AS i
FULL OUTER JOIN middle_phase AS m ON i.bowler = m.bowler;

intent: Compare the wicket-taking rate of bowlers in the death overs (last 6 overs) versus their overall career wicket-taking rate.
structure: Use CTEs to calculate death over wickets and runs, and overall wickets and runs. Calculate the wicket-per-run ratio for both phases. Handle division by zero.
sql:
WITH death_over_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS death_wickets,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS death_runs
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6
  GROUP BY bowler
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS overall_wickets,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS overall_runs
  FROM df
  GROUP BY bowler
)
SELECT 
  COALESCE(d.bowler, o.bowler) AS bowler,
  CAST(d.death_wickets AS REAL) / NULLIF(d.death_runs, 0) AS death_over_wicket_run_ratio,
  CAST(o.overall_wickets AS REAL) / NULLIF(o.overall_runs, 0) AS overall_wicket_run_ratio
FROM death_over_stats AS d
FULL OUTER JOIN overall_stats AS o ON d.bowler = o.bowler;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate for each batsman using CTEs and CASE statements for phase definition. Aggregate runs and balls faced per batsman for both phases. Compare the strike rates.
sql:
WITH batsman_phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS death_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(total_balls) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(total_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(total_balls) ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN SUM(death_balls) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(death_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(death_balls) ELSE 0 END AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM batsman_phase_stats
WHERE
  total_balls > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  overall_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by calculating the average runs scored on balls immediately following a boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use a window function to find the runs scored on the previous ball for each batsman. Filter for balls that followed a boundary and calculate the average runs scored on those subsequent balls.
sql:
WITH batsman_runs_lag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(batsman_runs) AS avg_runs_after_boundary
FROM batsman_runs_lag
WHERE
  previous_ball_runs IN (4, 6)
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_after_boundary DESC;

intent: Examine the trend of wickets taken by a bowler across consecutive overs.
structure: Use a window function to get the wickets taken in the previous over for each bowler. Filter for bowlers who took wickets and analyze the runs scored on balls following a wicket-taking over.
sql:
WITH bowler_over_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_number
),
lagged_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    over_number,
    wickets_in_over,
    LAG(wickets_in_over, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY over_number) AS previous_over_wickets
  FROM bowler_over_wickets
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  COUNT(*) AS overs_following_wicket_over
FROM lagged_wickets
WHERE
  previous_over_wickets > 0
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY

intent: Analyze the variation in batsman strike rate across different phases of an innings (powerplay, middle overs, death overs).
structure: Use CTEs to define phases based on CEIL(overs). Group by batsman and phase. Calculate strike rate (runs/balls) for each phase. Use CASE expressions for phase definition.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_balls,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS powerplay_strike_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS middle_overs_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS middle_overs_balls,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS middle_overs_strike_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_runs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) AS death_overs_balls,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phase_stats
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN total_balls ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  powerplay_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the momentum shift by comparing the average runs scored per over in the first half versus the second half of the innings.
structure: Use CASE expressions to divide overs into two halves. Group by batsman and the defined halves. Calculate the average runs scored per over. Use CTEs for phase definition.
sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
),
innings_halves AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    over_number,
    runs_in_over,
    CASE
      WHEN over_number <= (SELECT MAX(over_number) FROM (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS over_number FROM df)) / 2 THEN 'First Half'
      ELSE 'Second Half'
    END AS innings_half
  FROM over_runs
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'First Half' THEN runs_in_over ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_first_half,
  AVG(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'Second Half' THEN runs_in_over ELSE NULL END) AS avg_runs_second_half
FROM innings_halves
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  COUNT(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'First Half' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) > 0 AND COUNT(CASE WHEN innings_half = 'Second Half' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) > 0
ORDER BY
  (avg_runs_second_half - avg_runs_first_half) DESC;

intent: Calculate the longest streak of consecutive scoring shots (runs > 0) by any batsman.

WITH scoring_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_scoring_ball
  FROM df
),
streak_group AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_scoring_ball,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_scoring_ball = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS streak_id
  FROM scoring_balls
),
streak_lengths AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    streak_id,
    SUM(is_scoring_ball) AS streak_length
  FROM streak_group
  GROUP BY
    batsman,

)

  MAX(streak_length) AS longest_scoring_streak
FROM streak_lengths
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY

intent: Analyze the sequence of scoring shots by a batsman to identify consecutive boundary hitting streaks.

WITH ScoringBalls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,

    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball

),
ConsecutiveBoundaries AS (
  SELECT

    CASE

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death over strike rate for each batsman using CTEs and conditional aggregation. Group by batsman. Compare metrics.
sql:
WITH batsman_overall_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman
),
max_over_info AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num
  FROM df
),
death_over_stats AS (
  SELECT
    d.batsman,
    SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS death_runs,
    SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_balls
  FROM df AS d
  WHERE
    CEIL(d.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM max_over_info) - 5
  GROUP BY
    d.batsman
)
SELECT
  o.batsman,
  o.total_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(o.total_balls, 0) AS overall_strike_rate,
  d.death_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(d.death_balls, 0) AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM batsman_overall_stats AS o
INNER JOIN death_over_stats AS d
  ON o.batsman = d.batsman
WHERE
  o.total_balls > 0 AND d.death_balls > 0
ORDER BY
  o.batsman;

structure: Use CTEs to calculate total wickets and death over wickets for each bowler. The death overs are defined as the last 5 overs. Calculate the percentage of death over wickets out of total wickets. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH max_over AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over
  FROM df
),
death_over_wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS death_wickets
  FROM df
  CROSS JOIN max_over
  WHERE

  GROUP BY

),
total_wickets AS (
  SELECT

    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS total_wickets
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  coalesce(dw.bowler, tw.bowler) AS bowler,
  CASE WHEN tw.total_wickets > 0 THEN CAST(dw.death_wickets AS REAL) * 100 / tw.total_wickets ELSE 0 END AS percentage_death_over_wickets
FROM death_over_wickets AS dw
FULL OUTER JOIN total_wickets AS tw ON dw.bowler = tw.bowler
WHERE
  tw.total_wickets > 0
ORDER BY

intent: Calculate the wicket-run ratio for bowlers in the initial phase (first 6 overs) versus the middle phase (overs 7-15).
structure: Use CTEs to calculate wickets and runs given for each bowler in the initial phase and the middle phase. Then, join these CTEs to compute the wicket-run ratio for each phase. Group by bowler.
sql:
WITH initial_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_initial,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_initial
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) <= 6
  GROUP BY
    bowler
),
middle_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_middle,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_middle
  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(i.bowler, m.bowler) AS bowler,
  CASE WHEN i.runs_initial > 0 THEN CAST(i.wickets_initial AS REAL) / i.runs_initial ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_initial,
  CASE WHEN m.runs_middle > 0 THEN CAST(m.wickets_middle AS REAL) / m.runs_middle ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_middle
FROM initial_phase AS i
FULL OUTER JOIN middle_phase AS m ON i.bowler = m.bowler
WHERE
  i.runs_initial > 0 OR m.runs_middle > 0
ORDER BY
  bowler;

intent: Calculate the percentage of boundaries scored by a batsman in the first 10 overs, relative to their total runs in those overs.

sql:
WITH first_10_overs_stats AS (

    SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS boundary_runs,

  FROM df
  WHERE
    CEIL(overs) <= 10
  GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING

FROM first_10_overs_stats
ORDER BY
  boundary_percentage DESC
LIMIT 10;

intent: Analyze the batting momentum by calculating the average runs scored on deliveries immediately following a boundary (four or six).

sql:
WITH batsman_runs_lag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_runs
  FROM df
)

FROM batsman_runs_lag

intent: Compare the wicket-taking ability of bowlers in the first 6 overs versus the rest of the innings, expressed as wickets per run conceded.
structure: Uses two CTEs to calculate wickets and runs for the first 6 overs and the remaining overs separately. Then, performs a full outer join and calculates the wicket-to-run ratio for each phase. Aggregation is ratio.
sql:
WITH initial_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_initial,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_initial
  FROM df
  WHERE
    ceil(overs) <= 6
  GROUP BY
    bowler
),
late_phase AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    SUM(bowler_wickets) AS wickets_late,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_late
  FROM df
  WHERE
    ceil(overs) > 6
  GROUP BY
    bowler
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(i.bowler, l.bowler) AS bowler,
  CASE WHEN i.runs_initial > 0 THEN CAST(i.wickets_initial AS REAL) / i.runs_initial ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_initial,
  CASE WHEN l.runs_late > 0 THEN CAST(l.wickets_late AS REAL) / l.runs_late ELSE NULL END AS wicket_run_ratio_late
FROM initial_phase AS i
FULL OUTER JOIN late_phase AS l
  ON i.bowler = l.bowler
WHERE
  i.wickets_initial > 0 OR l.wickets_late > 0;

sql:
WITH first_ball_of_over AS (

intent: Analyze the distribution of dot balls across different phases of an innings for each batsman. This helps understand how batsmen perform under pressure or when settling in.
structure: Group by batsman and a phased over category (early, middle, late) derived from CEIL(overs). Calculate the count of dot balls (where batsman_runs = 0) and total balls faced within each phase. Then, compute the dot ball percentage for each batsman in each phase.
sql:
WITH BatsmanPhaseData AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball,
    batsman_bowls_faced
  FROM
    df
  WHERE
    batsman_bowls_faced > 0
),
BatsmanPhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(is_dot_ball) AS total_dot_balls,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM
    BatsmanPhaseData
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
),
QualifyingBatsmen AS (
  SELECT
    batsman
  FROM
    BatsmanPhaseStats
  WHERE total_balls_faced > 0 -- Ensure they actually faced balls in the phase for the phase to count
  GROUP BY
    batsman
  HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT phase) = 3
)
SELECT
  bps.batsman,
  bps.phase,
  CAST(bps.total_dot_balls AS REAL) * 100.0 / NULLIF(bps.total_balls_faced, 0) AS dot_ball_percentage
FROM
  BatsmanPhaseStats AS bps
JOIN
  QualifyingBatsmen AS qb
ON
  bps.batsman = qb.batsman
ORDER BY
  bps.batsman,
  CASE bps.phase
    WHEN 'Early' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Late' THEN 3
  END;

intent: Examine the scoring trend of batsmen within the first 10 overs of an innings, specifically looking at their boundary percentage (fours and sixes relative to balls faced). This helps identify aggressive starters.
structure: Filter the data for the first 10 overs (CEIL(overs) <= 10). Group by batsman and calculate the total boundaries hit and total balls faced. Compute the boundary percentage.

WITH first10overs AS (

  FROM df

batsmanboundaryruns AS (
