intent: Analyze the consistency of a batsman's strike rate across different phases of their innings, specifically comparing the first 5 overs to the rest of the match.
structure: Group by batsman and over phase (defined by CEIL(overs)). Calculate strike rate for each phase using conditional aggregation. Use CASE statement for over phases. Use CTE.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Early'
      ELSE 'Rest of Match'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_early,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_match
FROM over_phases
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_early DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs of the match).
structure: Filter for deliveries in the last 5 overs. Calculate average runs per ball for each batsman in this phase. Use CEIL(overs).
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS scoring_rate_death_overs
FROM df
WHERE
  CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY

structure: Define powerplay (first 6 overs) and death overs (last 5 overs) using CASE. Calculate wickets taken in each phase per bowler. Use CEIL(overs) and CASE.
sql:
SELECT

intent: Analyze the strike rate variation of batsmen during different phases of the match (first 10 overs vs. rest of the match).
structure: Use a CTE to define over phases based on CEIL(overs). Then, group by batsman and phase to calculate the strike rate (runs/balls faced) for each phase. Use CASE expressions within aggregation to differentiate between phases. Requires aggregation and CASE expressions.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'First 10 Overs'
      ELSE 'Rest of Match'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 
      CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_first_10_overs,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 
      CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_match
FROM over_phases
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'First 10 Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Match' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_first_10_overs DESC;

intent: Find the batsmen who score a boundary on balls immediately following a dot ball.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls and boundary balls. Then use a window function (LAG) to check the previous ball's status for each batsman. Finally, count the occurrences where a boundary follows a dot ball.
sql:
WITH delivery_flags AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary
  FROM df
),
consecutive_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    is_boundary,
    LAG(is_dot, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot
  FROM delivery_flags
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS boundaries_after_dot_count
FROM consecutive_balls
WHERE prev_is_dot = 1 AND is_boundary = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY boundaries_after_dot_count DESC;
description: Quantifies how often batsmen convert dot balls into boundaries on the very next delivery, indicating their ability to quickly shift momentum after a period of pressure. This query uses CTEs and a window function to track consecutive ball outcomes per batsman.

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a bowler bowls to take a wicket in the powerplay overs (first 10 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to filter for powerplay overs and identify wicket-taking deliveries. Then, group by bowler to count the total balls bowled and wickets taken in the powerplay. Calculate the average balls per wicket.
sql:
WITH powerplay_wickets AS (
  SELECT 
    bowler,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    bowler_wickets
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 10
)
SELECT 
  bowler,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_bowls_done) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_wickets)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS avg_balls_per_wicket_powerplay
FROM powerplay_wickets
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING SUM(bowler_wickets) > 0
ORDER BY avg_balls_per_wicket_powerplay ASC;

intent: Calculate the percentage of dot balls faced by batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Use a CTE to identify death overs. Then, within the death overs, calculate the total balls faced and the total dot balls faced by each batsman. Compute the percentage of dot balls.
sql:
WITH death_overs_data AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    batsman_runs
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN 
      CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS dot_ball_percentage_death_overs
FROM death_overs_data
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY dot_ball_percentage_death_overs DESC;

intent: Rank batsmen by their six-hitting efficiency (sixes per ball faced) in overs 1 to 6.
structure: Filter deliveries within the first 6 overs. Group by batsman and calculate the ratio of sixes to balls faced. Use a window function to rank them.
sql:
WITH first_six_overs AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_sixes,
    batsman_bowls_faced
  FROM df
  WHERE CEIL(overs) <= 1
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_sixes) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS six_per_ball_ratio,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_sixes) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END DESC) as rank_in_phase
FROM first_six_overs
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY rank_in_phase ASC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a batsman faces *after* hitting a six, to understand post-boundary pressure or momentum.
structure: Identify deliveries where a batsman hit a six. Use a window function (LEAD) to find the runs scored on subsequent deliveries for the same batsman. Calculate the average of these subsequent runs, grouping by batsman. Filter for batsmen who hit at least a certain number of sixes.
sql:
WITH SixDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_sixes,
        LEAD(batsman_runs) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS next_ball_runs
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        batsman_sixes = 1
),
BatsmanTotalSixes AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS total_sixes_hit
    FROM
        SixDeliveries
    GROUP BY
        batsman
    HAVING
        COUNT(*) >= 3
),
ValidSixFollowUps AS (
    SELECT
        sd.batsman,
        sd.next_ball_runs
    FROM
        SixDeliveries sd
    INNER JOIN
        BatsmanTotalSixes bts ON sd.batsman = bts.batsman
    WHERE
        sd.next_ball_runs IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    AVG(next_ball_runs) AS avg_runs_after_six
FROM
    ValidSixFollowUps
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    COUNT(next_ball_runs) > 2;

intent: Analyze the variation in batsman strike rate across different phases of an innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Use a CASE expression to define over phases based on CEIL(overs). Calculate strike rate (batsman_runs / batsman_bowls_faced) for each phase using conditional aggregation. Group by batsman and phase. Use a subquery to determine the total number of overs in the match for defining the 'late' phase.
sql: WITH BatsmanPhaseStats AS (SELECT batsman, CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early' WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 12 THEN 'Middle' ELSE 'Late' END AS phase, SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs, SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced FROM df GROUP BY batsman, CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early' WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 12 THEN 'Middle' ELSE 'Late' END), EligibleBatsmen AS (SELECT batsman FROM BatsmanPhaseStats WHERE total_balls_faced > 0 GROUP BY batsman HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT phase) = 3) SELECT bps.batsman, bps.phase, bps.total_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(bps.total_balls_faced, 0) AS strike_rate FROM BatsmanPhaseStats bps JOIN EligibleBatsmen eb ON bps.batsman = eb.batsman ORDER BY bps.batsman, CASE bps.phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Late' THEN 3 END;

intent: Determine the balls faced-to-runs scored ratio for batsmen who faced a certain minimum number of balls in the entire innings.
structure: Calculate the total runs scored and total balls faced by each batsman. Filter for batsmen who have faced more than a specified number of deliveries. Calculate the ratio and order the results.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS runs_per_ball
FROM df
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 10

intent: Compare the strike rate of a specific batsman in the initial overs versus the middle overs.
structure: Calculate the strike rate for a specified batsman, segmented into two phases: early overs (first 6) and middle overs (7-15). This requires a CASE expression for phase definition and grouping by batsman and phase.
sql:
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
    WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
    ELSE 'Late'
  END AS phase,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM df
WHERE
  batsman = 'Head' AND (CEIL(overs) <= 15)
GROUP BY
  batsman,
  phase
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;

intent: Identify the average number of balls a batsman takes to hit their first four.
structure: Use a CTE to find the delivery index of the first four for each batsman. Then, calculate the average difference in 'overs' between the first four and subsequent deliveries for each batsman. Window function with ROW_NUMBER() and subquery for min over.
sql:
WITH BatsmanFirstFourBall AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MIN(overs) AS first_four_overs_val
    FROM df
    WHERE batsman_fours > 0
    GROUP BY batsman
),
BallsFacedBeforeFirstFour AS (
    SELECT
        d.batsman,
        SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS balls_to_first_four
    FROM df AS d
    JOIN BatsmanFirstFourBall AS bffb
        ON d.batsman = bffb.batsman
    WHERE d.overs < bffb.first_four_overs_val
    GROUP BY d.batsman
),
BatsmenWithEnoughFours AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_fours) AS total_fours
    FROM df
    GROUP BY batsman
    HAVING SUM(batsman_fours) > 2
)
SELECT
    bbf.batsman,
    bbf.balls_to_first_four
FROM BallsFacedBeforeFirstFour AS bbf
JOIN BatsmenWithEnoughFours AS bwef
    ON bbf.batsman = bwef.batsman
ORDER BY bbf.balls_to_first_four ASC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen during different phases of the innings (e.g., first 6, overs 7-15, last 5).
structure: Use a CASE expression to define phases based on CEIL(overs), group by batsman and phase, calculate strike rate for each phase, and order by batsman and phase.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN ceil(overs) BETWEEN 7 AND 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
    THEN CAST(sum(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM over_phases
WHERE phase != 'Other'
GROUP BY batsman, phase
HAVING sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY batsman, CASE phase WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle Overs' THEN 2 WHEN 'Death Overs' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by calculating the count of consecutive scoring shots (runs > 0) after a dot ball.
structure: Use CTEs to flag dot balls and then use a window function to identify consecutive scoring shots after a dot ball. Group by batsman and count these instances, ordering by count descending.
sql:
WITH ball_types AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_scoring
  FROM df
),
consecutive_scoring AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    is_dot,
    LAG(is_dot, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_is_dot,
    is_scoring
  FROM ball_types
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS consecutive_scoring_after_dot
FROM consecutive_scoring
WHERE prev_is_dot = 1 AND is_scoring = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING count(*) > 0
ORDER BY consecutive_scoring_after_dot DESC;

SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(bowler_bowls_done) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_runs_given) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2) AS REAL) / SUM(bowler_bowls_done) FILTER (WHERE CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2)
    ELSE NULL

FROM df
GROUP BY bowler

ORDER BY economy_rate_death_overs ASC;

intent: Determine the average runs conceded per over by bowlers in the first 6 overs.
structure: Calculate average runs per over using AVG(SUM(team_runs)) grouped by bowler, considering only the first 6 overs. Uses CEIL(overs) for over number.
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  AVG(runs_conceded_in_match_over * 1.0) AS avg_runs_conceded_per_over_first_6
FROM (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    match_over_number,
    runs_conceded_in_match_over,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY match_over_number) AS bowler_spell_over_rank
  FROM (
    SELECT
      bowler,
      CEIL(overs) AS match_over_number,
      SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_conceded_in_match_over
    FROM df
    GROUP BY bowler, CEIL(overs)
  ) AS bowler_overs
) AS ranked_bowler_overs
WHERE
  bowler_spell_over_rank <= 6
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  COUNT(bowler_spell_over_rank) >= 1
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_conceded_per_over_first_6 DESC;

intent: Investigate the correlation between dot balls faced by a batsman and subsequent boundary hitting.
structure: Use a CTE to get the runs on the previous ball. Calculate the percentage of boundaries hit on balls following a dot ball, grouped by batsman. Uses LAG window function, CASE for conditions, and CEIL(overs) is NOT used for grouping.
sql:
WITH prev_ball_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_delivery_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN prev_delivery_runs = 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN prev_delivery_runs = 0 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN prev_delivery_runs = 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_percentage_after_dot
FROM prev_ball_runs
WHERE prev_delivery_runs = 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING sum(CASE WHEN prev_delivery_runs = 0 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY boundary_percentage_after_dot DESC;

intent: Analyze the bowler's economy rate in the death overs compared to the entire match.
structure: Calculate economy rate (total runs conceded / total balls bowled) for death overs (last 5 overs) and overall. Group by bowler. Uses CASE for phase and CEIL(overs).
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'All Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_runs_given ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 6 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN bowler_bowls_done ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS economy_rate_death_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN sum(bowler_bowls_done) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(bowler_runs_given) AS REAL) * 6 / sum(bowler_bowls_done)
    ELSE 0
  END AS economy_rate_overall
FROM over_phases
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING sum(bowler_bowls_done) > 0
ORDER BY economy_rate_death_overs ASC;

intent: Analyze the impact of dot balls on batsman strike rate in different phases of the innings.
structure: Use CASE expressions to define innings phases (early, middle, death). Calculate dot balls and total balls faced per batsman within each phase. Compute strike rate for each phase using these aggregated counts.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Death'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dot_balls,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM phase_data
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate
FROM phase_data
WHERE phase IN ('Early', 'Middle', 'Death')
GROUP BY
  batsman,
  phase
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Death' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END;

intent: Compare the boundary-hitting frequency of batsmen in the initial phase versus the death overs.
structure: Use CASE expressions to create two phases: 'Initial' (first 10 overs) and 'Death' (last 5 overs). Group by batsman and phase. Calculate boundary frequency (fours + sixes) per ball faced for each phase. Employ wide output format for comparison.
sql:
WITH max_over_num AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_total_overs
    FROM df
)
SELECT
    t.batsman,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_fours + t.batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / 
    NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS boundary_frequency_initial,
    CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > (m.max_total_overs - 5) THEN t.batsman_fours + t.batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / 
    NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > (m.max_total_overs - 5) THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS boundary_frequency_death
FROM df AS t, max_over_num AS m
GROUP BY
    t.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) <= 10 THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(t.overs) > (m.max_total_overs - 5) THEN t.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0;

intent: Analyze the conversion rate of dot balls into wickets by bowlers.
structure: Use CASE to identify dot balls and wicket-taking balls. Group by bowler. Calculate the ratio of wicket balls to dot balls faced by batsmen (bowler's perspective).
sql:
SELECT
  bowler,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(bowler_wickets) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS wicket_conversion_rate_from_dots
FROM df
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 -- Ensure the bowler has bowled at least one dot ball
ORDER BY
  wicket_conversion_rate_from_dots DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen during powerplay overs versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use CASE to define 'Powerplay' (first 6 overs) and 'Rest' phases. Group by batsman and phase. Calculate strike rate for each phase. Use wide output for comparison.
sql:
WITH batsman_phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS powerplay_balls,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS rest_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS rest_balls
  FROM
    df
  GROUP BY
    batsman
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  (powerplay_runs * 100.0) / NULLIF(powerplay_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  (rest_runs * 100.0) / NULLIF(rest_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_rest
FROM
  batsman_phase_stats
WHERE
  powerplay_balls > 0 AND rest_balls > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_powerplay DESC;

structure: Use CASE to create bins for over ranges (e.g., 1-5, 6-10, etc.). Group by batsman and the created over range bins. Sum fours and sixes for each bin.

intent: Identify batsmen who tend to hit boundaries (4s and 6s) immediately after facing a dot ball.
structure: Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) to identify dot balls and the subsequent ball. Use a window function to check if the previous ball was a dot ball. Filter for instances where a dot ball is followed by a boundary. Count these occurrences for each batsman. Use a minimum count threshold.
sql:
WITH LaggedData AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        LAG(batsman_runs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_ball_batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    COUNT(*) AS boundaries_after_dot
FROM
    LaggedData
WHERE
    prev_ball_batsman_runs = 0
    AND (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0)
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    COUNT(*) > 3
ORDER BY
    boundaries_after_dot DESC;

intent: Find the average runs scored by batsmen on balls immediately following a six.
structure: Identify deliveries where a six was hit. Use a window function to get the runs scored on the next ball for each batsman. Calculate the average of these subsequent runs. Group by batsman. Filter for batsmen who have hit a minimum number of sixes.
sql:
WITH SixHitterStats AS (
    -- Identify batsmen who have hit at least 3 sixes in total
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_sixes) AS total_sixes
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        batsman
    HAVING
        SUM(batsman_sixes) >= 3
)
SELECT
    t1.batsman,
    AVG(t1.next_ball_runs) AS avg_runs_after_six
FROM (
    -- Get runs and batsman for the current ball, and the immediately succeeding ball
    SELECT
        df.batsman,
        df.batsman_sixes,
        LEAD(df.batsman_runs, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY df.batsman ORDER BY df.overs) AS next_ball_runs,
        LEAD(df.batsman, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY df.batsman ORDER BY df.overs) AS next_batsman
    FROM
        df
) AS t1
JOIN
    SixHitterStats AS t2
ON
    t1.batsman = t2.batsman -- Filter for batsmen who have hit at least 3 sixes
WHERE
    t1.batsman_sixes = 1 -- Current delivery was a six
    AND t1.batsman = t1.next_batsman -- The same batsman faced the next ball (i.e., 'they' scored)
    AND t1.next_ball_runs IS NOT NULL -- Ensure there was a subsequent ball
GROUP BY
    t1.batsman
ORDER BY
    t1.batsman;

sql:
WITH final_over AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS last_over
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  df.batsman, 
  CASE WHEN SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(df.batsman_runs) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_final_over
FROM df 
JOIN final_over ON CEIL(df.overs) = final_over.last_over
GROUP BY df.batsman
HAVING SUM(df.batsman_bowls_faced) >= 1
ORDER BY strike_rate_final_over DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen in the first half of the innings versus the second half.
structure: Use a CASE statement to divide the innings into two halves based on the over number. Calculate the strike rate for each batsman within these two halves using conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH InningsInfo AS (
    SELECT CEIL(MAX(CEIL(overs)) / 2.0) AS middle_over_threshold
    FROM df
),
BallHalves AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(overs) <= (SELECT middle_over_threshold FROM InningsInfo) THEN 'First Half'
            ELSE 'Second Half'
        END AS half
    FROM df
),
BatsmanHalfStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        half,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM BallHalves
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        half
),
BatsmenInBothHalves AS (
    SELECT
        batsman
    FROM BatsmanHalfStats
    WHERE total_balls_faced > 0
    GROUP BY
        batsman
    HAVING
        COUNT(DISTINCT half) = 2
)
SELECT
    bhs.batsman,
    bhs.half,
    CAST(bhs.total_runs AS REAL) * 100.0 / bhs.total_balls_faced AS strike_rate
FROM BatsmanHalfStats AS bhs
INNER JOIN BatsmenInBothHalves AS bibh
    ON bhs.batsman = bibh.batsman
WHERE bhs.total_balls_faced > 0
ORDER BY
    bhs.batsman,
    CASE WHEN bhs.half = 'First Half' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen against a specific bowler across different phases of the innings (powerplay, middle, death).
structure: Use a CTE to define innings phases based on overs. Filter for a specific bowler and then group by batsman and phase to calculate strike rates.
sql:
with over_phases as (
  select 
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    bowler,
    case 
      when ceil(overs) <= 6 then 'Powerplay'
      when ceil(overs) <= 15 then 'Middle'
      else 'Death'
    end as phase 
  from df
)
select 
  batsman,
  case 
    when sum(case when phase = 'Death' then batsman_bowls_faced else 0 end) > 0 
    then cast(sum(case when phase = 'Death' then batsman_runs else 0 end) as real) * 100.0 / sum(case when phase = 'Death' then batsman_bowls_faced else 0 end)
    else 0 
  end as strike_rate_death_overs,
  case 
    when sum(case when phase = 'Powerplay' then batsman_bowls_faced else 0 end) > 0 
    then cast(sum(case when phase = 'Powerplay' then batsman_runs else 0 end) as real) * 100.0 / sum(case when phase = 'Powerplay' then batsman_bowls_faced else 0 end)
    else 0 
  end as strike_rate_powerplay 
from over_phases 
where bowler = 'Azmatullah' 
group by batsman 
having sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 
order by strike_rate_death_overs desc;

intent: Analyze the momentum of batsmen by calculating their strike rate in different phases of their innings, specifically comparing the initial phase (first 5 overs) with the middle phase (overs 6-15) and the death phase (last 5 overs).
structure: Group by batsman. Use CASE expression to define three phases based on CEIL(overs). Calculate strike rate (runs/balls faced) for each phase using conditional aggregation. Use SUM for runs and balls, and then compute the ratio.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Initial'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 5 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Death'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0 
  END AS strike_rate_initial,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0

    ELSE 0

  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0

    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_innings_over FROM df

        WHEN CEIL(t1.overs) > (SELECT max_innings_over FROM max_over_cte) - 10 THEN t1.batsman_runs
        ELSE 0
    END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE
        WHEN CEIL(t1.overs) > (SELECT max_innings_over FROM max_over_cte) - 10 THEN t1.batsman_bowls_faced
        ELSE 0
    END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
    SUM(t1.batsman_runs) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(t1.batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate_overall
FROM
    df AS t1
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE
        WHEN CEIL(t1.overs) > (SELECT max_innings_over FROM max_over_cte) - 10 THEN t1.batsman_bowls_faced
        ELSE 0
    END) > 0
    OR SUM(t1.batsman_bowls_faced) > 0

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall strike rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death overs strike rate for each batsman using CTEs for clarity. Use CASE statements to define death overs. Aggregations: SUM(batsman_runs), SUM(batsman_bowls_faced). Grouping: batsman.
sql:
WITH over_phases AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Other Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM over_phases
  GROUP BY
    batsman
),
death_overs_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_balls
  FROM over_phases
  WHERE
    phase = 'Death Overs'
  GROUP BY
    batsman
)
SELECT
  sr.batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN sr.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(sr.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / sr.total_balls
    ELSE 0
  END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN dosr.death_balls > 0 THEN CAST(dosr.death_runs AS REAL) * 100 / dosr.death_balls
    ELSE 0
  END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM strike_rates AS sr
LEFT JOIN death_overs_strike_rates AS dosr ON sr.batsman = dosr.batsman
WHERE sr.total_balls > 0
ORDER BY
  death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the sequence of dot balls faced by batsmen to understand their ability to break pressure.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Then, use window functions to count consecutive dot balls. Grouping: batsman. Aggregation: COUNT(*). Window Function: LAG.
sql:
WITH RankedDeliveries AS (
    -- Assign a row number to each delivery for a batsman, ordered by overs.
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS rn,
        CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot_ball
    FROM
        df
),
GroupConsecutiveDots AS (
    -- Identify groups of consecutive dot balls using the "gaps and islands" technique.
    -- The group_id is consistent for consecutive rows where is_dot_ball is the same.
    SELECT
        batsman,
        is_dot_ball,
        rn - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, is_dot_ball ORDER BY overs) AS group_id
    FROM
        RankedDeliveries
),
CountDotStreaks AS (
    -- Count the number of deliveries in each consecutive dot ball group.
    SELECT
        batsman,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_dots_count
    FROM
        GroupConsecutiveDots
    WHERE
        is_dot_ball = 1 -- Only consider dot balls
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        group_id
)
-- Finally, find the maximum consecutive dot balls for each batsman.
SELECT
    batsman,
    MAX(consecutive_dots_count) AS max_consecutive_dots_faced
FROM
    CountDotStreaks
GROUP BY
    batsman;

intent: Compare the boundary percentage (fours and sixes) of batsmen across different phases of an innings.
structure: Use a CASE statement to define three phases of the innings (e.g., Powerplay, Middle Overs, Death Overs). Calculate the total boundaries and total balls faced for each batsman in each phase. Then, compute the boundary percentage. Grouping: batsman, phase. Aggregation: SUM(batsman_fours), SUM(batsman_sixes), SUM(batsman_bowls_faced).
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs'
      ELSE 'Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
),
phase_boundary_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    phase,
    SUM(batsman_fours) AS total_fours,
    SUM(batsman_sixes) AS total_sixes,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
  FROM phase_data
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    phase
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  CASE
    WHEN total_balls_faced > 0 THEN CAST(total_fours + total_sixes AS REAL) * 100 / total_balls_faced
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_percentage
FROM phase_boundary_stats
WHERE total_balls_faced > 0
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  CASE phase WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle Overs' THEN 2 WHEN 'Death Overs' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END;

structure: Calculate runs scored in each over for each batsman. Use a window function to compute a running total of runs. Grouping: batsman, CEIL(overs). Aggregation: SUM(batsman_runs). Window Function: SUM() OVER().
sql:
WITH runs_per_over AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    batsman,
    over_number
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  over_number,
  runs_in_over,
  SUM(runs_in_over) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY over_number ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_runs
FROM runs_per_over
ORDER BY
  batsman,

intent: Assess the scoring rate of batsmen in the initial phase of the innings (first 10 overs) compared to the middle phase (overs 11-15).
structure: Use a CTE to define phases based on CEIL(overs). Then, calculate the strike rate (SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced)) for each batsman within these two phases. Finally, compare the strike rates across phases.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Initial'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > 10 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
      ELSE 'Late'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_initial,
  CASE WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_middle
FROM phase_stats
WHERE phase IN ('Initial', 'Middle')
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 10 -- Ensure batsman has faced a reasonable number of balls in these phases
ORDER BY strike_rate_middle DESC;

intent: Determine the number of instances where a batsman faced three consecutive dot balls.
structure: Use a CTE to identify dot balls. Then, use window functions (LAG) within another CTE to check for previous two deliveries being dots for each batsman. Finally, count the occurrences of three consecutive dot balls.
sql:
WITH dot_ball_sequences AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 2, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_prev_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND prev_runs = 0 AND prev_prev_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS instances_after_2_dots
FROM dot_ball_sequences
WHERE batsman_runs = 0 AND prev_runs = 0 AND prev_prev_runs = 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 AND prev_runs = 0 AND prev_prev_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) > 1 -- Minimum of 2 occurrences to show significant trend
ORDER BY instances_after_2_dots DESC;

intent: Determine the percentage of dot balls bowled by each bowler in the powerplay versus the middle overs.
structure: Define 'Powerplay' (first 6 overs) and 'Middle Overs' (overs 7-15) using CASE and CEIL(overs). Group by bowler and phase. Calculate the percentage of dot balls (batsman_runs = 0) within each phase. Use COUNT(*) for total balls and SUM(is_dot) for dot balls.
sql:
WITH phase_balls AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_dot,
    CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay' WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 AND ceil(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle Overs' ELSE NULL END AS phase
  FROM df
  WHERE ceil(overs) <= 6 OR (ceil(overs) > 6 AND ceil(overs) <= 15)
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  phase,
  CAST(SUM(is_dot) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) AS dot_ball_percentage
FROM phase_balls
WHERE phase IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY bowler, phase
ORDER BY bowler, CASE phase WHEN 'Powerplay' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle Overs' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls faced by a batsman after they have hit a boundary (four or six).
structure: Identify balls where a batsman hit a boundary. Use a window function to find the number of balls faced by that batsman between consecutive boundaries. Calculate the average of these counts.
sql:
WITH BallSequence AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_bowls_faced,
        CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS ball_seq_num
    FROM df
),
BoundaryGroupStartEnd AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        ball_seq_num AS current_boundary_ball_seq_num,
        LAG(ball_seq_num, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_boundary_ball_seq_num,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS boundary_occurrence_num
    FROM BallSequence
    WHERE is_boundary = 1
),
GroupedIntervals AS (
    SELECT
        bs.batsman,
        bgs.boundary_occurrence_num,
        SUM(bs.batsman_bowls_faced) AS balls_between_boundaries_count
    FROM BallSequence bs
    JOIN BoundaryGroupStartEnd bgs
        ON bs.batsman = bgs.batsman
        AND bs.ball_seq_num > bgs.prev_boundary_ball_seq_num
        AND bs.ball_seq_num < bgs.current_boundary_ball_seq_num
    WHERE bgs.prev_boundary_ball_seq_num > 0 -- Exclude the first boundary as it has no preceding interval
    GROUP BY
        bs.batsman,
        bgs.boundary_occurrence_num
),
BatsmanBoundaryCounts AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        MAX(boundary_occurrence_num) AS total_boundaries_hit
    FROM BoundaryGroupStartEnd
    GROUP BY batsman
    HAVING MAX(boundary_occurrence_num) >= 3
)
SELECT
    gi.batsman,
    AVG(CAST(gi.balls_between_boundaries_count AS REAL)) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM GroupedIntervals gi
JOIN BatsmanBoundaryCounts bbc ON gi.batsman = bbc.batsman
GROUP BY gi.batsman
ORDER BY avg_balls_between_boundaries ASC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CTE to filter for death overs. Calculate strike rate (runs/balls) for each batsman in death overs and overall. Group by batsman. Use CASE statements for conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH max_over AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_innings_over
  FROM df
),
DeathOversStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_balls
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max_innings_over FROM max_over) - 2
    GROUP BY
        batsman
),
OverallStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS overall_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS overall_balls
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    DOS.batsman,
    DOS.death_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(DOS.death_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs,
    OS.overall_runs * 100.0 / NULLIF(OS.overall_balls, 0) AS strike_rate_overall
FROM
    DeathOversStats DOS
JOIN
    OverallStats OS ON DOS.batsman = OS.batsman
WHERE
    DOS.death_balls > 0
ORDER BY
    strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Identify batsmen with the highest frequency of playing dot balls immediately after hitting a boundary (4 or 6).
structure: Use a CTE with a window function to identify the previous ball's outcome. Filter for deliveries that followed a boundary and were dot balls. Count these instances per batsman and order by frequency.
sql:
WITH prev_ball_outcome AS (
  SELECT 
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    LAG(batsman_fours + batsman_sixes, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as prev_balls_were_boundary
  FROM df
)
SELECT 
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) as dot_balls_after_boundary
FROM prev_ball_outcome
WHERE prev_balls_were_boundary > 0 AND batsman_runs = 0
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY dot_balls_after_boundary DESC;

intent: Calculate the strike rate of batsmen during the powerplay overs (first 6 overs) compared to the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to categorize deliveries into 'Powerplay' and 'Non-Powerplay' overs based on `ceil(overs)`. Calculate the strike rate for each batsman within these two categories using conditional aggregation. Group by batsman.
sql:
SELECT 
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0 
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0 
  END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM df
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) <= 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN ceil(overs) > 6 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_powerplay DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 2 overs) compared to their overall scoring rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and death overs strike rate for each batsman using CTEs for phase definition and aggregation. Compare these two metrics.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 2 THEN 'Death Overs' ELSE 'Normal' END AS phase
  FROM df
),
strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls
  FROM phase_data
  GROUP BY batsman
),
death_overs_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    SUM(batsman_runs) AS death_runs,
    SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_balls
  FROM phase_data
  WHERE phase = 'Death Overs'
  GROUP BY batsman
)
SELECT
  sr.batsman,
  CASE WHEN sr.total_balls > 0 THEN CAST(sr.total_runs AS REAL) * 100 / sr.total_balls ELSE 0 END AS overall_strike_rate,
  CASE WHEN dosr.death_balls > 0 THEN CAST(dosr.death_runs AS REAL) * 100 / dosr.death_balls ELSE 0 END AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM strike_rates AS sr
LEFT JOIN death_overs_strike_rates AS dosr ON sr.batsman = dosr.batsman
WHERE sr.total_balls > 0
ORDER BY death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Analyze the strike rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) versus the initial phase (first 10 overs).
structure: Use CTEs to define phases based on CEIL(overs), then group by batsman and phase, calculate total runs and balls faced for each phase, and finally compute strike rates, using CASE expressions for phases and conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH MatchMaxOver AS (
    SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over FROM df
)
SELECT
    d.batsman,
    (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 10 THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) /
     NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 10 THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0)) * 100 AS initial_phase_strike_rate,
    (CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_over - 5) THEN d.batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) /
     NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_over - 5) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0)) * 100 AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM
    df AS d, MatchMaxOver AS m
GROUP BY
    d.batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 10 THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_over - 5) THEN d.batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
    death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS runs_in_over
  FROM df
  GROUP BY
    bowler,
    over_number
)

  bowler,
  AVG(runs_in_over) AS average_runs_per_over
FROM over_runs
GROUP BY
  bowler

intent: Track the momentum of batsmen by analyzing their runs scored in consecutive balls.
structure: Use window functions (LAG) to access runs from previous deliveries, identify sequences of scoring (non-zero runs), and count these sequences.
sql:
WITH runs_sequences AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 2, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_prev_runs
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS instances_of_scoring_after_scoring
FROM runs_sequences
WHERE batsman_runs > 0 AND prev_runs > 0 AND prev_prev_runs > 0
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 5
ORDER BY
  instances_of_scoring_after_scoring DESC;

intent: Identify bowlers who are particularly effective at restricting scoring in the death overs (last 5 overs of the innings). This analysis focuses on their economy rate in high-pressure situations.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define the 'death overs' phase. Group by bowler and the death overs phase. Calculate the economy rate (total runs given / total balls bowled) for each bowler in this phase. Use SUM aggregations.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    bowler_runs_given,
    bowler_bowls_done,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Non-Death Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CAST(SUM(bowler_runs_given) AS REAL) / COUNT(bowler_bowls_done) AS economy_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_data
WHERE
  phase = 'Death Overs'
GROUP BY
  bowler
HAVING
  COUNT(bowler_bowls_done) > 0
ORDER BY
  economy_rate_death_overs ASC;

intent: Analyze the transition in batsman's strike rate from the initial phase of the innings (first 6 overs) to the middle phase (overs 7-15).
structure: Calculate strike rate for two distinct phases using CASE expression for phase definition, grouping by batsman, and using sum of runs and sum of balls faced for strike rate calculation.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Initial'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN 'Middle'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_initial,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_middle
FROM phase_stats
WHERE phase IN ('Initial', 'Middle')
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Middle' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_middle DESC;

intent: Identify batsmen who consistently hit boundaries (fours or sixes) after facing at least 10 balls in total, and calculate their boundary frequency.

sql:

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in the initial overs (first 10) versus the rest of the innings.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: 'Initial Overs' and 'Rest of Innings'. Calculate strike rate for each phase using aggregation. Use CTEs.
sql:
WITH PhaseStrikeRate AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Initial Overs' ELSE 'Rest of Innings' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE NULL END AS strike_rate_initial_overs,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE NULL END AS strike_rate_rest_of_innings
FROM PhaseStrikeRate
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Initial Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Rest of Innings' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0

  strike_rate_initial_overs DESC;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate difference between the first 6 overs and the last 6 overs for each batsman.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: 'Powerplay' (first 6 overs) and 'Death Overs' (last 6 overs). Calculate strike rate for each phase. Use CTEs and aggregation. Compare these strike rates.
sql:
WITH PhaseStrikeRates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE 
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT max(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL 
  END AS strike_rate_powerplay,
  CASE 
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE NULL 
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM PhaseStrikeRates
WHERE phase IN ('Powerplay', 'Death Overs')
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 OR SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_powerplay DESC;

intent: Analyze the variation in a batsman's strike rate across different phases of an innings, specifically comparing their strike rate in the first 6 overs versus the death overs (last 6 overs).
structure: This query uses a CTE to categorize deliveries into 'early' (first 6 overs) and 'death' (last 6 overs) phases based on `CEIL(overs)`. It then calculates the strike rate (runs/balls faced) for each batsman within each phase using conditional aggregation and sums across phases to get a wide output.
sql:
WITH phase_data AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'early'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 6 THEN 'death'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE 
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) 
    ELSE 0 
  END AS strike_rate_early_overs,
  CASE 
    WHEN sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 
    THEN CAST(sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'death' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / sum(CASE WHEN phase = 'death' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) 
    ELSE 0 
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_data
WHERE phase IN ('early', 'death')
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING sum(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

structure: Use CASE statement to define 'death overs' phase. Calculate overall strike rate and death overs strike rate using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced). Group by batsman. Use window function for max overs to determine death overs. CTE is used for phase definition.
sql:
WITH phase_stats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,

    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs' ELSE 'Normal Overs' END AS phase

  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS strike_rate_death_overs

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a bowler concedes between boundaries (fours or sixes) across the entire innings.
structure: Use a CTE to identify boundary balls. Use another CTE to calculate balls since the last boundary conceded for each bowler using a window function. Calculate the average of these values.
sql:
WITH boundary_balls_conceded AS (
  SELECT 
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_boundary_ball
  FROM df
),
balls_since_last_boundary AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_boundary_ball = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS balls_since_last
  FROM boundary_balls_conceded
  WHERE is_boundary_ball = 1
)
SELECT 
  bowler,
  AVG(balls_since_last) AS avg_balls_between_boundaries
FROM balls_since_last_boundary
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
ORDER BY avg_balls_between_boundaries DESC;

intent: Determine the boundary percentage for batsmen in the powerplay (first 10 overs) vs. middle overs (overs 11-15).
structure: Use a CASE statement to define 'powerplay' and 'middle overs' phases. Calculate boundary percentage for each phase. Group by batsman. CTE is used for phase definition.
sql:
SELECT
    batsman,
    (CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
          THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
          ELSE 0.0 END) AS boundary_percentage_powerplay,
    (CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
          THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_fours + batsman_sixes ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
          ELSE 0.0 END) AS boundary_percentage_middle
FROM
    df
GROUP BY
    batsman
HAVING
    SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 5
    OR SUM(CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > 10 AND CEIL(overs) <= 15 THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 5
ORDER BY
    batsman;

intent: Track the cumulative runs conceded by each bowler throughout their spell, highlighting over-by-over progression.

WITH OverRuns AS (

intent: Analyze the momentum of scoring by batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs of the innings) by calculating the average runs scored per ball faced in this phase.
structure: Group by batsman, calculate the average of batsman_runs for balls faced within the last 5 overs using a CASE expression for phase definition. Use window functions for calculating the total overs to determine the death overs.
sql:
WITH OverData AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CEIL(overs) AS over_number,
    MAX(CEIL(overs)) OVER () AS max_over_in_innings
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_runs) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS avg_runs_per_ball_in_death_overs
FROM OverData
WHERE
  over_number > (max_over_in_innings - 5)
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  avg_runs_per_ball_in_death_overs DESC;

sql:

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in the first 10 overs versus the rest of the innings, to see how their scoring changes.
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: 'Early' (first 10 overs) and 'Late' (rest of the innings). Group by batsman and phase, then calculate strike rate. Use conditional aggregation.
sql:
WITH PhaseStats AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 10 THEN 'Early' ELSE 'Late' END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_early,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_early,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS runs_late,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) AS balls_late,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_early,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_late
FROM PhaseStats
WHERE phase IN ('Early', 'Late')
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0
ORDER BY
  strike_rate_late DESC;

intent: Analyze the trend of wickets taken by a specific bowler across different phases of the innings (early, middle, late).
structure: Define three phases (early, middle, late) based on CEIL(overs). Group by bowler and phase, then count the wickets (bowler_wickets).
sql:
SELECT

  CASE
    WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Early'

    ELSE 'Late'
  END AS phase,

FROM df
WHERE bowler_wickets > 0
GROUP BY
  bowler,
  phase
ORDER BY
  bowler,
  CASE phase WHEN 'Early' THEN 1 WHEN 'Middle' THEN 2 WHEN 'Late' THEN 3 END;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the death overs (last 5 overs) compared to their overall scoring rate.
structure: Calculate overall strike rate and strike rate in death overs for each batsman using CTEs and CASE expressions for phase definition. Group by batsman. Use aggregations for sums and counts, then compute ratios.
sql:
WITH phase_overs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Normal Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Normal Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Normal Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS normal_overs_strike_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END), 0) AS death_overs_strike_rate
FROM phase_overs
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  death_overs_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Calculate the average number of balls a batsman faces before hitting their first boundary in an innings.
structure: Use a CTE with a window function to find the delivery number of the first boundary (four or six) for each batsman. Then, calculate the average of these delivery numbers, grouped by batsman. Ensure only batsmen who hit at least one boundary are included.
sql:
WITH first_boundary AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) as delivery_no
  FROM df
  WHERE
    batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(delivery_no) AS avg_balls_to_first_boundary
FROM first_boundary
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  COUNT(overs) > 0
ORDER BY
  avg_balls_to_first_boundary ASC;

intent: Identify batsmen who score a significantly higher percentage of their runs through boundaries (fours and sixes) in the death overs.
structure: Use a CTE to define 'Death Overs' (last 5 overs). Calculate the total runs scored and boundary runs scored by each batsman in these overs. Compute the percentage of runs from boundaries. Group by batsman. Use aggregations for sums and counts, then compute ratios.
sql:
WITH death_over_runs AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    CASE WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_death_over
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over = 1 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over = 1 THEN (batsman_fours * 4 + batsman_sixes * 6) ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over = 1 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS boundary_run_percentage_death_overs
FROM death_over_runs
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_death_over = 1 THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundary_run_percentage_death_overs DESC;

structure: Use CTEs to identify bowler wicket balls. Use a window function to check the previous ball's context for the current batsman. Count balls faced by the batsman after a bowler's wicket.
sql:
WITH bowlerwicketlag AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN LAG(bowler_wickets, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) > 0 THEN 1

  FROM df
)

  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced_after_bowler_wicket
FROM bowlerwicketlag
WHERE is_wicket_ball_by_bowler_prev_delivery = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0

intent: Identify batsmen who are slow starters but finish strong. Calculate a batsman's strike rate in the first 5 overs versus their strike rate in the last 5 overs.
structure: Use a CASE expression based on `CEIL(overs)` to classify deliveries into 'Early' (first 5) and 'Late' (last 5) phases. Then, use conditional aggregation to calculate strike rates for each phase.
sql:
WITH phase_strike_rates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE 
      WHEN ceil(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Early'
      WHEN ceil(overs) > (SELECT max(ceil(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Late'
      ELSE 'Middle' 
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_early,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) ELSE 0 END AS strike_rate_late
FROM phase_strike_rates
WHERE phase IN ('Early', 'Late')
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 10 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Late' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 10
ORDER BY strike_rate_late DESC;

intent: Evaluate bowler consistency by analyzing wicket-taking streaks. Find the average length of wicket-taking streaks for each bowler.
structure: Use a CTE to flag balls where wickets were taken. Then use a window function to group consecutive wicket balls into streaks. Finally, calculate the average streak length per bowler.
sql:
WITH wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket
  FROM df
),
streak_starts AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_wicket,
    CASE WHEN is_wicket = 1 AND LAG(is_wicket, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new_streak
  FROM wickets
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_wicket,
    SUM(is_new_streak) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM streak_starts
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CAST(SUM(is_wicket) AS REAL) / COUNT(CASE WHEN streak_group IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS avg_wickets_per_streak
FROM streak_groups
WHERE is_wicket = 1
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN streak_group IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) > 0
ORDER BY avg_wickets_per_streak DESC;

structure: Grouping by batsman, using a CTE to identify dot balls and the ball immediately following them using a window function (LAG), then calculating the average of runs scored on the balls after a dot ball.
sql:
WITH BallData AS (

    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_runs

FROM BallData

intent: Identify batsmen who consistently hit boundaries after facing a certain number of dot balls in sequence.
structure: Using a CTE to track sequences of dot balls for each batsman using window functions (LAG). Then, filtering for boundary hits (4 or 6 runs) that occur after a specified number of consecutive dot balls, and counting these occurrences per batsman.
sql:
WITH DotSequences AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_fours,
    batsman_sixes,
    SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS consecutive_dots_before
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  COUNT(*) AS boundary_hits_after_3_dots
FROM DotSequences
WHERE
  batsman_runs IN (4, 6) AND consecutive_dots_before >= 3
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY
  boundary_hits_after_3_dots DESC;

intent: Find the batsman who scores the most runs immediately after hitting a boundary (four or six).
structure: Using a CTE to identify boundary shots and the subsequent ball's runs using LAG. Then grouping by batsman and counting instances where runs were scored on the ball after a boundary, ordering by runs scored.
sql:
WITH BoundaryFollowup AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    batsman_runs,
    LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS previous_ball_runs,
    CASE WHEN LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) IN (4, 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_after_boundary
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  SUM(batsman_runs) AS runs_after_boundary
FROM BoundaryFollowup
WHERE
  is_after_boundary = 1
GROUP BY
  batsman
ORDER BY
  runs_after_boundary DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rate of batsmen in the initial phase (first 6 overs) versus the middle phase (overs 7-12).
structure: Use a CASE expression to define two phases: 'Initial' (CEIL(overs) <= 6) and 'Middle' (CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 12). Group by batsman and phase, calculating strike rate for each phase. Uses CTEs and CASE expressions.
sql:
WITH BattingPhaseStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        CASE
            WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 6 THEN 'Initial'
            WHEN CEIL(overs) > 6 AND CEIL(overs) <= 12 THEN 'Middle'
            ELSE 'Other'
        END AS phase,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_bowls_faced
    FROM
        df
    WHERE
        CEIL(overs) <= 12 -- Filter raw data early to limit processing to relevant overs
),
AggregatedPhaseStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        phase,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM
        BattingPhaseStats
    WHERE
        phase IN ('Initial', 'Middle') -- Only consider the two phases of interest
    GROUP BY
        batsman,
        phase
    HAVING
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 -- Only include phase stats if batsman faced at least one ball in that phase
),
QualifiedBatsmen AS (
    SELECT
        batsman
    FROM
        AggregatedPhaseStats
    GROUP BY
        batsman
    HAVING
        COUNT(DISTINCT phase) = 2 -- Ensure batsman is present in both 'Initial' and 'Middle' phases (i.e., faced balls in both)
)
SELECT
    aps.batsman,
    aps.phase,
    (aps.total_runs * 100.0) / NULLIF(aps.total_balls_faced, 0) AS strike_rate
FROM
    AggregatedPhaseStats aps
JOIN
    QualifiedBatsmen qb ON aps.batsman = qb.batsman
ORDER BY
    aps.batsman,
    CASE WHEN aps.phase = 'Initial' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END;

intent: Analyze the scoring rate of batsmen in the first 5 overs compared to their scoring rate in the death overs (last 5 overs).
structure: Uses CTEs to define phases (early vs. death overs) based on CEIL(overs). Calculates strike rates (runs per ball) for each phase using SUM(batsman_runs) / SUM(batsman_bowls_faced). Aggregates by batsman. Groups by batsman and phase. Uses CASE statements to define phases. Uses window functions to find max over. Wide output preference used for phases.
sql:
WITH phase_strikerates AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    batsman_runs,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(overs) <= 5 THEN 'Early Overs'
      WHEN CEIL(overs) > (SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) FROM df) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE 'Middle Overs'
    END AS phase
  FROM df
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_early_overs,
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_runs ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END)
    ELSE 0
  END AS strike_rate_death_overs
FROM phase_strikerates
WHERE phase = 'Early Overs' OR phase = 'Death Overs'
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Early Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN batsman_bowls_faced ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY strike_rate_death_overs DESC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a batsman takes to score their first boundary (4 or 6) after a bowler has taken a wicket.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify balls immediately following a bowler's wicket. Then, it calculates the cumulative balls faced by each batsman after such events and finds the average number of balls to the next boundary (4 or 6). It involves a window function to lag bowler wickets and a subsequent aggregation.
sql:
WITH BaseData AS (
  SELECT
    overs,
    batsman,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    (CASE WHEN batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_batsman_boundary,
    (CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_wicket_on_ball
  FROM df
),
ContextualBalls AS (
  SELECT
    overs,
    batsman,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    is_batsman_boundary,
    is_wicket_on_ball,
    -- Identify the 'overs' of the most recent wicket prior to the current ball.
    -- This defines the start of the 'period after a bowler's wicket'.
    MAX(CASE WHEN is_wicket_on_ball = 1 THEN overs ELSE NULL END) OVER (ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS period_start_overs
  FROM BaseData
),
PeriodsAndEvents AS (
  SELECT
    overs,
    batsman,
    batsman_bowls_faced,
    is_batsman_boundary,
    is_wicket_on_ball,
    period_start_overs,
    -- For each batsman within a specific post-wicket period, find the 'overs' of their first boundary.
    MIN(CASE WHEN is_batsman_boundary = 1 THEN overs END)
      OVER (PARTITION BY batsman, period_start_overs ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
      AS batsman_first_boundary_in_period,
    -- For each post-wicket period, find the 'overs' of the next wicket (any player).
    MIN(CASE WHEN is_wicket_on_ball = 1 THEN overs END)
      OVER (PARTITION BY period_start_overs ORDER BY overs ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
      AS next_any_wicket_in_period
  FROM ContextualBalls
  WHERE period_start_overs IS NOT NULL -- Only consider balls that occur after at least one wicket
),
SuccessfulSequences AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    batsman,
    period_start_overs,
    batsman_first_boundary_in_period AS boundary_hit_overs
  FROM PeriodsAndEvents
  WHERE
    overs = batsman_first_boundary_in_period -- Filter for the exact ball on which the first boundary was hit
    AND (batsman_first_boundary_in_period < next_any_wicket_in_period OR next_any_wicket_in_period IS NULL) -- Boundary must occur before the next wicket or if no more wickets
),
BallsFacedInSequences AS (
  SELECT
    ss.batsman,
    ss.period_start_overs,
    SUM(cb.batsman_bowls_faced) AS balls_to_boundary
  FROM SuccessfulSequences ss
  JOIN ContextualBalls cb
    ON cb.batsman = ss.batsman
    AND cb.overs > ss.period_start_overs -- Balls strictly after the wicket
    AND cb.overs <= ss.boundary_hit_overs -- Up to and including the boundary ball
  GROUP BY
    ss.batsman,
    ss.period_start_overs
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(balls_to_boundary) AS avg_balls_to_next_boundary_after_bowler_wicket
FROM BallsFacedInSequences
GROUP BY
  batsman
HAVING
  COUNT(period_start_overs) >= 1 -- Ensure batsman had at least one successful sequence (one boundary after a wicket)
ORDER BY
  avg_balls_to_next_boundary_after_bowler_wicket ASC;

intent: Calculate the conversion rate of batsmen from facing a dot ball to hitting a boundary (4 or 6) on the very next legal delivery.
structure: Uses CTEs to identify consecutive deliveries. The first CTE identifies dot balls, and the second identifies boundaries. A JOIN then links these consecutive deliveries to find instances where a dot ball is immediately followed by a boundary hit by the same batsman. Aggregates by batsman.
sql:
WITH BatsmanDeliveries AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        overs,
        batsman_runs,
        batsman_fours,
        batsman_sixes,
        LAG(batsman_runs, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY batsman ORDER BY overs) AS prev_batsman_runs
    FROM
        df
),
BatsmanStats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_dot_balls_faced,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN prev_batsman_runs = 0 AND (batsman_fours > 0 OR batsman_sixes > 0) THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END) AS boundaries_after_dot
    FROM
        BatsmanDeliveries
    GROUP BY
        batsman
)
SELECT
    batsman,
    (CAST(boundaries_after_dot AS REAL) * 100.0) / total_dot_balls_faced AS boundary_conversion_rate_after_dot
FROM
    BatsmanStats
WHERE
    total_dot_balls_faced >= 1
    AND boundaries_after_dot >= 1
ORDER BY
    boundary_conversion_rate_after_dot DESC;

sql:
WITH max_over_info AS (
    SELECT CEIL(MAX(overs)) AS max_full_over FROM df
),
overall_stats AS (
    SELECT
        batsman,
        SUM(batsman_runs) AS total_runs,
        SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM
        df
    GROUP BY
        batsman
),
decathlon_over_stats AS (
    SELECT
        d.batsman,
        SUM(d.batsman_runs) AS death_over_runs,
        SUM(d.batsman_bowls_faced) AS death_over_balls_faced
    FROM
        df AS d
    JOIN
        max_over_info AS m ON 1=1
    WHERE
        CEIL(d.overs) > (m.max_full_over - 5)
    GROUP BY
        d.batsman
)
SELECT
    o.batsman,
    CASE
        WHEN o.total_balls_faced > 0 THEN (o.total_runs * 100.0 / o.total_balls_faced)
        ELSE NULL
    END AS overall_strike_rate,
    CASE
        WHEN d.death_over_balls_faced > 0 THEN (d.death_over_runs * 100.0 / d.death_over_balls_faced)
        ELSE NULL
    END AS death_over_strike_rate
FROM
    overall_stats AS o
LEFT JOIN
    decathlon_over_stats AS d ON o.batsman = d.batsman
ORDER BY
    death_over_strike_rate DESC;

intent: Determine the average number of balls a bowler bowls between taking wickets.
structure: Use CTEs to identify wicket-taking balls and then calculate the time difference between consecutive wickets for each bowler. Window functions are used to lag and group wickets.
sql:
WITH wickets AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN bowler_wickets > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_wicket
  FROM df
),
streak_starts AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_wicket,
    CASE WHEN is_wicket = 1 AND LAG(is_wicket, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new_streak
  FROM wickets
),
streak_groups AS (
  SELECT
    bowler,
    overs,
    is_wicket,
    SUM(is_new_streak) OVER (PARTITION BY bowler ORDER BY overs) AS streak_group
  FROM streak_starts
)
SELECT
  bowler,
  CAST(SUM(is_wicket) AS REAL) / COUNT(CASE WHEN streak_group IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS avg_balls_between_wickets
FROM streak_groups
WHERE is_wicket = 1
GROUP BY bowler
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN streak_group IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) > 0
ORDER BY avg_balls_between_wickets DESC;

intent: Analyze the momentum shift by calculating the average runs scored on balls immediately following a six.
structure: Use a CTE to identify balls on which a six was hit and the subsequent ball's runs. Then, group by batsman and calculate the average runs scored on the ball after a six.
sql:
WITH six_balls AS (
  SELECT
    batsman,
    overs,
    CASE WHEN batsman_runs = 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_six
  FROM df
),
balls_after_six AS (
  SELECT
    sb.batsman,
    sb.overs,
    df.batsman_runs,
    LAG(sb.is_six, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY sb.batsman ORDER BY sb.overs) AS prev_ball_was_six
  FROM six_balls AS sb
  JOIN df ON sb.batsman = df.batsman AND sb.overs = df.overs
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  AVG(batsman_runs) AS avg_runs_after_six
FROM balls_after_six
WHERE prev_ball_was_six = 1
GROUP BY batsman
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY avg_runs_after_six DESC;

intent: Compare the strike rates of batsmen in different phases of the innings (e.g., powerplay, middle overs, death overs) to understand their scoring patterns throughout an innings.
structure: Use a CTE to categorize deliveries into different phases (e.g., first 6 overs, overs 7-15, last 5 overs). Then, calculate the strike rate (runs per 100 balls) for each batsman within each phase. Group by batsman and phase. Use CASE statement for phase definition.
sql:
WITH MaxOver AS (
  SELECT MAX(CEIL(overs)) AS max_over_num FROM df
),
PhaseAssignments AS (
  SELECT
    d.batsman,
    d.batsman_runs,
    d.batsman_bowls_faced,
    CASE
      WHEN CEIL(d.overs) <= 6 THEN 'Powerplay'
      WHEN CEIL(d.overs) > (SELECT max_over_num FROM MaxOver) - 5 THEN 'Death Overs'
      ELSE NULL -- Balls outside Powerplay and Death Overs will be filtered out
    END AS phase
  FROM df AS d
)
SELECT
  batsman,
  phase,
  SUM(batsman_runs) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(batsman_bowls_faced), 0) AS strike_rate
FROM PhaseAssignments
WHERE
  phase IS NOT NULL -- Filter to include only Powerplay and Death Overs
GROUP BY
  batsman,
  phase
HAVING
  SUM(batsman_bowls_faced) > 0 -- Only include batsmen who faced at least one ball in the phase
ORDER BY
  batsman,
  CASE
    WHEN phase = 'Powerplay' THEN 1
    WHEN phase = 'Death Overs' THEN 2
  END;
